astm-a193.sum: Material specification for alloy steel and stainless steel bolting used in high-temperature, high-pressure, or special service on pressure vessels, valves, flanges, and fittings. It has ferritic and austenitic grades such as B5, B7, and B8; nuts are covered in Section 13.
facts: The scope is bolting materials and bolting components for high-temperature, high-pressure, or special service. Nuts are covered in Section 13 (A194 is among the referenced standards); it points to A320 for low-temperature service and A354 for the lower end of the high-temperature range.
Grades: ferritic (B5, B7, B7M, etc.) and austenitic (B8, B8M, etc.). Austenitic grades are divided into solution-treated products and products strain-hardened after solution treatment.
B7M is a hardness-limited grade for bolting exposed to sour (H2S) service; NACE MR0175/ISO 15156 lists B7M as an allowed bolting material.

Common requirements such as melting, chemical composition, and mechanical testing follow A962; if the two differ, A193 takes precedence. Supplementary requirements (S) apply only when written in the order.
watch: If the BOM gives only a bolt grade such as "A193 B7", check the nut (A194 grade) separately.
B7 and B7M are not substitutes for each other. The bolting material that ISO 15156 lists for sour exposure is B7M (hardness controlled to 22 HRC or less).

Even a stud made from JIS- or EN-equivalent steel must meet all the chemical and test criteria of A193 B7 to qualify for a B7 certificate. Do not treat them as the same based only on a material correspondence table.
For flange studs over 1", 8UN (8 threads per inch) is the usual practice. Even at the same diameter, UNC and a different thread count do not fit, so state the threads per inch as well.
eq_notes: ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code Section II Part A adopted edition (may differ from the current ASTM edition depending on the adopted edition)

astm-a194.sum: Specification for carbon steel, alloy steel, and stainless steel nuts for high-temperature, high-pressure bolting. It sets the chemical composition and the hardness, proof load, and cone proof load tests, and nuts are specified separately, matched to the bolt.
facts: Size range: carbon steel, alloy steel, and martensitic stainless steel nuts are 1/4" to 4" (M12 to M100); austenitic nuts are 1/4" (M12) and larger.

It covers carbon steel, alloy steel, and martensitic stainless steel nuts, and austenitic stainless steel nuts. Among these, 2H nuts can be used instead of A563 DH in structural bolt sets (RCSC 2025).
The standard prohibits supplying a different grade in place of the specified one without the buyer's permission.
watch: When buying nuts alone, state the grade, thread series (flange nuts over 1" are usually 8UN), and whether heavy or not.
For sour-service bolting, check that the nut is also of a grade that meets the hardness limit in the specification (for example, 22 HRC or less).
Hot-dip galvanized nuts are overtapped after plating, so match them as a set with the galvanized stud.
eq_notes: ASME Section II Part A adopted edition

astm-a320.sum: Bolting specification for low-temperature pressure equipment. It covers ferritic grades such as L7, L7M, and L43 and austenitic grades such as B8, and low-temperature toughness is confirmed by Charpy impact values.
facts: Scope: bolting materials and components for pressure vessels, valves, flanges, and fittings in low-temperature service. Nuts are covered in Section 10, and nut material must also be impact tested.
There are ferritic (L7, L7M, L43, etc.) and austenitic (B8, etc.) grades; austenitic grades come as solution-treated and strain-hardened products.
Impact criteria are in Table 2. The standard notes that meeting the -101 °C (-150 °F) criterion for L43 may require AISI 4340 steel with reduced P and S.
L7M is a low-temperature grade and a hardness-limited grade that ISO 15156 lists as bolting material for sour (H2S) service.
watch: Nuts must also meet the same impact requirements. Check any BOM that pairs an L7 stud with a general 2H nut.
Check that the impact test temperature on the certificate is at or below the minimum design metal temperature (MDMT).
eq_notes: ASME Section II Part A adopted edition

astm-a453.sum: High-temperature bolting specification for materials whose thermal expansion coefficient is similar to that of austenitic stainless steel. It has 5 grades and 12 classes (yield 345 to 825 MPa), and because special processing is required it is not for general use.
facts: Grades: 5 grades including 651, 660, 662, and 665, with 12 classes; yield ranges from about 345 to 825 MPa (50 to 120 ksi). Grade 660 has Class A, B, C, and D; 651, 662, and 665 have Class A and B.
It covers bolts, screws, studs, nuts, washers, and their bar stock for high-temperature use on pressure vessels, valve flanges, and similar.
General requirements follow A962; supplementary requirements apply only when written one by one in the purchase order.
watch: State the A453 grade (for example, 660) and the Class (A, B, C, D) in the order and on the certificate.
The reason for selecting it is thermal expansion similar to austenitic flanges. A453 also covers nuts, so specify the nut material together.
eq_notes: ASME Section II Part A adopted edition

astm-a962.sum: General requirements specification that pressure bolting standards such as A193, A194, A320, and A453 commonly cite. It collects common rules such as melting, chemical composition, mechanical testing, and marking; if it differs from the individual standard, the individual standard takes precedence.
facts: Product standards that cite the common requirements: A193/A193M, A194/A194M, A320/A320M, A437/A437M, A453/A453M, A540/A540M, A1014/A1014M, A1082/A1082M, and others.
Topics covered: melting process, quality control, chemical composition (product analysis), mechanical testing (proof load, cone proof load, impact, hardness), decarburization depth, and so on.
If the requirements differ from those of the individual product standard, the product standard takes precedence.
It is not an ordering standard on its own. In the order, write the product standard and grade, such as "A193 B7".
watch: Even when A962 is also listed on the certificate, grade acceptance is judged by the values of the product standard such as A193 or A194.
If the BOM has only A962 and no product standard, the material grade cannot be identified, so check.
eq_notes: ASME Section II Part A adopted edition

astm-a307.sum: Specification for carbon steel bolts, studs, and threaded rod of the 60 ksi (about 414 MPa) tensile class (1/4" to 4"). Grade A is for general use; Grade B is a low-strength grade for cast iron flange piping.
facts: Size 1/4" to 4". Grade A has a minimum tensile strength of 414 MPa (60 ksi); Grade B is 414 to 690 MPa (60 to 100 ksi), with an upper limit (MPa values are converted from ksi).
Grade A is for general use; Grade B is for bolts, studs, and threaded rod for cast iron flange piping joints.
Grade C, which was used for anchor bolts, was dropped and moved to ASTM F1554 Grade 36.
The mating nut is A563 Grade A (Grade A bolts: hex up to 1-1/2" and heavy above; Grade B: heavy).
watch: A307 Grade A threaded rod cannot replace an F1554 Grade 36 anchor bolt. The anchor bolt use (the former Grade C) has moved to F1554.
A307 is a low-strength bolt of the 60 ksi tensile class, with strength roughly at the ISO 4.6 level. Do not use it interchangeably with SAE Grade 5 or 8 or with the 8.8 class.
Read an "A307 Grade C" anchor bolt on an old drawing as F1554 Grade 36.
eq_notes: Metric grade of similar strength level (thread systems differ, so it cannot be a direct substitute)
ASME Section II Part A adopted edition

astm-f3125.sum: Specification for high-strength bolts for steel structure connections. In 2015 the six standards A325, A325M, A490, A490M, F1852, and F2280 were combined into one and retained as grades.
facts: Grades: A325 and A325M (120 ksi, 830 MPa), A490 and A490M (150 ksi, 1040 MPa), and twist-off types F1852 (120 ksi) and F2280 (150 ksi). The 2025 edition added the inch-only Grade 144 (144 ksi).
The types are heavy hex and twist-off. Sizes: A325 and A490 are 1/2" to 1-1/2" (M12 to M36); F1852, F2280, and Grade 144 are 1/2" to 1-1/4".
Type 1 is medium carbon steel, carbon boron steel, or alloy steel (including boron-added); Type 3 is weathering steel. The head carries a grade mark and a manufacturer mark.
F3125 Grade A325 is the 120 ksi class (Group 120). The former A325 was divided into 120/105 ksi depending on diameter.

A490 (Group 150) cannot be hot-dip or mechanically galvanized. The current RCSC Specification (2025) allows the zinc flake coating ASTM F3393 (F1136, F2833, and F3019, which the 2020 edition listed, were replaced by F3393 in 2025).
A325 can be hot-dip (F2329) or mechanically (B695 Class 55) galvanized; in that case the nut is overtapped and lubricated, and a rotational capacity test is run on the matched bolt and nut.

Mating parts: nut ASTM A563 DH (for uncoated A325 Type 1, C, C3, D, and DH3 are also possible; for Type 3, C3 and DH3 for A325 and DH3 for A490; the A194 2H heavy nut is allowed instead of C, D, and DH), washer ASTM F436. Dimensions follow ASME B18.2.6.
watch: Read "A325" and "A490" on drawings as "F3125 Grade A325 and A490" now. The standard number changed; it is not a different product.
A BOM that specifies hot-dip or mechanical galvanizing for A490 or F2280 violates the RCSC Specification, so check the coating.
Structural bolts have a shorter threaded portion than ordinary heavy hex bolts. Do not replace them with SAE Grade 5 or 8 bolts or B18.2.1 bolts.
For galvanized A325, bolts and nuts are plated in the same process, and the rotational capacity test records of the matched assembly are obtained.

The Korean standards for the same use are the KS B 1010 (F10T) and KS B 2819 (S10T) sets; their strength systems and dimensions differ and they are not interchangeable. F3125 is specified on US-designed drawings.
eq_notes: European high-strength structural bolt set (thread and dimension systems differ)
Korean friction-grip high-strength bolt set (same use, separate standard and strength system)
astm-f3125.status: Current (established 2015 · A325 · A325M · A490 · A490M · F1852 · F2280 withdrawn in 2016 and consolidated as grades)

table.note: MPa values for A325M and A490M are the metric edition's specified values; MPa for Grade 144 is a converted value. Grades and sizes are a summary of the range in the current edition of F3125/F3125M.

astm-a325.sum: Former specification for heat-treated high-strength bolts for steel structure connections. It was withdrawn in 2016 and continued as Grade A325 of ASTM F3125, but it still often remains on drawings and BOMs.
facts: The former standard's minimum tensile strength was 120 ksi (about 827 MPa) or 105 ksi (about 724 MPa) depending on diameter; F3125 Grade A325 is the 120 ksi class.
Type 1 (medium carbon steel, carbon boron steel, and alloy steel family) and Type 3 (weathering steel). It is a heavy hex structural bolt in sizes 1/2" to 1-1/2".
Mating parts are A563 nuts (DH, etc.) and F436 hardened washers.
The metric A325M and the twist-off type F1852 were also consolidated into F3125 along with it.
watch: Even if you order "A325", it is normal for the certificate to read "F3125 Grade A325". It is not nonconforming because the standard number differs.
Do not substitute ordinary hex bolts (including SAE grade bolts) for A325. The heavy hex head, short threaded portion, and set rotational capacity test differ.

astm-a490.sum: Former specification for 150 ksi class alloy steel high-strength bolts for steel structure connections. It was withdrawn in 2016 and continued as Grade A490 of ASTM F3125.
facts: Minimum tensile strength is of the 150 ksi (about 1034 MPa) class, and the size is 1/2" to 1-1/2".
There are Type 1 and Type 3 (weathering steel).

Hot-dip or mechanical galvanizing, which applies zinc, cannot be used (RCSC 2025). RCSC 2020 allowed F1136 Grade 3, F2833 Grade 1, and F3019 Grade 4 coatings; these three were withdrawn in 2025 and replaced by F3393, and the current RCSC (2025) allows F3393 zinc flake.
The metric A490M (classes 10.9 and 10.9.3) and the twist-off type F2280 were also consolidated into F3125 along with it.
Mating parts are A563 DH (or DH3) nuts and F436 hardened washers.
watch: For a BOM that requires hot-dip galvanizing for A490, check so that the coating is changed.

If A490 properties are needed but the size exceeds 1-1/2" or the shape is an ordinary hex bolt or stud, specify ASTM A354 BD, and consider whether to add the head size, lubrication, and magnetic particle inspection requirements of F3125.

The current RCSC Specification (2025) allows reuse only for uncoated Group 120 and 144 heavy hex bolts (for snug-tightened joints without approval; for pretensioned and slip-critical joints, approval of the engineer of record is required), and prohibits reuse of Group 150 bolts such as A490 and of galvanized or coated bolts.

astm-a354.sum: Specification for Q&T alloy steel bolts, studs, and threaded rod for high strength at ambient temperature. It has two strength levels, Grade BC and BD, and covers sizes up to 4". For structural bolting over 1-1/2", BC and BD can be considered.
facts: Size 4" or less. It is for high strength at ambient temperature in air, and use at high temperature is limited, so it points to A193 for high-temperature bolting.

Mating nuts (A563, scope clause of the A354-17 edition): uncoated BC with C heavy, galvanized BC with DH heavy, and BD with DH heavy regardless of finish. The 2026 edition's scope clause does not have this table.
For steel structure connections of 1-1/2" or less, it directs the use of F3125.
BD is a grade considered for structural bolting over 1-1/2" when tensile strength above 150 ksi is needed.
watch: Even though A354 BD and A490 have similar strength, their shape and set tests differ, so do not substitute one for the other in steel structure connections.
eq_notes: Strength level similar to BD (thread system differs)
ASME Section II Part A adopted edition

astm-a449.sum: Specification for general-use Q&T steel hex cap screws, bolts, and studs. The thicker the diameter, the lower the minimum tensile strength: 120, 105, and 90 ksi; it covers 1/4" to 3".
facts: Minimum tensile strength: 120 ksi for 1" or less, 105 ksi for over 1" to 1-1/2", and 90 ksi for 1-3/4" to 3" (about 827, 724, and 621 MPa, converted values).
Type 1 is carbon steel, carbon boron steel, alloy steel, or alloy boron steel; Type 3 is weathering steel.
Quenched and tempered fasteners for general machine use (General Use) in sizes 1/4" to 3".
watch: A449 over 1-1/2" is 90 ksi (about 621 MPa), considerably lower than class 8.8 (nominal tensile strength 800 MPa). Do not regard it as a substitute for 8.8.
Even for the same A449, strength differs by diameter range, so match the certificate values to the diameter range.
Do not substitute A449 for high-strength bolts for steel structure connections (F3125).
eq_notes: ASME Section II Part A adopted edition

astm-a563.sum: Specification for carbon steel and alloy steel nuts for general structural and machine use. It sets strength grades from Grade A to DH and DH3, and is used as the mating nut for A307, F3125, and A354 bolts.
facts: Inch grades (A, C, C3, D, DH, DH3, etc.) and metric property classes are covered in one combined inch-metric standard (A563/A563M).
C3 and DH3 are weathering steel nuts and mate with weathering (Type 3) bolts.
It covers hex and hex flange nuts, and an appendix gives guidance on the suitable nut grade for each bolt type.
Unless prevented in the order, the manufacturer may supply a nut of a higher grade instead.
Nuts mated to hot-dip galvanized bolts are usually re-tapped larger after plating (overtapped), and galvanized DH is given additional lubrication.
watch: A563 DH and A194 2H are different standards (in structural sets, 2H can be used instead of DH). For high-temperature, high-pressure flange bolting, specify nuts to A194.
Do not mix non-overtapped nuts with galvanized bolts, or overtapped nuts with uncoated bolts.
Mate DH3 and C3 weathering nuts with weathering (Type 3) bolts.
eq_notes: ASME Section II Part A adopted edition
Metric nut property class (thread system differs)

astm-f436.sum: Specification for heat-treated hardened washers. It covers round, beveled, clipped, and thick washers for bolts of 1/4" to 4" and M12 to M100, used for structural bolt sets and other general machine and structural uses.
facts: For bolts of nominal size 1/4" to 4" and M12 to M100, as a combined inch-metric edition (F436/F436M). It is intended for use with A354, A449, A563, F959, and F3125 fasteners.
Type 1 is carbon steel; Type 3 is weathering steel.

Shapes: round; beveled washers (square and rectangular, 1:6 bevel, 1/2" to 1-1/2", for American Standard beam and channel flanges); clipped washers with one side cut away; and thick round washers for structural oversize holes (nominal thickness 5/16", 1/2" to 4").
ASME B18.2.6, the dimensional standard for structural fasteners, includes F436 hardened washers (round, clipped, and beveled).
watch: Ordinary flat washers (B18.21.1 Type A, F844) cannot replace F436. Check that the "washer" in a high-strength bolt BOM is a hardened washer.
For galvanized structural bolt sets, bolt, nut, and washer are plated by the same method.
When tightening a high-strength bolt, place it on the side that rotates (usually the nut side) so the bearing face is not dented.
eq_notes: Flat washer of the European structural bolt set (separate system)

astm-f1554.sum: Specification for anchor bolts embedded in concrete foundations to fix structures and equipment. It has three grades of yield 36, 55, and 105 ksi and covers straight, bent, and headed shapes and threaded rod.
facts: Shapes: straight, bent (L and J types, etc.), headed, and headless anchor bolts, and threaded rod.
The grade number is the minimum yield (ksi): 36 -> about 248 MPa, 55 -> about 379 MPa, 105 -> about 724 MPa (converted values).
Supplementary requirements can specify permanent manufacturer and grade marking and impact requirements for Grade 55 and 105.
For Grade 55, a weldable steel can be specified by a supplementary requirement.
It is the standard that replaces the former A307 Grade C anchor bolts.
watch: A307 Grade A threaded rod cannot replace F1554 Grade 36 (the anchor bolt use has moved to F1554).
Set the projection length so that thread remains above the nut after final tightening.
Anchor bolts for pump and machinery foundations often are not within the equipment supply scope, so check separately.
eq_notes: Korean and Japanese foundation bolts (strength system differs)

astm-f593.sum: Specification for general corrosion-resistant inch stainless steel bolts, cap screws, and studs (1/4" to 1-1/2"). It divides the alloys into 7 groups, and strength is set by group and condition (strain hardening, etc.).
facts: Size 1/4" to 1-1/2". The mating nut is F594 of the same alloy group, and the nut proof stress must be at least the bolt minimum tensile strength.
Alloy groups: 1 (304 family), 2 (316, 316L), 3 (321, 347), 4 (430 family, ferritic), 5 (410 family), 6 (431), 7 (630, precipitation hardened).
Conditions: groups 1 to 4 are strain-hardened (CW) and the like; martensitic groups 5 and 6 are quenched and tempered (H); 630 is age hardened (AH).
watch: If 316 is essential, do not give only the group number; write the alloy (for example, 316) together in the order.
Stainless steel on stainless steel galls easily, so apply lubricant and tighten slowly (general practice).
For high-temperature, high-pressure flange bolting, use A193 B8 or B8M, not F593.
eq_notes: Metric stainless steel bolt (strength system differs)

astm-f594.sum: Specification for general corrosion-resistant inch stainless steel nuts (1/4" to 1-1/2"). Strength is set by the same 7 alloy groups and condition system as F593 bolts.
facts: Group 1 (304 family), 2 (316), 3 (321, 347), 4 (430 family), 5 (410 family), 6 (431), 7 (630). Groups 1 to 4 are strain-hardened (CW), 5 and 6 are quenched and tempered (H), and 7 is age hardened (AH).
The mating bolt is F593 of the same group; select so that the nut proof stress is at least the bolt minimum tensile strength.
watch: For nuts on high-temperature, high-pressure flange studs, specify austenitic grades of A194. Do not substitute F594.

astm-a574.sum: Specification for Q&T alloy steel hex socket head bolts (socket head cap screws). It covers high-strength cap screws of 0.060" to 4".
facts: Size 0.060" (#0) to 4". Quenched and tempered alloy steel products.
Made of fine-grain alloy steel, with tensile (wedge), proof load, yield, elongation, and Rockwell and Vickers hardness tests.
The metric edition A574M (1.6 to 48 mm) was withdrawn in 2015. Stainless steel socket head cap screws are F837, alloy steel button, low-head, and flat head are F835, and set screws are F912.
watch: If electroplating is specified for high-hardness socket head cap screws, state the hydrogen embrittlement countermeasures (baking, etc.) and the verification method in the order.
If an old drawing specified the 1936 series socket head cap screw, check whether it is the same as the current dimensions (it is listed separately in ASME B18.3 Appendix C).
eq_notes: Metric hex socket head bolt (thread and strength systems differ)
ASME Section II Part A adopted edition

astm-f912.sum: Specification for Q&T alloy steel hex socket set screws (0.060" to 2"). Because they are parts used only in compression, they are controlled by hardness of 45 to 53 HRC instead of tensile strength.
facts: Size 0.060" to 2". The metric edition F912M was withdrawn in 2015.
For compression use only, with hardness specified as 45 to 53 HRC. This is a level equivalent to 45H of ISO 898-5.
Stainless steel set screws are ASTM F880.
watch: Set screws are not parts that carry tensile load. Use them only for fixing shafts.
If shorter than the standard minimum length, the wrench engagement is shallow and the socket is easily rounded off.

astm-f606.sum: Test methods specification for the mechanical properties of bolts, nuts, washers, DTIs, and rivets. When a product standard (A193, F3125, etc.) sets the acceptance values, F606 sets how to test.
facts: Externally threaded: product hardness, proof load (Method 1 length measurement, Method 2 yield strength, Method 3 uniform hardness), full-size axial tension and wedge tension, machined test specimen tension, total elongation at fracture, and single shear.
Internally threaded (nuts): product hardness, proof load, and cone proof load.

For washers and DTIs it covers hardness (through-hardened, carburized, stainless, nonferrous) and compression load tests, and for rivets, hardness tests. It also has embrittlement tests for metal-coated fasteners and decarburization and carburization inspection.
The metric edition F606M was withdrawn in 2015 and merged into the combined edition F606/F606M.
Its content overlaps with ASTM A370, the general test standard for steel products (for fasteners, Appendix A3), so check which one the product standard cites.
watch: Check by which method (1, 2, or 3) the "proof load acceptance" on the certificate was tested.
Machined test specimen tension values and full-size tension values do not mean the same thing. Check which test the product standard requires.

astm-a370.sum: Standard for test methods and definitions of terms for tension, bend, hardness, and impact (Charpy) testing of steel products. It is used to confirm the properties required by product standards, and Appendix A3 covers tests of steel fasteners.
facts: It contains the methods and definitions for tension testing (yield, tensile strength, elongation, reduction of area), bend, hardness (Brinell, Rockwell, portable), and Charpy impact testing.
The annexes are divided by product form: A1 bar, A2 tubular products, A3 fasteners, A4 wire, and so on. Bolt wedge tension test methods are also in F606.
ASME adopts it as SA-370.
Test methods specific to fasteners are also in ASTM F606/F606M, so check which one the product standard cites.
watch: Read Charpy values together with the test temperature. Check that the test temperature on the certificate meets the order (design minimum temperature) condition.
Hardness conversion values (HB <-> HRC) are approximate. Judge by actual measured values by the method the standard specifies.
eq_notes: ASME Section II Part A adopted edition
Metal tension test · Charpy impact test (ISO family)

astm-a153.sum: Specification for hot-dip galvanizing of iron and steel hardware such as bolts, nuts, and washers. It applies to items from which excess zinc is removed by centrifuging or similar, and sets the minimum zinc thickness in Class A to D depending on the item type.
facts: It applies to iron and steel hardware from which excess zinc (free zinc) is removed by centrifuging or similar.
Items are divided into Class A, B, C, and D, and each Class sets a minimum zinc thickness (coating weight).
For fasteners subject to the US Fastener Quality Act (FQA), statistical sampling follows F2329.
A separate hot-dip galvanizing standard for bolts, nuts, and washers, ASTM F2329, exists, and structural bolt sets follow F2329 (RCSC 2025).
watch: Threads become larger by the zinc layer thickness, so overtap the mating nut.
Do not use hot-dip galvanizing on high-strength structural bolts such as A490 and F2280.
eq_notes: Hot-dip galvanizing dedicated to bolts, nuts, and washers

astm-f2329.sum: Specification for hot-dip galvanizing of carbon steel and alloy steel bolts, screws, washers, nuts, and special threaded parts. It targets fasteners from which excess zinc is removed by centrifuging or similar after plating.
facts: Scope: carbon steel and alloy steel bolts, screws, washers, nuts, and special threaded parts. Nails and rivets are excluded.
It assumes products from which excess zinc has been removed by centrifuging or similar.
Test items: coating thickness, appearance, embrittlement test, and adhesion.
The RCSC Specification stipulates that hot-dip galvanizing of structural bolt sets follows F2329.
It is a combined inch-metric edition.
watch: Do not use hot-dip galvanizing on Group 150 bolts such as A490 and F2280 (RCSC 2025).
Overtap nuts after plating and match them to the bolt in the same process. Do not mix hot-dip zinc and mechanical zinc (B695) in one set.
Coating thickness changes thread fit and friction, so the clamping force differs at the same torque.
eq_notes: General hardware hot-dip galvanizing (cited by older bolt standards and drawings)

astm-f1941.sum: Specification for electroplating of inch and metric threaded fasteners. It sets plating thickness, hexavalent (Cr6+) chromate and trivalent (Cr3+) chromite post-treatment, corrosion resistance, and the control and removal (baking) of hydrogen embrittlement in high-strength parts.
facts: Scope: Unified inch and metric threaded fasteners. It can also be applied to unthreaded parts such as washers and pins.

Covers: plating thickness, hexavalent (Cr6+) chromate or non-Cr6+ (trivalent, Cr3+) conversion treatment, corrosion resistance, control of the hydrogen embrittlement risk of high-strength parts, and the removal treatment (baking).
The current edition is a combined inch-metric edition (F1941/F1941M).
ASTM F1940 is the test method for verifying process control of hydrogen embrittlement.
watch: If electroplating is specified for high-strength bolts, state the hydrogen embrittlement countermeasures (whether to bake and under what conditions) and the verification method (F1940) in the order. F1941-15 does not make baking mandatory if the specified maximum hardness is 39 HRC or less.
If RoHS compliance is required, specify trivalent (Cr3+) treatment rather than hexavalent (Cr6+) chromate.
eq_notes: General standard for electrogalvanizing on steel

astm-f1136.sum: Specification for a corrosion-protective coating for fasteners using a water-based zinc/aluminum dispersion inorganic basecoat (with optional sealer or topcoat). It was withdrawn in 2025 and consolidated into the zinc flake standard ASTM F3393.
facts: A non-electrolytic coating applying a water-based zinc/aluminum dispersion inorganic basecoat by dip-spin, dip-drain, or spray, to which a sealer or topcoat can be added.
The basecoat came in chromium-containing (C) and chromium-free (NC) types, and Grades were divided by minimum basecoat thickness.
The RCSC Specification (2020) allowed F1136 Grade 3 (Grade 5 for nuts), F2833 Grade 1, and F3019 Grade 4 for structural bolts.
It was withdrawn in 2025, and F3393 (zinc flake coating system) replaces F1136/F1136M, F2833, and F3019/F3019M together. F3393 coatings are supplied without hexavalent (Cr6+) chromium.
If there is no acid or phosphate pretreatment (alkaline cleaning, blasting), the process itself is regarded as not causing internal hydrogen embrittlement, so it is used on high-strength bolts.
watch: Check the "F1136 Grade 3" on an old drawing against the corresponding grade of the current F3393.
The chromium-containing (C) type may not suit RoHS-regulated items, so check that it is the chromium-free type.
The coating changes the friction coefficient, so the relationship between torque and clamping force changes.
eq_notes: Successor consolidated standard (zinc flake coating system, no hexavalent (Cr6+) chromium)

asme-b1-1.sum: Standard for inch thread form, series, class, tolerance, and designation. It covers constant-pitch series such as UNC, UNF, UNEF, and 8UN, and classes 1A to 3B.
facts: Thread forms: UN (external and internal), UNR (external only, rounded root), and UNJ (form with a specified larger root radius). The title of the current 2024 edition includes all three forms.
Series: UNC (coarse), UNF (fine), UNEF (extra fine), and constant-pitch series such as 8UN, 12UN, and 16UN.
Classes: 1A and 1B (loose), 2A and 2B (general), 3A and 3B (precision). External 1A and 2A have an allowance for plating and the like, and 3A has none.
For flange and high-temperature, high-pressure bolting over 1", 8UN (8 threads per inch) is the usual practice.
watch: Even at the same diameter, UNC and 8UN have different thread counts and may not fit. Write the diameter, threads per inch, series, and class from the specification as they are.
Electroplating is fitted within the 2A allowance, and for thick coatings such as hot-dip galvanizing, overtap the nut.
UNR is only an external thread designation and mates with an internal UN thread of the same class.

asme-b18-2-1.sum: Standard for the shape and dimensions of inch bolts and screws. It covers 9 types: square, hex, and heavy hex bolts, hex cap screws, heavy hex screws, hex flange screws, and lag screws.
facts: The 9 types covered: square head, hex, heavy hex, and bevel head bolts; hex, heavy hex, hex flange, and lobed head screws; and lag screws.
A hex bolt and a hex cap screw are separate products with separate dimension tables.
The dimensions of structural heavy hex bolts (F3125) are set separately by ASME B18.2.6. Material is specified separately by material standards such as A307, A449, and A354.
watch: Structural bolts (F3125) have B18.2.6 dimensions with a short threaded portion. Do not substitute B18.2.1 heavy hex bolts.
For plant bolting over 1", 8UN is the usual practice, so state the thread count.
eq_notes: Metric hex bolt (thread and dimension systems differ)

asme-b18-2-2.sum: Standard for the shape and dimensions of inch nuts. It covers machine screw nuts, square, hex, and heavy hex nuts, and jam, slotted, thick, castle, flange, and coupling nuts.
facts: Shapes listed: machine screw square and hex nuts, square and heavy square nuts, hex and heavy hex nuts (regular and jam), hex flat nuts, slotted, thick, and castle nuts, hex flange and large flange nuts, and hex coupling nuts.
The dimensions of heavy hex nuts for structural bolt sets follow ASME B18.2.6 (RCSC 2025).
The 2022 edition (a revision of the 2015 edition) has dimension tables from machine screw nuts to coupling nuts.
watch: UNC, UNF, and 8UN nuts do not fit each other. State the thread count.
Dimension table numbers have changed from edition to edition. Specify by nut name (for example, heavy hex nut) rather than by table number.
A jam nut is a low nut that does not carry the full load. Do not use it in place of the main fastening nut.

asme-b18-31-2.sum: General and dimensional standard for inch studs. It covers continuous-thread studs, double-end studs (fastener type and tap-end type), and stud bolts for ASME B16.5 flanges; material is specified separately by ASTM standards.
facts: Continuous-thread stud: the entire length is threaded.

Double-end stud: in the fastener type both ends have the same thread and nuts are fitted on both sides. The tap-end type is driven into a tapped hole at one end, and the thread lengths at the two ends differ.
Flange stud bolts: used on ASME B16.5 flanges and made of ASTM Committee A01 bolting materials (A193, A320, A453, etc.).
The metric edition is ASME B18.31.1M, and inch threaded rod is B18.31.3.
watch: Check on the drawing or specification whether the length of a continuous-thread stud is measured to the point (overall length) or excluding the points.
When a flange is thicker than standard, as with a pump nozzle, follow the length in the equipment general arrangement (GA) drawing, not the B16.5 table length.
For tap-end studs, specify the thread form of the driven end (normal fit or interference fit) and the thread lengths of both ends on the drawing.

asme-b18-3.sum: Dimensional standard for inch hex socket head cap screws (socket head cap screws), flat, button head, shoulder, and set screws, and hex keys. Material is specified by A574, F835, F837, F912, and others.
facts: Scope: hex socket head cap screws, flat head, button head, and low-head cap screws, shoulder screws, set screws, and hex keys (table of contents of the 2012 edition).
Material standards: alloy steel A574 (cap screws), F835 (button and flat head), F912 (set screws); stainless steel F837, F879, and F880.
The appendices have reference material such as socket gauges, wrench and bit application tables, and counterbore and drill diameters.
watch: If an old drawing specified the 1936 series socket head cap screw, check whether it is the same as the current dimensions (listed separately in Appendix C).
The minimum head diameter differs by edition, so fix the edition used as the incoming inspection basis.

asme-b18-21-1.sum: Dimensional standard for inch spring lock washers, tooth lock washers, and flat washers. From the 2009 edition it combines the flat washer standard B18.22.1, so inch washers are covered in one standard.
facts: Spring lock washers: Regular, Heavy, Extra-Duty, and High-Collar.

It covers tooth lock washers (internal tooth, heavy internal tooth, external tooth, countersunk external tooth, internal-external tooth), flat washers Type A (narrow series N, wide series W), Type B, and fender washers.
Size range: spring lock washers #0 to 3", tooth lock washers #2 to 1-1/4", flat washers #0 to 3".
The 2009 edition merged B18.22.1 (flat washers), Type A was reorganized into a preferred size table, and a fender washer table is also included.
watch: "SAE washer" is the common name for Type A narrow series, and "USS washer" for Type A wide series. There are no separate SAE or USS washer standards.
Electroplating of carbon steel spring lock washers is not recommended because of hydrogen embrittlement.
Stainless steel lock washers have a lower hardness range than carbon steel.
For structural high-strength bolts, use F436 hardened washers, not flat washers.

asme-b18-22-1.sum: Former standard for inch flat washer dimensions. It set the Type A and Type B series, and was merged into ASME B18.21.1 in 2009, so current inch flat washers are found in B18.21.1.
facts: It set the dimensions of inch flat washers of the Type A (narrow series N, wide series W) and Type B series.
It was merged at the 2009 revision of B18.21.1 (B18.21.1-2009 is the revised and combined edition of the two standards).
Material is specified separately by ASTM F844 (unhardened steel flat washers) and others.
watch: Check "B18.22.1 Type A" on a drawing against the Type A flat washer table of B18.21.1.
Do not use a flat washer in place of the hardened washer for high-strength bolts (F436).

asme-b16-5.sum: Standard for pressure-temperature ratings, materials, dimensions, tolerances, marking, and testing of NPS 1/2 to 24 pipe flanges and flanged fittings. It also has a bolting materials list, a drilling template (bolt count and diameter), and an appendix for calculating stud length.
facts: Pressure Classes 150, 300, 400, 600, 900, and 1500 (NPS 1/2 to 24) and 2500 (NPS 1/2 to 12). NPS 26 and above is ASME B16.47.
It has a table of applicable bolting materials and a table of recommended flange bolting dimensions (Tables 1B and 1C in the 2017 edition's table of contents).
The stud bolt length calculation method is in Appendix C (2017 edition's table of contents).
watch: B16.5 Class and the PN (EN 1092-1) and K (JIS B 2220) ratings are different systems. Check the bolt circle, bolt count, and diameter separately in each standard's tables.
Pump and equipment nozzle flanges may be thicker than standard, so check the stud length against the equipment drawing.
RTJ face flanges may have longer studs than RF of the same NPS and Class. If the face type changes, recheck the length.
eq_notes: European flange of the PN system (separate system)

asme-b16-47.sum: Standard for large-diameter steel flanges of NPS 26 to 60. It has separate dimension tables for two series, Series A and Series B.
facts: Sizes NPS 26 to 60. Pressure Classes 75, 150, 300, 400, 600, and 900; Class 75 exists only in Series B.
Series A and B have separate dimension tables, so check the series in the BOM.
Bolt diameters and bolt hole dimensions are shown in inch units only.
Spiral wound gasket dimensions have separate tables for Series A and B in ASME B16.20.
watch: If the BOM has only "B16.47" and no Series, check A or B. Stud count, diameter, and length may differ depending on the series.
NPS 24 and below is B16.5; NPS 26 and above is B16.47. Check a BOM that lists B16.5 for 26" or larger.
Large-diameter flange bolting often uses hydraulic tensioning, so check the extra thread length separately.

asme-b16-20.sum: Standard for materials, dimensions, tolerances, and marking of metallic gaskets for B16.5 and B16.47 flanges. It covers ring joint (R, RX, BX), spiral wound, and grooved metal gaskets with covering layers.
facts: Ring joint gaskets: R, RX, and BX types. Maximum hardness is set by material, and they are identified by ring number.

Spiral wound gaskets: the tables set dimensions for B16.5 and B16.47 Series A and B, the inner ring inside diameter, and the maximum flange bore they can be used with, and the material is indicated by color.

The current edition (2023) has three parts: ring joint, spiral wound, and grooved metal gaskets with covering layers (commonly the Kammprofile type); the metal jacketed gaskets of earlier editions were dropped.
A ring gasket must be of a softer material than the flange groove, so there is an upper hardness limit.
Nonmetallic flat gaskets are covered separately by ASME B16.21.
watch: If the ring gasket hardness is higher than the flange groove, the groove is damaged. Check the gasket material and hardness together with the flange material.
If the gasket type changes (spiral wound for RF <-> RTJ ring), recheck the stud length too.
A spiral wound gasket compresses to its design thickness only when the bolt load is sufficient. When combining with low-strength bolting, check with the gasket manufacturer.
In the BOM, write the gasket designation down to type, NPS, Class, and material (winding material, filler, ring).

asme-pcc-1.sum: ASME guideline collecting methods to assemble bolted flange joints of pressure equipment without leakage. It covers face inspection, gasket installation, lubrication, tightening sequence and stages, target clamping force, records, and assembler training and qualification.
facts: Scope: flange joints in which a ring-type gasket lies inside the bolt hole circle and does not contact outside it (full-face gasket joints are out of scope).

Content: inspection of flange and gasket faces, bolt lubrication, bolt numbering, tightening patterns (star, cross) and staged tightening, selection of target bolt stress, torque and tensioning, and joint records.
Appendix A covers training and qualification criteria for bolting assemblers.
Guidance on the use of through-hardened washers and their purchase specification, and guidance on bolt reuse, are given as appendices.
It is a guideline, not a statutory code. It becomes a mandatory requirement only when a contract or specification cites it.
watch: A work order giving only a torque value is meaningful only when the lubricant and nut factor conditions are also given. If the coating or lubricant changes, the clamping force changes greatly even at the same torque.
The detailed values for tightening sequence, number of passes, and target stress have changed from edition to edition. Check the edition the specification designates.
Check whether the specification requires field assembler qualification (Appendix A).
If washers for flange bolting must be bought separately, check whether they are through-hardened washers (see the purchase specification in the PCC-1 appendix).

sae-j429.sum: Specification of mechanical and material requirements for inch steel externally threaded fasteners (bolts, screws, studs, sems screws, U-bolts, 1-1/2" or less) for automotive and general machinery.
facts: The scope is inch steel bolts, screws, studs, washer-assembled screws (sems), and U-bolts of 1-1/2" or less.
Grades are distinguished by the number of radial lines on the head: none (Grade 1, 2), 3 lines (Grade 5), 6 lines (Grade 8).
Grade 5 has a minimum tensile strength of 120 ksi up to 1" and 105 ksi over 1"; Grade 8 is 150 ksi over the whole range (table).
The mating nut matches the SAE J995 grade (Grade 5 <-> J995 Grade 5, Grade 8 <-> J995 Grade 8).
NRC Bulletin 87-02 included SAE J429 Grade 5 and 8 in the fastener testing for nuclear plants, and reported cases where bolts marked Grade 8 turned out to be Grade 8.2.
watch: Even at the same diameter, UNC and UNF do not fit each other. Treat a line with no thread count as UNC and check.
Grade 5 and 8 bolts do not replace structural F3125 bolts (heavy hex, short threaded portion).
For high-temperature, high-pressure flange bolting, use ASTM A193, A320, etc., not SAE grades.

table.note: Checked against public technical data from 3 or more manufacturers and distributors; not yet checked against the original standard. MPa values are converted. Grade 2 is not listed because its hardness figures differ between sources.

sae-j995.sum: Specification of mechanical and material requirements for inch steel nuts for automotive and general machinery. It sets three grades for nuts of 1/4" to 1-1/2".
facts: Three grades, sizes 1/4" to 1-1/2". Machine screw nuts are not covered.
Dimensions follow SAE J482 or ASME B18.2.2.
It does not set surface defect limits; if needed, specify them separately with ASTM F812 (1/4" to 1").
watch: SAE J995 nuts and ASTM A194 and A563 nuts are different standards. Use A194 for flange bolting.
Even at the same diameter, UNC and UNF nuts do not fit each other.

api-20e.sum: Specification of qualification, production, and documentation requirements for alloy steel and carbon steel bolting for oil and gas equipment (especially offshore and subsea). It divides the requirement level into three stages, BSL-1 to 3.
facts: Scope: manufacturing qualification, production, and documentation of alloy steel and carbon steel bolting (studs, bolts, screws, nuts, etc.) for oil and gas equipment.
There are three stages: BSL-1 (basic), BSL-2 (intermediate), and BSL-3 (most stringent); the higher the number, the more technical, quality, and qualification requirements.
Corrosion-resistant bolting such as stainless steel and nickel alloys is covered by the companion standard API Spec 20F (Corrosion Resistant Bolting).
watch: 20E conformity cannot be attached by finished product inspection alone; the product must come from a manufacturing process matched to 20E requirements. Do not relabel ordinary A193 B7 as a 20E product.
If the BOM has only "API 20E" and no BSL, check the BSL level.
Read the BSL that the equipment standard requires together with the material grade (for example, B7, L7).

asme-b18-2-6.sum: Dimensional standard for 5 types of US structural high-strength fasteners. It covers heavy hex and twist-off structural bolts, heavy hex nuts, F436 washers, and F959 DTIs.
facts: The 5 types covered: heavy hex structural bolts (currently F3125), heavy hex nuts (A563), hardened washers round, clipped, and beveled (F436), compressible-washer-type DTIs (F959), and twist-off structural bolts (heavy hex, round head).
The dimensions of structural heavy hex bolts and nuts follow this standard (RCSC 2025).
Structural bolts have a shorter threaded portion than ordinary heavy hex bolts.
The metric edition is ASME B18.2.6M.
watch: Do not substitute ordinary heavy hex bolts (B18.2.1) or SAE bolts for structural bolts.
Match the DTI type (325, 490, weathering -3) to the bolt grade.

astm-f468.sum: General-use specification for nonferrous metal bolts, cap screws, and studs (F468) and nuts (F467). It covers various commonly used nonferrous alloys, so specify down to the alloy.
facts: F468 covers bolts, hex cap screws, and studs (1/4" to 1-1/2") and socket-type screws (#0 to 1-1/2"); F467 covers nuts (1/4" to 1-1/2").
The mating nut of F468 bolts is F467, and both F468 and F467 have separate metric editions (F468M and F467M).
Both standards use inch-pound units only.
watch: For a BOM that gives only a trade name such as "Monel (trademark) bolt", check the alloy and the F468 grade designation.
Check for dissimilar metal corrosion where it contacts carbon steel and stainless steel parts.
Mate nuts with F467.

gr-b7.sum: Quenched and tempered bolting grade of Cr-Mo steel (4140 family) in ASTM A193. Minimum tensile strength is 125 ksi (converted 862 MPa) up to 2-1/2", and the criterion falls as the diameter gets larger; the mating nut is usually A194 2H.
facts: A193 mandatorily follows the A962 common requirements, and points to A320 for low-temperature bolting and to A354 for alloy steel bolting in the lower high-temperature range.
Minimum tensile/yield by diameter: 125/105 ksi up to 2-1/2", 115/95 ksi over 2-1/2" to 4", 100/75 ksi over 4" to 7" (table).
The maximum hardness is the same for all diameters: 321 HBW (35 HRC).
The "diameter" in the table is based on the thread diameter of the finished product, not the bar stock (ASME Interpretation BPV II-A-22-07, SA-193, applicable to the 2017 edition).
ASME VIII-1 Interpretation VIII-81-68 (1981): to use SA-193 B7 under 2-1/2" down to -50 °F (converted -46 °C), impact testing must be done or the UCS-66 exemption provision must apply.

MIL-DTL-1222J (US Navy high-reliability fasteners, 2000) accepts commercial A193 B7 but separately requires an upper strength limit, a lower upper hardness limit, and a higher minimum tensile strength for products over 2-1/2".
watch: If the BOM has only "A193 B7" and no nut, confirm by asking whether the nut is a 2H heavy nut or Grade 7, and also whether it is coated.
For studs over 2-1/2", the basis is 115 ksi, not 125 ksi (100 ksi over 4") - check the strength value in the clamping force and torque calculation.
For bolting exposed to H2S, use B7M, not B7 (A320 L7M for low temperature) - ISO 15156-2 A.2.2.4 lists these two grades.
Do not trust the stamping alone - NRC Bulletin 87-02 reported a case where the actual tensile strength of a bolt stamped B7 was about 55 ksi. Confirm with the certificate and hardness.
eq_notes: Corresponding grade of alloy steel bolt material for high-temperature use (A193 B7 is noted for reference in the JIS table). KS D 3755 of the same name has been withdrawn

The strength, elongation, and reduction of area of the first two rows were also confirmed to be the same as the A193 of the time by the footnote to MIL-DTL-1222J Table II. MPa values are converted (the last digits may differ from the metric values of A193M).

gr-b7m.sum: Hardness-limited Cr-Mo steel bolting grade of ASTM A193. With a maximum hardness of 235 HBW it is softer than B7 and has a lower minimum tensile strength of 100 ksi, and is used for H2S-exposed bolting. The final heat treatment clause is subject to revision after A193-25 (WK95557), so check the applicable edition.
facts: ASTM work item WK95557 covers a revision that removes "cut to length" from the B7M final heat treatment clause of A193-25 - whether it is reflected in the current A193-26 issued afterward has not been confirmed, so state the applicable edition when ordering.
Minimum tensile strength 100 ksi (converted 689 MPa) - lower than the 125 ksi of B7 of the same diameter (2-1/2" or less).
Maximum hardness 235 HBW (321 HBW for B7).
ISO 15156-2 (NACE MR0175) A.2.2.4 lists A193 B7M and A320 L7M as bolting exposed to H2S (citing the BSEE and LBNL 2016 presentation).
The general hardness limit that ISO 15156-2 sets for carbon steel and low-alloy steel is 22 HRC (NACE interpretation collection, 2025).
watch: If B7M is used as a substitute for B7 on an ordinary line, the strength is lower and the clamping force may be insufficient - check the design strength value.
Pair B7M studs with hardness-limited nuts (2HM, 7M) - if only the nut is 2H, the sour condition is not met.
Public sources differ on the Rockwell notation of 235 HBW, as 99 HRB or 22 HRC - judge the certificate by the notation of the applicable edition.

gr-b16.sum: Cr-Mo-V steel bolting grade of ASTM A193. Up to 2-1/2" the minimum tensile strength is 125 ksi (converted 862 MPa), the same as B7, and with added vanadium it is used at higher temperatures than B7. JIS G 4107 SNB16 corresponds to it.
facts: Corresponding material: JIS G 4107 SNB16 (KS D 3755 of the same name has been withdrawn).
Minimum tensile/yield 125/105 ksi (converted 862/724 MPa) up to 2-1/2", elongation 18 %, reduction of area 50 %.
Over 2-1/2" the minimum tensile strength falls - MIL-DTL-1222J (2000) states that it separately requires a higher minimum tensile strength than A193 in this range.

As a Cr-Mo-V steel with added vanadium, it is described as a grade used for high-temperature bolting at higher temperatures than B7 - check the service temperature limit in the allowable stress table of the applicable code.
watch: B16 over 2-1/2" has a lower minimum strength, so check the strength value in the calculation by diameter.
B16 and B7 look the same - distinguish them by stamping and certificate.
eq_notes: Corresponding grade of alloy steel bolt material for high-temperature use (A193 B16 is noted for reference in the JIS table). KS D 3755 has been withdrawn

gr-b8.sum: Type 304 austenitic stainless steel bolting grade of ASTM A193. Class 1 is solution-treated with a minimum tensile strength of 75 ksi (converted 517 MPa); Class 2 is strain-hardened and raises this up to 125 ksi at 3/4" or less, but it falls as the diameter gets larger.
facts: When ordering strain-hardened austenitic steel, A193 directs the buyer to understand Appendix X1 thoroughly.
Class 1 (solution-treated): minimum tensile/yield 75/30 ksi (converted 517/207 MPa), elongation 30 %.
Class 2 (strain-hardened after solution treatment): falls by diameter from 125/100 ksi at 3/4" or less to 100/50 ksi at 1-3/8" to 1-1/2" (table).
The diameter of Class 2 is judged by the thread diameter of the finished product, not the bar stock - ASME Interpretation BPV II-A-22-07 (SA-193, applicable to the 2017 edition).
ASME VIII-1 Interpretation VIII-77-09 (1977): at high temperature, Class 2 also loses the strength obtained by strain hardening, so the same allowable stress as Class 1 is used.
watch: Austenitic studs and nuts gall easily - apply an anti-seize compound and tighten slowly.
For a BOM that says only "B8", check the Class - at the same 3/4" or less, the minimum tensile strength differs by 50 ksi between Class 1 and 2.
Some specifications require SH and Cl. 2 marking on both ends of Class 2 for field identification (NASA Stennis Space Center piping standard SSTD-8070-0047-PIPE).

gr-b8m.sum: Type 316 (Mo-containing) austenitic stainless steel bolting grade of ASTM A193. Class 1 is solution-treated with a minimum tensile strength of 75 ksi (converted 517 MPa), and strain-hardened Class 2 has separate values by diameter.
facts: A193 treats austenitic steel in the solution-treated or strain-hardened-after-solution-treatment condition, and directs the buyer to understand Appendix X1 thoroughly when ordering strain-hardened products.
Class 1 (solution-treated): minimum tensile/yield 75/30 ksi (converted 517/207 MPa), elongation 30 % - the same as B8 Class 1.

For Class 2 the strength falls as the diameter gets larger, and the diameter is judged by the thread diameter of the finished product - ASME Interpretation BPV II-A-22-07 (SA-193, applicable to the 2017 edition).
ASME VIII-1 Interpretation BPV VIII-1-19-10 (2019): SA-193 B8M2 in Table UHA-23 is read as Class 2B - Class 2 and 2B are different classifications.
Unlike B8, which is 304, B8M contains Mo and is mainly used in chloride environments; the mating nut is A194 8M.
watch: Class 2 values differ between public sources (a minimum tensile strength of 110 ksi and one of 125 ksi are both given for 3/4" or less) - confirm with the applicable edition's table and the certificate.
Stainless steel nuts and studs risk galling - use an anti-seize compound.

gr-l7.sum: Grade L7 of the Cr-Mo steel in ASTM A320 (low-temperature bolting). Up to 2-1/2" its strength is in the 125 ksi class (converted 862 MPa), the same as A193 B7, and after Charpy impact testing at -150 °F (converted -101 °C) it is used for low-temperature flanges.
facts: A320 sets in Table 1 the diameters to which the minimum mechanical properties of each grade and Class apply, and notes that because of hardenability the maximum diameter at which the required properties can be obtained may be limited for some grades.
Nut material used with A320 bolting is also subject to impact testing (A320 1.4).
Charpy impact: an average of 3 specimens of 20 ft·lbf (converted 27 J) or more at -150 °F (converted -101 °C).
Minimum tensile/yield 125/105 ksi (converted 862/724 MPa) up to 2-1/2", elongation 16 %, reduction of area 50 %.

ASME VIII-1 Interpretation VIII-1-01-25 (2001): SA-320 L7, L7A, and L43 impact tested at -150 °F can be used with SA-194 Grade 4 and 7 nuts carrying the low-temperature impact supplementary requirement at an MDMT of -150 °F or above without additional lateral expansion testing.
The US Coast Guard rule for low-temperature vessel piping (46 CFR 56.50-105) also sets bolting L7 and L43 at a minimum service temperature of -150 °F and an average of 20 ft·lbf.
watch: If only the stud is L7 and the nut is 2H, it is not a low-temperature combination - match the nut to one that is also impact tested.
L7 and B7 look the same - distinguish them by stamping and the impact test record on the certificate.
For L7 over 2-1/2", the diameter range and values differ because public sources list different ranges (up to 2-1/2", 4", and 7") - confirm with the applicable edition's table.

gr-l43.sum: Grade L43 of ASTM A320, a low-temperature bolting grade of the AISI 4340 family. A320 notes that meeting the -101 °C (-150 °F) impact value may require further composition limits, such as steel with reduced P and S.
facts: The standard notes that to meet the -101 °C impact value with L43, additional composition limits may be required, such as using steel with further reduced P and S.
Impact test temperature -150 °F (-101 °C): the A320 scope clause gives this value as the test temperature for the L43 Table 2 impact value.
The steel type is of the AISI 4340 (Ni-Cr-Mo) family - as stated in the A320 scope clause.
ASME VIII-1 Interpretation VIII-1-01-25 (2001) and 46 CFR 56.50-105 treat L43 together with L7 as a -150 °F impact-tested, minimum service temperature grade.

The mating nut named in ASME Interpretation VIII-1-01-25 (2001) is SA-194 Grade 4 and 7 with the low-temperature impact supplementary requirement - confirm before ordering whether Grade 4 is currently listed.
watch: To meet the -101 °C impact value with L43, additional composition limits (reduced P and S, etc.) may be required - first check the test temperature and additional impact requirements in the specification.

gr-660.sum: ASTM A453 Grade 660 high-temperature bolting made of A-286 (UNS S66286), a Fe-Ni-Cr precipitation-hardening iron-based superalloy. A453 sets Class A, B, C, and D for Grade 660.
facts: Alloy: an iron-based precipitation-hardening alloy with about 25 % Ni and about 15 % Cr plus Ti, Mo, V, and B - the corresponding EN 1.4980 has Ni 24.0-27.0, Cr 13.5-16.0, and Ti 1.90-2.30 %.
Heat treatment: solution treatment followed by aging (precipitation hardening). The solution treatment and aging conditions differ by Class.
A453 covers nuts, washers, and screws as well as bolts and studs.
Corresponding materials: JIS SUH660, EN 1.4980 (X6NiCrTiMoVB25-15-2).
NACE MR0175/ISO 15156-3 Table A.26 places UNS S66286 in the solution-treated and aged (or 2-step aged) condition at 35 HRC or less (NACE interpretation MP 2017-04).
watch: "A-286" is a common name - in the order, write A453 Grade 660 together with the Class (A, B, C, D).
If the Class is omitted, the strength criterion cannot be known - A453 sets the yield strength by Class, and the overall range is 50-120 ksi (345-825 MPa in the metric edition).
Because it is an austenitic alloy, galling occurs easily - use a high-temperature anti-seize compound.

gr-2h.sum: Carbon steel nut grade 2H of ASTM A194 (quenched and tempered according to public manufacturer and distributor data). With a heavy hex proof stress of 175 ksi (converted 1207 MPa) it is a common mate for B7 studs, and RCSC allows it in structural connections in place of A563 C, D, and DH.
facts: A194 scope: carbon, alloy, and martensitic stainless steel nuts 1/4" to 4" (M12 to M100), austenitic nuts 1/4" (M12) and larger.
The standard prohibits grade substitution without the buyer's permission.
Heavy hex proof stress 175 ksi (converted 1207 MPa).
According to public manufacturer and distributor data: carbon steel is quenched and tempered, and the minimum tempering temperature is 850 °F (converted 454 °C).
ASME Interpretation IIA-89-07 (1989): SA-194 2H nuts cannot be made of AISI 4140 - alloy steel nuts belong to Grade 7.
watch: Public sources agree on a lower hardness limit of 24 HRC, but the upper limit differs between sources, at 35 HRC and 38 HRC - confirm with the applicable edition's table.
If the B7 stud BOM has no nut grade, check whether it is 2H or Grade 7.
eq_notes: Structural heavy nut - RCSC allows A194 2H in place of A563 C, D, and DH

gr-a194-7.sum: Cr-Mo alloy steel quenched and tempered nut grade 7 of ASTM A194, and its hardness-limited variant 7M. Grade 7 has a heavy hex proof stress of 175 ksi (converted 1207 MPa) and mates with B7, B16, and L7 studs.
facts: A194 scope: carbon, alloy, and martensitic stainless steel nuts 1/4" to 4" (M12 to M100). Grade substitution without the buyer's permission is prohibited.
Grade 7 is a nut of quenched and tempered Cr-Mo alloy steel (4140 family); 7M is the same family with limited hardness, for sour service.
Grade 7 heavy hex proof stress 175 ksi (converted 1207 MPa) - the same class as 2H.
ASME Interpretation IIA-92-06 (1991): if 2H and 7 nuts are heat treated as 2HM and 7M, the hardness test must be redone.

ASME Interpretation VIII-1-01-25 (2001): SA-194 Grade 4 and 7 nuts with the low-temperature impact supplementary requirement are used with L7 and L43 impact tested at -150 °F at an MDMT of -150 °F or above.
watch: Whether "Grade 4" nuts in an old specification are currently listed differs between public sources, so confirm before ordering.

gr-7l.sum: A nut made by adding the low-temperature impact test supplementary requirement to A194 Grade 7 and 7M nuts, used as the mate for A320 low-temperature bolting. A320 requires the nut material used with bolting to be impact tested as well; confirm the supplementary requirement number and marking against the applicable edition.
facts: Nut material used with A320 bolting is also subject to impact testing (A320 1.4).
A320 requires that the nut material fitted to ferritic low-temperature bolting also follow impact requirements.

ASME VIII-1 Interpretation VIII-1-01-25 (2001, shown at that time as SA-194 supplementary requirement S4): SA-194 Grade 4 and 7 nuts with the low-temperature impact supplementary requirement can be used with L7, L7A, and L43 impact tested at -150 °F at an MDMT of -150 °F or above.
46 CFR 56.50-105 (vessel low-temperature piping) sets nut Grade 4 at a minimum service temperature of -150 °F and an average impact of 20 ft·lbf.
watch: If the stud test temperature is specified lower than the default, specify the nut test temperature the same (practical recommendation).

The supplementary requirement number may differ by edition (the 2001 ASME Interpretation shows S4) - in the order, write "low-temperature impact test supplementary requirement" together with the test temperature.

gr-a194-8.sum: Austenitic stainless steel nut grades 8 (304) and 8M (316) of ASTM A194. Heavy hex proof stress is 80 ksi (converted 552 MPa), and strain-hardened austenitic nuts are specified by supplementary requirement S1.
facts: Supplementary requirement S1: used when specifying austenitic nuts strain-hardened after solution treatment; for this, A194 directs the buyer to understand 8.2.2, S1, and Appendix X1 thoroughly.
Grade 8 is 304 and 8M is 316 stainless steel.

The "A" in 8A and 8MA indicates a nut given a carbide solution treatment, and the alloy is the same as 8 and 8M (304, 316). Do not reinterpret the 8 and 8A designations in a BOM; write them as they are and confirm with the supplier's documents (checked against public technical data from 3 manufacturers and distributors; not yet checked against the original standard).
Heavy hex proof stress 80 ksi (converted 552 MPa) - the same for 8 and 8M.
ASME Interpretation BPV II-A-21-27 (applicable to the SA-194 2019 edition): the proof load test (8.2.1, Table 3) also applies to 5/8" Grade 8 heavy hex and hex nuts.
Mating studs are 8 for B8 and 8M for B8M - match the alloy.
watch: Stainless steel nuts and studs risk galling - use an anti-seize compound.

gr-sae-5.sum: Inch-system medium carbon steel quenched and tempered bolt grade of SAE J429. Minimum tensile strength is 120 ksi (converted 827 MPa) up to 1" and 105 ksi over 1" to 1-1/2", and 3 radial lines are marked on the head. The range is up to 1-1/2".
facts: The standard's range is up to 1-1/2" (scope of SAE J429).
1/4" to 1": proof stress 85 ksi, yield 92 ksi, tensile 120 ksi, hardness 25–34 HRC (table).
Over 1" to 1-1/2": proof stress 74 ksi, yield 81 ksi, tensile 105 ksi, hardness 19–30 HRC.
The head marking is 3 radial lines.
The mating nut is SAE J995 Grade 5 as the basic combination.
watch: Do not use a Grade 5 hex bolt in place of an F3125 A325 structural bolt - RCSC specifies structural connection bolts as F3125 grades.
Grade 5 over 1" falls to a tensile strength of 105 ksi - check the strength value in the calculation for large diameters.
