Proof stress
Yield min
Tensile min
Hardness
table.note: Checked against public technical data from 3 or more manufacturers and distributors; not yet checked against the original standard. MPa values are converted.

gr-sae-8.sum: Inch-system medium carbon alloy steel quenched and tempered bolt grade of SAE J429. Minimum tensile strength is 150 ksi (converted 1034 MPa) over the whole range of 1/4" to 1-1/2", and 6 radial lines are marked on the head.
facts: 1/4" to 1-1/2": proof stress 120 ksi (converted 827 MPa), yield 130 ksi (converted 896 MPa), tensile 150 ksi (converted 1034 MPa), hardness 33–39 HRC.
The head marking is 6 radial lines.
The mating nut is SAE J995 Grade 8 as the basic combination.
NRC Bulletin 87-02: among nuclear plant samples, there was a case where a bolt marked as SAE Grade 8 turned out to be Grade 8.2.

The post-plating baking criterion differs between standards - ISO 21457 recommends it for products over 31 HRC, and ASTM F1941 (2015) does not make it mandatory if the maximum hardness is 39 HRC or less (citing the BSEE and LBNL presentation). Grade 8 (33–39 HRC) falls on this boundary.
watch: Do not use Grade 8 in place of an A490 structural bolt - RCSC specifies structural connection bolts as F3125 grades.
Do not confuse "Grade 8" (SAE bolt), the nut property class "8", and the metric bolt "8.8".
Do not trust the grade from the head marking alone - confirm with the certificate and hardness.

gr-f3125-a325.sum: The 120 ksi class of heavy hex structural bolts for steel structure connections. Consolidated into the current ASTM F3125, A325 (hex head) and F1852 (TC type, tightened by twisting off the end spline) are included as the same strength grade.
facts: Diameter: heavy hex 1/2" to 1-1/2", and TC type F1852 up to 1-1/4" (F3125 range). Minimum tensile strength 120 ksi (converted 827 MPa) - the withdrawn A325 had two steps of 120/105 ksi, but F3125 has the single 120 ksi.
Type 1: medium carbon steel, carbon boron steel, alloy steel (including boron-added); Type 3: atmospheric corrosion-resistant (weathering) steel - Type 3 has an underline on the grade symbol.

Mating parts (RCSC): for uncoated Type 1, A563 C, C3, D, DH, DH3; for plated products DH; for Type 3, C3 and DH3 heavy nuts. A194 2H is allowed instead of C, D, and DH. Washers are F436, of the same Type as the bolt.

Coating (RCSC): hot-dip zinc (F2329), mechanical zinc (B695 Class 55), and zinc flake (F3393) are possible. Plated nuts are overtapped per A563, and galvanized bolts go through the rotational capacity test as a set with lubricated nuts.
F1852 (TC type): a Group 120 tension control set tightened by twisting off the end spline. The head marking is A325TC.
The metric edition grade is F3125M Grade A325M (830 MPa).
watch: Do not substitute ordinary hex bolts such as A449 or SAE Grade 5 - RCSC specifies structural connection bolts as F3125 Grade A325, A490, and so on.
Calculations and drawings based on the withdrawn A325 (105 ksi for large diameters) may differ from F3125 (120 ksi) certificate values.

RCSC (2025): plated and coated bolts and the 150 ksi class cannot be reused. Uncoated A325 heavy hex can be reused for snug-tightened joints; for pretensioned and slip-critical joints, approval of the engineer of record is required.
Bolt, nut, and washer must be bundled in the same plating process and lot - if only the nut is changed, the rotational capacity test result becomes meaningless.

KS B 1010 F10T (1000 MPa class), commonly used for steel structure friction-grip connections in Korea, has a different strength system from A325. F10T (tensile 1000–1200 MPa per JIS B 1186) and ISO 10.9 (tensile 1040 MPa or more) are at a similar level but are not the same grade.
eq_notes: A325 at 120 ksi (converted 827 MPa) and 8.8 (800, 830 MPa) are at a similar level but are not the same grade, and dimension and set requirements also differ, so direct substitution is not possible
gr-f3125-a325.status: Current (F3125 grade). The standalone standards A325 and F1852 were withdrawn (→ ASTM F3125, 2016)

gr-f3125-a490.sum: The 150 ksi class of structural heavy hex bolts (RCSC Group 150). Tensile strength is 150–173 ksi; hot-dip and mechanical galvanizing are not allowed, and they cannot be reused.
facts: Diameter: heavy hex 1/2" to 1-1/2", and TC type F2280 up to 1-1/4" (F3125 range). Tensile 150–173 ksi (converted 1034–1193 MPa).
Maximum hardness 38 HRC. Two kinds: Type 1 and Type 3 (weathering, underline on the grade symbol).
Coating: RCSC does not allow hot-dip or mechanical galvanizing on the 150 ksi class. Zinc flake (F3393) was confirmed in the IFI 144 evaluation not to cause delayed hydrogen fracture of A490.

Mating parts (RCSC): for uncoated Type 1, A563 DH and DH3; for coated products (zinc flake F3393), DH; for Type 3, DH3 heavy nuts - A194 2H is allowed instead of DH. Washers are F436, of the same Type as the bolt.
F2280 (TC type): a Group 150 tension control set tightened by twisting off the end spline (marking A490TC).
Reuse prohibited (RCSC) - an A490 that has been tension-tightened once is not reused.
watch: "Galvanized A490" is a combination RCSC does not allow - if it appears on a drawing, ask the designer whether to change it to galvanized A325 or to F3393 zinc flake.
Do not replace with SAE Grade 8 or A354 BD - RCSC specifies structural connection bolts as F3125 grades.

In hot-dip galvanizing, hydrogen picked up during pickling can be trapped in the zinc layer, raising a delayed fracture concern for A490 class bolts - RCSC does not allow galvanizing of the 150 ksi class.
eq_notes: A490 150–173 ksi (converted 1034–1193 MPa), 10.9 tensile 1040 MPa or more, F10T 1000 MPa class (1000–1200 MPa per JIS) - at a similar level but not the same grade, and dimension, set, and test requirements also differ
gr-f3125-a490.status: Current (F3125 grade). The standalone standards A490 and F2280 were withdrawn (→ ASTM F3125, 2016)

gr-f1554.sum: The three strength grades of the anchor bolt standard for bolts embedded in concrete foundations. The number is the minimum yield strength (ksi), the projecting end is painted blue, yellow, or red to distinguish them, and for Grade 55 a weldable steel can be specified by supplementary requirement S1.
facts: Grade 36: minimum yield 36 ksi (converted 248 MPa), blue.
Grade 55: minimum yield 55 ksi (converted 379 MPa), yellow.
Grade 105: minimum yield 105 ksi (converted 724 MPa), red.
Forms: includes straight, headed, bent (L and J types), and threaded rod anchors. Length, thread length, and bend dimensions are set by the foundation drawing.
S1: supplementary requirement specifying weldable Grade 55 steel.
S2 and S3: supplementary requirements for permanent identification of manufacturer and grade; S4: impact requirement for Grade 55 and 105.

Galvanizing requirements are in Section 7 of the standard - example from a state highway agency specification (Iowa DOT): F2329 hot-dip or B695 Class 55 mechanical zinc, bolt, nut, and washer in the same process, and plated nuts overtapped per A563.
watch: If field welding (base plate reinforcement or position correction) is possible, state the welding conditions in the specification, such as weldable Grade 55 (S1).
The color marking is only on the projecting end and is hard to check after casting - compare grade, color, and certificate at receiving.
Read an old A307 Grade C anchor bolt designation as F1554 Grade 36 (A307 states that it replaced Grade C with F1554 Grade 36).
eq_notes: A307 states that it replaced Grade C with F1554 Grade 36

gr-a563-dh.sum: High-strength nut grade of ASTM A563. RCSC specifies DH for structural bolts such as A325 and A490, and DH3 for weathering (Type 3), and regards it as a grade with sufficient strength even as an overtapped plated nut.
facts: DH3: nut for weathering (Type 3) structural bolts.
Plated DH is overtapped, and a lubricated nut is rotational-capacity tested as a matched set with the bolt and washer - RCSC treats plated bolts and nuts as matched sets.
RCSC allows A194 2H nuts instead of A563 C, D, and DH, and regards only A563 DH and DH3 and A194 2H as suitable for overtapped plated nuts.
Marking: DH or DH3 plus the manufacturer's symbol.
watch: For A490 (150 ksi class), by RCSC criteria only uncoated DH and DH3, and for coated products (zinc flake) only DH - C and D nuts are not used (A194 2H is allowed instead of DH).
Do not fit uncoated DH on hot-dip galvanized bolts - a nut that is not overtapped will not go on or will damage the thread.
Even when accepting A194 2H instead, check that it has the same finish (plated or not, overtapped).
A563 "DH" and A194 "2H" are grades of different standards - distinguish them by marking.
eq_notes: Allowed by RCSC instead of A563 C, D, and DH (same finish condition)

gr-b7-vs-b16.sum: Comparison of B7, B16, and B7M of ASTM A193. Up to 2-1/2", B7 and B16 are the same at a minimum tensile strength of 125 ksi and B7M is lower at 100 ksi; B16 is for high temperature and B7M for H2S-exposed bolting.
facts: Classification based on JIS G 4107: SNB7 (A193 B7 noted for reference) is chromium-molybdenum steel, and SNB16 (A193 B16 noted for reference) is chromium-molybdenum-vanadium steel.
Minimum tensile strength up to 2-1/2": B7 and B16 125 ksi (converted 862 MPa), B7M 100 ksi (converted 689 MPa).
Maximum hardness: B7 321 HBW, B7M 235 HBW - B7M lowers the hardness, and the strength is also lower as a result.
ISO 15156-2 A.2.2.4 lists B7M (A320 L7M for low temperature) as H2S-exposed bolting (citing the BSEE and LBNL 2016 presentation).
B16 is a Cr-Mo-V steel with added vanadium, described as a grade used at higher temperatures than B7.
watch: The three grades look the same and are distinguished only by stamping and certificate - compare the stamping at receiving to prevent mix-ups.
If B7M is used in place of B7, the strength is lower - unless it is a sour condition, first check the design strength value.

head: Item
B7
B16
B7M
table.note: Strength is checked against public technical data from 3 or more manufacturers and distributors (not yet checked against the original standard); steel type is from Table 1 of the JIS G 4107 revision draft.

mat-4140.sum: A family of medium carbon low-alloy steels containing Cr and Mo. JIS G 4107 lists SAE 4140, 4142, and 4145 as the representative steel types for bolt material SNB7 (A193 B7 noted for reference).
facts: JIS G 4107 SNB7 composition (revision draft): C 0.38–0.48, Mn 0.75–1.00, Cr 0.80–1.10, Mo 0.15–0.25 %.
JIS G 4053 SCM440 composition: C 0.38–0.43, Mn 0.60–0.90, Cr 0.90–1.20, Mo 0.15–0.30 % - lower Mn range and higher Cr range than SNB7.

A320 notes that because of hardenability the maximum diameter at which the required properties can be obtained may be limited for some grades, and also has grade L43, a low-temperature grade of the AISI 4340 family with added Ni.
Corresponding steel type: JIS G 4053 SCM440. Bar stock for bolts is JIS G 4107 SNB7 (KS D 3755 of the same name has been withdrawn).
watch: "4140 bolt" is only a material name, not a standard grade - specify with grades such as B7 and L7 that have test and marking requirements.

When making SNB7 or B7 bolts from SCM440 bar stock, confirm with the mill certificate that the composition of each heat is within the range of the bolt material in question (by JIS, the Mn and Cr ranges of SCM440 and SNB7 differ).
eq_notes: Corresponding steel type - with Mn 0.60–0.90 and Cr 0.90–1.20 % it is not the same as the SNB7 composition range

mat-316.sum: Mo-containing austenitic stainless steel. UNS S31600, EN 1.4401, and JIS SUS316 correspond to each other, and the low-carbon type 316L is S31603, 1.4404, and SUS316L.
facts: 316L (S31603): low-carbon type - the corresponding EN 1.4404 has C 0.030 % or less, and ISO 3506 also allows the "L" designation (for example, A4L-80) for austenitic fasteners with C 0.030 % or less.

It is not hardened by heat treatment, and strength is raised by cold working - A193 provides the solution-treated or strain-hardened-after-solution-treatment condition, and ISO 3506 treats A4-80 and above as strain-hardened products.
Correspondence: JIS SUS316 / EN 1.4401 (X5CrNiMo17-12-2); for 316L, SUS316L / 1.4404 (X2CrNiMo17-12-2). 316Ti is 1.4571.
watch: For a specification that says only "316L bolt", also specify and confirm the strength grade (B8M Class, A4-70, etc.).
Confirm the distinction between 304 and 316 (presence of Mo) by certificate and PMI, not by a magnet.

mat-304.sum: Austenitic stainless steel with about 18 % Cr and about 8–10 % Ni (18-8). UNS S30400, EN 1.4301, and JIS SUS304 correspond to each other, and the low-carbon type 304L is S30403, 1.4307 (or 1.4306), and SUS304L.
facts: Corresponding EN 1.4301 (X5CrNi18-10): C 0.07 % or less, Cr 17.0–19.5, Ni 8.0–10.5 %.
304L (S30403): low-carbon type - the corresponding EN 1.4307 has C 0.030 % or less, and ISO 3506 also allows the "L" designation for C 0.030 % or less.

It is not hardened by heat treatment, and strength is raised by cold working - A193 provides the solution-treated or strain-hardened-after-solution-treatment condition, and ISO 3506 treats A2-80 as a strain-hardened product.
Correspondence: JIS SUS304 / EN 1.4301 (X5CrNi18-10); for 304L, SUS304L / 1.4307 (X2CrNi18-9) - 1.4306, with slightly higher Ni, is also used as a 304L family material.
watch: For a BOM that says only "SUS bolt", also check whether it is 304 or 316 and the strength grade (B8 Class, A2-70).
Cold-worked products can be magnetic - do not judge by a magnet.

mat-a286.sum: Iron-based superalloy hardened by precipitation, with about 25 % Ni and about 15 % Cr plus Ti and others (UNS S66286, commonly A-286). Bolting is sourced as ASTM A453 Grade 660, and bar and forgings as A638 Grade 660.
facts: Strength is obtained by solution treatment followed by aging (precipitation hardening) - A453 sets Class A, B, C, and D for Grade 660.
Bolting standard: ASTM A453 Grade 660 (Class A, B, C, D). For high-temperature bar and forgings, ASTM A638 Grade 660.
Correspondence: JIS SUH660, EN 1.4980 (X6NiCrTiMoVB25-15-2).
watch: "A-286" is a common name - order bolts as A453 Grade 660 + Class.
Because it is a precipitation-hardening alloy, welding and local heating change its properties.
Use a high-temperature lubricant to prevent galling.

mat-718.sum: Alloy 718, a precipitation-hardening (age-hardening) nickel-based alloy, UNS N07718. It is the subject alloy of ASTM A1014 (bolting for high-temperature use) and API 6A718 (for oil and gas equipment).
facts: Strength is obtained by solution treatment followed by aging to form a Ni-Nb precipitate phase (γ″) - it keeps its strength for a long time even at high temperature.
Bolting standard: ASTM A1014/A1014M (718 bolting for high-temperature use). The material standard for oil and gas equipment is API 6A718.
Bar and forgings: ASTM B637 (precipitation-hardening nickel alloys for high-temperature use) includes N07718.
API 6A718 calls it "Nickel Base Alloy 718 (UNS N07718)", and it is also commonly called by the trade name Inconel (trademark) 718.
watch: For a BOM that says only "Inconel bolt", check the alloy number (625, 718, etc.) and the heat treatment condition.
For 718 for oil and gas equipment, confirm the process and microstructure control requirements of API 6A718 against the specification.
Check that the certificate has the solution treatment and aging conditions and the hardness.

mat-duplex.sum: 2-phase austenitic-ferritic stainless steel. Bolting is specified by ASTM A1082 (high-strength precipitation-hardening and duplex stainless steel bolting).
facts: 2205 (UNS S31803, S32205): about 22Cr-5Ni-3Mo-N - corresponds to EN 1.4462 (X2CrNiMoN22-5-3) and JIS SUS329J3L.
Super duplex 2507 (UNS S32750): about 25Cr-7Ni-4Mo-N - corresponds to EN 1.4410 (X2CrNiMoN25-7-4) and JIS SUS327L.
Bolting standard: ASTM A1082/A1082M (high-strength precipitation-hardening and duplex stainless steel bolting).
Correspondence (JSSA table, not a guarantee of equivalence): S31803, S32205 <-> EN 1.4462 · SUS329J3L, S32750 <-> EN 1.4410 · SUS327L.
watch: In subsea cathodic protection zones, there is a risk of hydrogen-induced stress cracking (HISC) of duplex - check design guidelines such as DNV-RP-F112 and the specification.
Do not mix carbon steel nuts and washers with duplex bolts (galvanic and reduced corrosion resistance).
When using in high-temperature equipment, check the temperature upper limit of the applicable code.

mat-monel.sum: Ni-Cu alloys. Alloy 400 (UNS N04400) is the subject of ASTM B164, and the age-hardening K-500 (UNS N05500) of ASTM B865 bar and forgings. Monel is a trademark.
facts: Alloy 400 (N04400): subject of ASTM B164, the Ni-Cu alloy rod and bar standard (B164 also includes N04405).
Alloy K-500 (N05500): Ni-Cu-Al precipitation-hardening alloy - subject of ASTM B865 (bar and forgings).
Monel (trademark) is a trade name - order to the standard by alloy number and UNS (N04400, N05500).
watch: Where it contacts carbon steel or aluminum, the mating metal suffers galvanic corrosion - use nuts and washers of the same family.
400 (solid solution strengthened) and K-500 (precipitation hardened) have different heat treatment and strength systems, so write the alloy number exactly in the BOM.

iso-898-1.sum: Basic standard that defines bolt property classes such as 8.8, 10.9, and 12.9. It specifies the tensile strength, yield, hardness, and proof load of carbon steel and alloy steel externally threaded fasteners on the basis of room-temperature (10–35 °C) testing.
facts: Scope: coarse thread M1.6–M39, fine thread M8×1–M39×3. Set screws that do not carry tension are covered separately by ISO 898-5.
Property classes: 4.6, 4.8, 5.6, 5.8, 6.8, 8.8, 9.8, 10.9, 12.9. 9.8 exists only for d ≤ 16 mm.
First number × 100 = nominal tensile strength (MPa), second number × 0.1 = nominal yield ratio. Multiplying the two gives the nominal yield strength (8.8 → 800 × 0.8 = 640 MPa).

Acceptance is judged not by the nominal value but by the minimum value in the table. 10.9 is nominally 1000 but has a minimum tensile strength of 1040 MPa, and 12.9 is nominally 1200 with a minimum of 1220 MPa.
8.8, 9.8, 10.9, and 12.9 must be quenched and tempered, and a lower limit of tempering temperature is set (mostly 425 °C).
Bolts whose load capacity is reduced by the head shape (countersunk, low head, etc.) have a 0 placed before the property class (08.8, 010.9).

Standard note: it assumes use from -50 °C to +150 °C, and use outside it (up to +300 °C) is subject to expert review. For low-temperature and high-temperature materials, it points to EN 10269, ASTM A320, and so on.

Drawing designations are split into ISO 898-1, EN ISO 898-1 (European adoption), DIN EN ISO 898-1 (German adoption), and KS B ISO 898-1 (Korean identical adoption), but the editions adopted may differ from each other.
watch: KS B ISO 898-1 is the edition identical (IDT) to ISO 898-1:1999 (as shown on the KS portal). The KS designation on Korean drawings and the current ISO edition may differ in test items and designations, so confirm the edition used as the basis for judging certificates.
The minimum value of 8.8 splits at a diameter of 16 mm (d ≤ 16: tensile 800 MPa, d > 16: 830 MPa). M16 is judged by the d ≤ 16 value.
A property class is a designation for metric fasteners. Do not write it interchangeably with ASTM and SAE grades such as B7 and Grade 5 (the correspondence is approximate).
For low temperatures below -50 °C and flange bolting above 150 °C, specify ASTM A320 (low temperature) or A193 (high temperature) or EN 10269 materials instead of a property class.
The 010.9 marking on countersunk and low-head bolts means a lower load capacity. Do not expect the load of a 10.9 hex bolt of the same diameter.
eq_notes: Identical (IDT) to ISO 898-1:1999 - an older edition than the current ISO edition
Inch bolt grade system - do not write interchangeably with a property class

iso-898-2.sum: Standard that defines nut property classes (04, 05, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12), nut types (styles 0, 1, 2) and pairing with bolts. Coarse thread M5–M39, fine thread M8×1–M39×3.
facts: Property classes: regular and high nuts 5, 6, 8, 10, 12 / thin nuts 04, 05. In the current edition, class 9 and fine-thread class 5 were deleted (replaced by 10 and 6, respectively).
For regular and high nuts, the number is the first number of the highest bolt property class the nut can be paired with. A class 10 nut is used up to 10.9 bolts.
A nut of a higher property class can replace one of a lower class. However, prevailing torque (locking) nuts are paired only with bolts of the same property class.
The design principle is that, with matching property classes, nut height and strength are set so that the bolt breaks before the nut threads strip under overload.
The leading 0 of a thin nut is a warning that it is not designed to prevent thread stripping under overload. When used as a jam nut, it is used together with a regular or high nut.
Service temperature is assumed to be −50 °C to +150 °C, and up to +300 °C is used in certain applications. Hot-dip galvanized nuts follow the additional requirements of ISO 10684.
ISO 898-6, which covered fine-thread nuts, was merged into this standard in the 2012 edition.
watch: KS B ISO 898-2 is the identical (IDT) edition of ISO 898-2:1992 and covers coarse thread only (KS portal). The 1992 edition has classes 4 and 9 that are not in the current edition, so check which edition the certificate acceptance criteria are based on.
For a line without a nut property class ("M16 nut"), determine it from the mating bolt class (8.8 → 8, 10.9 → 10, 12.9 → 12).
Inch nut grades (A563 DH, A194 2H) and ISO nut property classes are different systems. A metric B7 stud with an ISO 4032 class 8 nut is not regarded as the same as an A194 2H combination.
If the specification calls for style 2 (ISO 4033), do not substitute style 1 (ISO 4032).
eq_notes: Identical (IDT) to ISO 898-2:1992, coarse thread only
Fine-thread nuts — merged into ISO 898-2 in the 2012 edition

iso-3506-1.sum: Standard that designates stainless steel bolts by "steel grade–property class", as in A2-70 and A4-80. It sets properties for austenitic, martensitic, ferritic and duplex steel grades.
facts: The designation has two blocks separated by a hyphen. The first is the steel grade (A austenitic, C martensitic, F ferritic, D duplex + composition number), and the second is the property class (minimum tensile strength ÷ 10).
For low-carbon austenitic steel with carbon of 0.030 % or less, L may be added after the steel grade (example: A4L-80).
Scope: coarse thread M1.6–M39, fine thread M8×1–M39×3, tested at room temperature (10–35 °C).
The current edition added duplex steel grades (D), austenitic property class 100 and steel grade A8.

Standard note: −20 °C to +150 °C can be used without restriction, and −196 °C to +300 °C is also used but is left to the user's judgment. For high-temperature use see ISO 3506-5; for general rules on selecting steel grades see ISO 3506-6.
Austenitic, ferritic and duplex fasteners get their strength from cold working. Unlike quenched and tempered bolts, properties are not uniform across the part.
A bolt with low load capacity because of its head or shank shape has 0 placed before the property class.
watch: The domestic KS B 0241 is the identical (IDT) edition of ISO 3506-1, -2 and -3:1997 (KS portal). It does not have content of the current edition such as duplex and property class 100.
SUS304 = A2 and SUS316 = A4 are commonly matched, but A2 and A4 are names that group several steel grades. If a specific steel grade such as 316L is needed, state it separately.
For a line that has only "A2" without a property class, ask again for the strength (50, 70, 80).
Galling (seizing) occurs easily when stainless bolts and nuts of the same stainless steel are tightened together. Consider an anti-seize compound or tightening speed.
eq_notes: Identical (IDT) to ISO 3506-1, -2 and -3:1997 — old edition
High-temperature, high-pressure plant bolting — not regarded as the same standard

iso-3506-2.sum: Standard that designates stainless steel nuts by steel grade and property class, as in "A2-70". It separately defines regular and high nuts and thin nuts, which have a 0 placed before the class.
facts: Steel grade symbols are the same as in ISO 3506-1 (A·C·F·D + number). The property class number is 1/10 of the proof stress in MPa (70 → 700 MPa).
A thin nut (style 0) has 0 placed before the property class to show that its load capacity is low (example: A2-035).
The current edition added duplex steel grades, property class 100, steel grade A8, the design of bolt–nut combinations and nut design principles.
Product standard example: ISO 4032 and 4033 provide A2-70, A4-70 and A4-80 up to M24, and A2-50, A2-70, A4-50 and A4-70 above M24 up to M39.
watch: For a BOM with mixed steel grades and classes, such as an A2-70 nut on an A4-80 bolt, check whether it is intended.
Do not use a thin nut (A2-035, etc.) where it carries bolt load.
Stainless nuts and bolts gall easily. Consider an anti-seize compound.
A4-80 nuts above M24 are not in the product standards ISO 4032 and 4033. For large diameters, confirm 70 or 50.
eq_notes: Identical (IDT) to ISO 3506-2:1997, etc. — old edition

iso-4014.sum: Dimensional standard for hexagon bolts with a plain cylindrical part on part of the shank (partially threaded). Coarse thread M1.6–M64, product grades A and B. It replaced DIN 931.
facts: Steel and stainless steel, coarse thread M1.6–M64. Select strength from ISO 898-1, and for stainless steel from ISO 3506-1. Thread tolerance 6g.
Product grade A applies to M24 or smaller with length of 10d or 150 mm or less (whichever is shorter); everything else has grade B tolerance (ISO 4759-1).
Thread length b: 2d+6 for nominal length of 125 mm or less, 2d+12 for over 125 up to 200, and 2d+25 for over 200.

The shortest standard length in the current edition is the diameter multiple (M5–M8 5d, M10 4.5d, M12–M22 4d, M24–M60 3.75d) rounded to the nearest standard length, and the longest is 10d or 500 mm, whichever is shorter (example: for M14, 4d = 56 → 55 mm).

Changes in the current edition: property classes 4.8 and 12.9 added, 9.8 deleted, stainless D4, D6 and class 80 added, M7 added, rules for shortest and longest standard length and a marking clause newly added.
The domestic KS B 1002 (hexagon bolts) is a standard modified (MOD) from ISO 4014, 4016, 4017, 4018 (1999 edition), etc. (KS portal).
watch: When changing a line marked DIN 931 to an ISO 4014 product, compare dimensions such as width across flats and do not change them arbitrarily.
If shorter than the standard shortest length, no cylindrical part remains and the bolt becomes fully threaded (ISO 4017) (example: M12 under 50 mm).
For joints loaded in shear, select the length so that the cylindrical part sits across the joint plane. Keep the threaded portion off the shear plane.
For hot-dip galvanized partially threaded bolts, use oversize-tapped nuts of the same system as a set.
eq_notes: Replaced by DIN EN ISO 4014 via DIN EN 24014 (1992)
Inch hex bolt — different thread system

iso-4017.sum: Dimensional standard for hexagon bolts threaded up to the head (fully threaded). Coarse thread M1.6–M64, product grades A and B. It replaced DIN 933.
facts: Steel and stainless steel, coarse thread M1.6–M64, thread tolerance 6g. The product grade split is the same as in ISO 4014.
Standard length: the shortest is about 2d rounded to the nearest standard length, and the longest is 10d or 200 mm, whichever is shorter (current edition rule).

Changes in the current edition: 4.8 and 12.9 added, 9.8 deleted, stainless D4, D6 and class 80 added, M7 added, the longest standard length that was missing from the previous edition restored, marking clause newly added.
Drawing designation example: ISO 4017 - M12 × 50 - 8.8. The same content is also written as EN ISO 4017 (Europe) and DIN EN ISO 4017 (Germany).

Domestic standards are KS B ISO 4017 (hexagon head screws — product grades A and B) and KS B 1002 (hexagon bolts), which is modified (MOD) from ISO 4017:1999, etc. (KS portal). The lists of lengths and property classes may differ from the current ISO edition.
watch: When changing a line marked DIN 933 to ISO 4017, compare dimensions such as width across flats. For a line with a width across flats stated, purchase based on that width across flats.
Fully threaded bolts over 200 mm are outside the standard range. Consider partially threaded bolts (ISO 4014) or an agreed length.
Even for M16–M24, product grade B tolerance applies if the length exceeds 150 mm or 10d.
For electro-galvanized or black zinc plated products of 10.9 and above, check by certificate whether hydrogen embrittlement measures (baking, process validation) were applied.
eq_notes: Replaced by DIN EN ISO 4017 via DIN EN 24017 (1992)
Domestically adopted standard — check the adopted edition against the original KS standard
Domestic hexagon bolt standard (modified (MOD) from ISO 4017:1999, etc.)
Inch hex cap screw — different thread system

iso-4016-4018.sum: Hexagon bolts of product grade C, which has wide tolerances. ISO 4016 is partially threaded and ISO 4018 is fully threaded, with coarse thread M5–M64.
facts: ISO 4016 = partially threaded, ISO 4018 = fully threaded. Both are coarse thread M5–M64, product grade C.
Product grade C has the widest tolerances of ISO 4759-1. The external thread tolerance is 8g, and 6g for property class 8.8 and above (grades A and B are 6g).
The basic combination of mating parts is the grade C nut ISO 4034 and the grade C plain washer ISO 7091 (100HV).

Select the property class from ISO 898-1. The ISO 7091 (100HV) washer is stated for grade C bolts of 6.8 or below, and ISO 898-3 recommends 100HV for 5.8 or below and treats 6.8 as conditional on joint verification.
Changes in the current edition of ISO 4016: M7 added, allowed range of head shape added, rules for shortest and longest standard length and a marking clause newly added.
The domestic KS B ISO 4034 (hexagon nuts — product grade C) is the identical edition of ISO 4034:1999 (as shown on the KS portal).
watch: Grade C has wide head and shank dimensional tolerances, so it is not used for precision fits such as reamed holes or for machine assembly.
For a line with only "ISO 4016" and no property class, ask again for the strength.
For a line marked DIN 601 or 558, compare dimensions with the ISO product.
eq_notes: Grade C partially threaded bolt (replaced by ISO 4016 via DIN EN 24016)
Grade C fully threaded bolt (replaced by ISO 4018 via DIN EN 24018)
Included in the domestic hexagon bolt standard (modified)

iso-4032.sum: Dimensional standard for the most common metric hexagon nut (style 1). The current edition sets property classes for M5–M39, and the nut is taller than DIN 934 so that it can fully take the bolt strength.
facts: Current edition range M5–M39 (sizes below M5 and above M39 moved to an informative annex). Thread tolerance 6H, product grade A for M16 and below and B above.
Steel nut property classes: M5–M16 5, 6, 8, 10, 12; above M16 up to M39 5, 6, 8, 10. Classes 10 and 12 must be quenched and tempered.
Changes in the current edition: property classes 5 and 12 added, stainless D4, D6 and class 80 added, M7 added, non-ferrous nuts deleted, marking clause newly added.
The domestic KS B 1012 (hexagon nuts and hexagon thin nuts) is a standard modified (MOD) from ISO 4032:1999 (KS portal).
Fine-thread hexagon nuts are ISO 8673, high nuts are ISO 4033 and thin nuts are ISO 4035.
watch: When changing a line marked DIN 934 to ISO 4032, compare height (ISO 4032 is taller) and width across flats.
For a "hexagon nut" without a property class, determine it from the mating bolt strength (8.8 ↔ 8, 10.9 ↔ 10).
Style 1 of class 12 exists only up to M16. The mating nut for a 12.9 bolt larger than M16 is ISO 4033 (style 2) class 12.
Hot-dip galvanized nuts are tapped oversize after plating (6AZ, 6AX), so use them only as a set with plated bolts of the same system.
For M3, M4 and M42 and above, the current edition gives reference dimensions without property classes. Strength is agreed at the time of order.
eq_notes: Replaced by DIN EN ISO 4032 via DIN EN 24032 (1992), height differs
Inch hex nut — different thread system

head: Nominal size
Width across flats s
Height m max
table.note: Values from ISO 4032:2023 Tables 1 and 2.

iso-4033.sum: Hexagon nut taller than style 1 (minimum height 0.89D or more). Property classes 8, 10, 12, coarse thread M5–M39. Required as the mating nut for 12.9 bolts larger than M16.
facts: Coarse thread M5–M39, thread tolerance 6H, product grade A for M16 and below and B above. Width across flats is the same as ISO 4032 and only the height is greater.
Steel nut property classes 8, 10, 12 (M5–M39). Quenching and tempering is mandatory for 10 and 12, and at the manufacturer's option for 8.
The composition of stainless steel grades and property classes is the same as ISO 4032 (up to M24 A2-70, A4-70, A4-80, etc.).
Changes in the current edition: M7, M18, M22, M27, M33 and M39 added, property class 9 deleted, stainless nuts added, marking clause newly added.
A class 12 nut exists in style 1 (ISO 4032) only up to M16, so style 2 is needed for larger 12.9 bolts.
The domestic KS B ISO 4033 is the identical (IDT) edition of ISO 4033:1999, and its scope is M5–M36 (KS portal).
watch: If the specification calls for ISO 4033, do not change it to ISO 4032 (height difference).
Because the nut is taller, the bolt protrusion becomes shorter. Check the bolt length again.
Nuts of structural high-strength bolt sets (EN 14399, KS B 1010) are covered by separate standards. Do not replace them with ISO 4033.

iso-4035.sum: Hexagon thin nut with a height of about 0.5d (style 0, chamfered type). Because its load capacity is low, the property classes are 04 and 05, and it is used for double-nut locking and position locking.
facts: A style 0 nut with a minimum height of 0.45D or more and less than 0.80D (ISO 898-2).
Steel nut property classes 04 and 05; stainless steel uses property classes with a 0 added, such as A2-035.
Thin nuts are not designed to prevent thread stripping under overload (standard warning).
When used as a jam nut, 04 is used together with a regular or high nut of class 8 or below, and 05 with one of class 12 or below (ISO 898-2).
The thin nut without chamfer is ISO 4036 (product grade B). DIN 439-2 was replaced by DIN EN ISO 4035, and DIN 439-1 by ISO 4036.
The domestic KS B ISO 4035 is the identical (IDT) edition of ISO 4035:1999 (KS portal).
watch: Do not use a thin nut alone where it carries bolt load. Use a regular nut (ISO 4032).
For a line with only "jam nut", sort it out by thread (metric, UNC) and grade (whether it is an A194 heavy jam nut).

iso-4762.sum: Dimensional standard for socket head cap screws (wrench bolts), with a cylindrical head and a hexagon socket. Coarse thread M1.6–M64, product grade A. It replaced DIN 912.
facts: Coarse thread M1.6–M64, product grade A. Property classes are 8.8, 10.9 and 12.9, and A2 and A4 for stainless steel (1997 edition requirement table).
Thread tolerance: 5g6g for 12.9 and 6g for the other property classes (1997 edition requirement table).
Head height k (maximum) equals d, and head diameter dk is about 1.5 to 1.75 times d (table).
Length L is measured from the underside of the head to the end.
The corresponding international standard of the domestic KS B 1003 (hexagon socket head bolts) is the old edition ISO 4762:1997 (KS portal).
watch: For electro-galvanizing of 12.9 socket head cap screws, the current edition of ISO 4042 is a combination that requires both process validation and baking. Consider black oxide (+ rust-preventive oil) or zinc flake first.
Inch BOMs that list "cap screw" (ASTM A574) have a different thread system and are not interchangeable.
Check the counterbore depth by adding the washer thickness to the head height k (= d).
For 10.9, a 300HV washer fits; for 12.9, the 380HV washer recommended by ISO 898-3 fits, but 380HV is not in the product standard and needs to be agreed.
eq_notes: Inch socket head cap screw — different thread system

head: Nominal size
Head diameter dk
Head height k
Hexagon socket s
table.note: ISO 4762:2004 Table 1. dk is the maximum for a smooth head (a knurled head is slightly larger).

iso-10642.sum: Bolt with a 90° countersunk head and a hexagon socket. Because of the head shape its load capacity is low, so 0 is placed before the property class (010.9). It replaced DIN 7991.
facts: The standard title itself is "reduced load capacity" (from the 2019 edition). Strength is shown with a 0 added, such as 08.8, 010.9 and 012.9 (ISO 898-1 rule).
Product grade A, countersink angle 90°. Length is measured from the top of the head to the end (overall length).
From the 2019 edition, the thread length of partially threaded M14–M20 increased to 3d.
The domestic KS B ISO 10642 is the identical (IDT) edition of the old ISO 10642:1997, and its scope is M2–M20 (KS portal).
watch: Do not calculate 010.9 with the same load as a 10.9 hexagon bolt.
Do not mix with inch countersunk head socket head cap screws (ASME B18.3). Check that the bearing face angle matches.
The length measuring reference differs from ordinary socket head cap screws (from underside of head). Check which reference the BOM length uses.
If it has to fit an existing countersink, state in the order whether it is DIN 7991 dimensions or ISO dimensions.
eq_notes: Inch countersunk head socket head cap screw — not compatible

iso-7380.sum: Socket head cap screw with a low, round head and a hexagon socket. ISO 7380-1 is coarse thread M3–M16, product grade A. Head load capacity is limited to 80 % of the threaded portion.
facts: ISO 7380-1 is the button head, and ISO 7380-2 is the button head with flange (collar).
ISO 7380-1 current edition: steel and stainless steel, coarse thread M3–M16, product grade A.
Load capacity on the head side is taken as 80 % of the threaded portion, and 0 is placed before the property class (example: 010.9).
The hexagon socket is smaller than on an ordinary socket head cap screw of the same diameter (M8: socket head cap screw 6 mm, button head 5 mm).
The domestic KS B 1067 (hexagon socket button head bolts) is the identical (IDT) edition of the old ISO 7380:1983 (KS portal).
watch: Where a large clamping force is needed, check with the designer whether to use an ordinary socket head cap screw (ISO 4762) instead of a button head.
"Round head bolt" sometimes means a machine screw without a socket (pan head), so distinguish them.
The thread length of the M16 partially threaded bolt was increased in the current edition (48 mm, 3d).

iso-4026-4029.sum: Dimensional standards for 4 types of headless hexagon socket set screws. Only the end shape differs (4026 flat, 4027 cone, 4028 dog, 4029 cup). Not for tensile loads.
facts: Strength is shown by hardness class, not tensile strength: 45H, etc. for steel (ISO 898-5), and the hardness classes of ISO 3506-3 for stainless steel.
Fasteners that do not carry tension, such as set screws, are not covered by ISO 898-1 (separated into ISO 898-5).

The cup end bites into the shaft and is the most commonly used, the flat end causes less damage to the shaft, the cone end locates in a seat hole in the shaft, and the dog end fits into a groove or hole in the shaft to prevent sliding.
ISO 4042 exempts set screws that do not carry tension from baking after electroplating.
watch: For a line without the end shape, ask again.
The dog end has a longer minimum length than the cup and flat ends.
Do not mix with inch set screws (ASME B18.3, ASTM F912).
State the plating specification (electro-galvanized, black oxide, stainless steel, etc.) in the order.

iso-7089-7090.sum: Dimensional standard for the most common metric plain washers. ISO 7089 is flat, and ISO 7090 has a chamfered outer edge. Select the 200HV or 300HV hardness class to suit the bolt strength.
facts: The nominal size is the diameter of the screw it fits (for M12 = 12). Up to M36, the hole diameter d1 is the same as the fine series hole of ISO 273.
The chamfered ISO 7090 exists only for M5 and above.
Hardness class 200HV (200–300 HV) suits up to 8.8 bolts and class 8 nuts, and 300HV (300–370 HV, quenched and tempered) suits up to 10.9 bolts and class 10 nuts (scope of ISO 7089, ISO 898-3).
DIN 125-1 was replaced by DIN EN ISO 7089 and 7090.
Designation example: ISO 7089 - 12 - 200 HV (nominal size 12, hardness class 200HV). Stainless steel is designated by a steel grade such as A2 or A4.
watch: Specify 300HV for 10.9 bolts. Using a 200HV washer with 10.9 is a conditional combination in ISO 898-3 that requires joint design verification.
The current edition of ISO 4042 does not require baking for electroplated 300HV washers, but for uses where the washer bends, such as slotted or oversize holes, have the buyer specify baking.
Do not assume that a washer marked KS B 1326 has the same dimensions as ISO 7089. If the outside diameter matters, state the ISO standard as well.
For soft materials (aluminum, wood) or slotted holes, consider the large washer (ISO 7093-1).
eq_notes: Domestically adopted standard (plain washers — normal series — product grade A)
Domestic plain washer standard (no corresponding ISO shown on the KS portal)
Inch plain washers (merged from former B18.22.1) · hardened washers — different system

head: Nominal size
Hole diameter d1
Outside diameter d2
Thickness h
table.note: Nominal values of ISO 7089:2000 Table 1.

iso-7091-7093.sum: ISO 7091 is the grade C plain washer with wide tolerances (100HV), and ISO 7093 is the large washer with an outside diameter about 3 times the bolt diameter (-1 grade A, -2 grade C).
facts: ISO 7091 is the plain washer paired with grade C bolts (ISO 4016, 4018), with hardness class 100HV, and is stated for bolts of 6.8 or below and nuts of class 6 or below.
ISO 898-3 recommends 100HV washers for 4.6–5.8 bolts (class 5 nuts) and says not to use them with bolts of 8.8 and above.
ISO 7093-1 (grade A) is 200HV and 300HV, and ISO 7093-2 (grade C) is 100HV.
Large washer outside diameter examples: M10 30, M12 37, M16 50 mm.
DIN 9021 was replaced by DIN EN ISO 7093-1 and 7093-2. DIN 126 (grade C washer) was withdrawn, and ISO 7091 corresponds to the same use.
watch: In a line written "M16×50×3", 50 is the outside diameter and 3 is the thickness.
A large washer can bend over a large hole, so check the thickness.
Inch fender washers (example: 3/8 × 1-1/2) are not this standard.
Do not use 100HV washers with bolts of 8.8 and above.
eq_notes: Withdrawn — corresponds to ISO 7091 (no replacement standard shown in DIN Media)

iso-8734.sum: Hardened parallel pin for locating two parts. Diameter 1–20 mm, diameter tolerance m6. Type A is through-hardened, type B is case-hardened, and there is a martensitic stainless steel (C1).
facts: Nominal diameter 1–20 mm, diameter tolerance m6, so it is press-fitted into the hole. The hole tolerance follows the design drawing.
Type A is through-hardened (quenched and tempered), and type B is case-hardened. Stainless steel is martensitic C1.
It is the successor standard of DIN 6325 (DIN Media: DIN 6325 → DIN EN 28734 = ISO 8734:1986).
The bolt takes the clamping force, and the pin only locates.
watch: A pin in a blind hole cannot be pulled out. If disassembly is needed, choose a parallel pin with internal thread (ISO 8735).
Hardened pins have a hydrogen embrittlement risk when electroplated, so the default is untreated (rust-preventive oil).
Austenitic stainless steel parallel pins belong to the non-hardened parallel pin (ISO 2338, A1).
For a line without the type (type A, type B), ask again.

iso-2338.sum: Parallel pin made of non-hardened steel (St) and austenitic stainless steel (A1). Diameter 0.6–50 mm, diameter tolerance m6 or h8.
facts: Nominal diameter 0.6–50 mm. The diameter tolerance is chosen between m6 (press fit) and h8 (looser side).
The materials are non-hardened steel St and austenitic stainless steel A1.
It replaced DIN 7 (DIN EN ISO 2338).
Its hardness is lower than the hardened dowel pin (ISO 8734) (steel St 125–245 HV30).
watch: For a line without the tolerance (m6, h8), ask again.
A 304 (A2) pin is not a standard material but an agreed material.
For locating under large loads, use the hardened dowel pin (ISO 8734).
For coated products (black oxide, zinc, phosphate), the tolerance is the dimension before coating.

iso-8752.sum: Elastic slotted pin made by rolling sheet (heavy duty). The nominal size is the hole diameter to be fitted, and the hole tolerance is H12. It replaced DIN 1481.
facts: Nominal size = hole diameter (from 1 mm). The pin outside diameter is slightly larger than the nominal size, so it is held in the hole by elasticity.
The hole is drilled to the nominal diameter with tolerance H12.
Heavy duty is ISO 8752 (formerly DIN 1481), and light duty is ISO 13337 (formerly DIN 7346). Light duty has a thinner wall and a smaller minimum double shear load.
Materials: steel (quenched and tempered), martensitic and austenitic stainless steel. A minimum double shear load is specified for each nominal size, and there are no load values for austenitic.
watch: Spring pins are by default not plated because of the hydrogen embrittlement risk. If corrosion is a concern, choose stainless steel.
For a line with only "spring pin", check whether it is heavy duty (ISO 8752) or light duty (ISO 13337).
It is a different item from coiled spring pins (ISO 8750, etc.).

iso-1234.sum: Split pin whose legs are spread after insertion in a hole to prevent it from coming out. The nominal size is not the pin diameter but the hole diameter to be fitted (0.6–20 mm).
facts: Nominal size = hole diameter 0.6–20 mm. The actual pin diameter is slightly smaller than the nominal size.
Length l is from below the eye to the end of the short leg.
Materials: steel (St), austenitic stainless steel (A), brass (CuZn), etc.
The standard lists, for reference, the range of bolt and clevis pin diameters that fit each nominal size.
It replaced DIN 94 (DIN EN ISO 1234). The inch split pin is ASME B18.8.1.
watch: Do not reuse a split pin once it has been spread and straightened.
Select the nominal size that fits the bolt hole or castle nut slot, and where vibration is large consider one size larger.
The nominal size systems differ from inch split pins, so do not mix them.

iso-4162.sum: Fasteners with a circular disc (flange) under the head or nut. ISO 4162 is the small series flange bolt M5–M16, and ISO 4161 is the style 2 flange nut M5–M20.
facts: ISO 4162: small series flange bolt, coarse thread M5–M16, product grade A (grade B only for the drive part). KS B ISO 4162 is the identical (IDT) edition of ISO 4162:1990 and covers property classes 8.8–10.9 and A2-70 (KS portal).
ISO 4161: hexagon nut with flange, style 2, coarse thread M5–M20, grade A for M16 and below and B above. KS B ISO 4161 is the identical (IDT) edition of ISO 4161:1999 (KS portal).
The width across flats of the ISO 4162 (small series) M8 bolt is 10 mm, smaller than the ordinary hexagon bolt (13 mm) (ISO 272).
The width across flats of the ISO 4161 M10 flange nut is 15 mm, which differs from the regular hexagon nut (16 mm).
DIN 6921 bolts were replaced by the heavy series EN 1665, and DIN 6923 nuts by EN 1661 (ISO/DIS 4161 modified).
watch: Check whether "FLANGE BOLT" in an English BOM means a stud for a pipe flange. If a grade or NUTS is written, treat it as a stud.
For a line that does not state whether serrations are wanted, ask again. Avoid serrations on painted surfaces, thin plates and hardened washers.
When exchanging small series (ISO 4162) and heavy series (EN 1665) bolts, compare the width across flats.

iso-7040-10511.sum: Nut in which a nylon ring is pressed onto the bolt thread to give prevailing torque. ISO 7040 is the regular type and ISO 10511 is the thin type. Prevailing torque performance is in ISO 2320.
facts: The current edition of ISO 7040 extended the range to M39 and added stainless steel nuts. In the 2012 edition, ISO 7040 was M3–M36, classes 5, 8, 10, and ISO 10511 was M3–M36, classes 04, 05.

ISO 7040 has the ISO 4032 (style 1) height and ISO 10511 has the ISO 4035 (style 0) height, with the prevailing torque part added. In the current edition the height of the prevailing torque part is made the same for regular, high and thin types.
ISO 10511 (thin type) has low load capacity and does not guarantee resistance to thread stripping.
Prevailing torque nuts are paired only with bolts of the same property class (an exception to the "replace with a higher strength nut" rule of ISO 898-2).
DIN 985 was replaced by DIN EN ISO 10511, and DIN 982 by DIN EN ISO 7040. For ISO 10511 (2012 edition) M10, the width across flats is 16 mm and the maximum height is 8.56 mm.
watch: For a "nylon nut" line without the type (regular type, thin type), ask again.
Prevailing torque arises only when the bolt end passes completely through the nylon ring.
The nylon ring is weak at high temperature. For high-temperature locations, consider all-metal prevailing torque nuts.
The prevailing torque of a disassembled nylon nut decreases, so replacing it with a new one is recommended.
When changing a line marked DIN 985 or 982 to an ISO product, compare height and width across flats. Purchase based on the standard stated.
eq_notes: Domestic non-metallic insert prevailing torque nut

iso-68-1.sum: Standard that defines the basic profile of the metric thread (thread angle 60°) and the basic relationships between diameters. Diameter and pitch combinations are covered by ISO 261, and tolerances by ISO 965.
facts: Thread angle 60°, fundamental triangle height H = 0.866025P (√3/2 × P).
The basic thread height (engagement height) is 5H/8 = 0.541266P.
Pitch diameter d2 = d − 0.649519P, basic minor diameter d1 = d − 1.082532P.
In the basic profile, the flat width on the major diameter side is P/8 and on the minor diameter side is P/4.
d3 = d1 − H/6, used in the stress area As = π/4 × ((d2 + d3)/2)² of ISO 898-1, is a different value from d1 of the basic profile.
Unified inch threads also use the same 60° basic profile (ISO 68-2), but the diameter and pitch series differ and they do not fit each other.
watch: Even at 60°, metric and UNC·UNF have different pitches and do not assemble. Do not mix similar diameters such as 1/2" (12.7 mm) and M12.
Pipe parallel threads (G, ISO 228-1) have a flank angle of 55° and differ from metric threads.

iso-261.sum: ISO 261 covers all combinations of diameter and pitch of metric threads (1st, 2nd and 3rd choice diameters, coarse and fine pitches), and ISO 262 is the selection of those combinations for bolts and nuts.
facts: Each diameter has 1 coarse pitch and several fine pitches. The coarse pitch is omitted in the designation (M12) and the fine pitch is written (M12×1.5).
Diameters are divided into 1st (preferred), 2nd and 3rd choice. 2nd choice sizes such as M14, M18, M22, M27 and M33 are shown in parentheses (non-preferred) in product standards.
The fine threads for which ISO 898-1 and 898-2 define mechanical properties run from M8×1 to M39×3.
The metric coarse and fine thread standards of KS and JIS also use the same diameter and pitch series.
watch: A metric designation without a pitch is taken as coarse thread. For fine threads (M20×1.5, etc.), the nut also needs the same pitch.

head: Nominal size
Coarse pitch
Fine pitch (ISO 262)
table.note: Fine pitches from ISO 262:2023 Table 1. The fine threads for which ISO 898-1 and 898-2 define properties are a subset of these (example: M20 only ×1.5). ISO 261 also has other pitches (example: M6×0.75).

iso-965.sum: Standard that defines the tolerance grade (number) and tolerance position (letter) of metric threads. General bolts and nuts use 6g/6H, and hot-dip galvanizing uses special positions such as 6AZ, 6AX and 6az.
facts: The tolerance position is written with a lowercase letter for external threads (example: g, h) and an uppercase letter for internal threads (G, H). The number is the tolerance grade; the smaller it is, the tighter.
The tolerance grade (number) and tolerance position (letter) are written together, as 6g and 6H, and when the tolerances for pitch diameter and crest diameter differ, two are written, as 5g6g.
Tolerance quality (fine, medium, coarse) and length of engagement (S, N, L) are combined. Product standards for general bolts and nuts normally use medium quality 6g/6H.

Part 4 covers hot-dip galvanized external threads (fitted with H and G nuts after plating), and Part 5 covers the limits of dimensions of oversize-tapped internal threads that fit external threads at the h position before plating.
watch: The plating or coating thickness must fit within the allowance (fundamental deviation) of the thread tolerance. A thick plating may prevent the nut from going on (ISO 4042, 10683).
A hot-dip galvanized bolt (plated as 6g) and an ordinary 6H nut do not fit. Match the system of oversize-tapped nuts (marked Z, X) or undersize bolts (marked U).
Using an oversize-tapped nut marked Z or X together with an undersize bolt marked U carries a high risk of thread stripping (ISO 10684).
Metric tolerances (6g/6H) and inch classes (2A/2B) are different systems.

iso-4759.sum: Standard that groups the dimensional tolerances of bolts and nuts into product grades A (tightest), B and C (widest). When a product standard specifies a grade, these tolerances apply.
facts: Thread tolerance: external thread 6g for grades A and B, and 8g for grade C (6g for property class 8.8 and above). Internal threads are set by the product standard (example: ISO 4032 6H, ISO 4034 7H).
For hexagon bolts (ISO 4014, 4017), grade A is M24 or smaller with length 10d or 150 mm or less (whichever is shorter), and everything else is B. Grade C bolts are ISO 4016 and 4018.
For hexagon nuts (ISO 4032, 4033), grade A is M16 and below and B is above.
Plain washer tolerances are set separately by ISO 4759-3 (product grades A and C).
watch: Even with the same nominal size, head and shank dimensional tolerances differ if the grade differs. For precision fit holes, check the grade.
A long hexagon bolt (over 10d or 150 mm) automatically becomes grade B, and its tolerances widen.

iso-273.sum: Standard that defines the diameters of holes through which bolts pass in 3 series: fine, medium and coarse. It covers screw diameters of 1–150 mm and remains valid after reconfirmation since its establishment.
facts: Tolerance (reference): fine H12, medium H13, coarse H14.
Up to M36, the fine series hole diameter is the same as the hole diameter of the ISO 7089 plain washer.
Fastener standards such as ISO 898-1 cite values such as test hole diameters from this standard.
watch: For a drawing without the hole series, check with the designer. Reamed bolts and fitted locations need a separate tolerance tighter than the fine series.
The bolt hole diameters of EN 1092-1 flanges are set by the flange standard. Do not substitute the ISO 273 table.
For coarse series holes, check the washer outside diameter and bearing face pressure.

head: Nominal size
Fine (H12)
Medium (H13)
Coarse (H14)
table.note: Nominal sizes common in fasteners from the ISO 273 table (a subset of the screw diameter range 1–150 mm).

iso-4042.sum: Standard that defines the requirements for electroplating of fasteners (zinc, zinc-nickel, zinc-iron, cadmium) and the measures to prevent hydrogen embrittlement. For plated fasteners it takes precedence over general plating standards.
facts: The main subjects are zinc, zinc-nickel and zinc-iron plating (+ conversion coating, sealer, topcoat, lubricant). Other platings such as tin, nickel and chromium are covered only for dimensional requirements.

Hydrogen embrittlement measures are divided by hardness: 360 HV or below no additional measure; over 360 up to 390 HV process validation and product testing or baking (manufacturer's choice); over 390 HV both process validation and baking.
Alkaline zinc-nickel (Ni 12–16 %) has a low hydrogen embrittlement risk, and baking may be omitted if there is test evidence and agreement.
For case-hardened screws (tapping screws, etc.), the measures are set by core hardness. Set screws that do not carry tension are exempt from baking.
The current edition drops the citations of ISO 2081 and ISO 19598 and is a self-contained standard for fasteners.
watch: For electroplated 10.9 and 12.9 products, check by certificate whether baking was done and the process validation records. Do not assume that baking alone completely eliminates hydrogen embrittlement.
For 12.9 socket head cap screws, consider black oxide or zinc flake (ISO 10683) first.
If a thick plating is specified, it may exceed the thread tolerance allowance and the nut may not go on.

Conversion coatings come with and without hexavalent chromium (Cr(VI)-free). The current edition was revised to reflect conversion coatings free of hexavalent chromium, so state the type at the time of order.

iso-10683.sum: Non-electrolytic coating in which zinc and aluminum flakes are applied with a binder and cured by heating. No hydrogen is generated during deposition, so it is used for 10.9 and 12.9 high-strength fasteners.
facts: It includes systems with and without hexavalent chromium, and with and without topcoat and lubricant. It applies to bolts, nuts, washers, pins, etc.
No hydrogen is generated in the deposition process, and with alkaline or solvent cleaning + mechanical cleaning as pretreatment there is no risk of internal hydrogen embrittlement.
Above 390 HV or for 12.9 and above, acid pickling must not be done. Cathodic cleaning is not permitted.
The curing temperature rises up to 320 °C depending on the system and must not exceed the tempering temperature of quenched and tempered fasteners.
Corrosion resistance is specified by the neutral salt spray test (ISO 9227) hours, with no red rust. Thickness is a reference value.
The zinc flake coating standard for inch fasteners is ASTM F3393. The zinc/aluminum coating standard ASTM F1136 was withdrawn in 2025 and replaced by F3393.
watch: Coating thickness affects thread engagement. For thick specifications, check gauges and assembly.
The friction coefficient changes depending on the coating type (with or without lubricating topcoat), so set the torque value again (ISO 16047 test).
A distributor that buys uncoated fasteners and has them coated before passing them on is treated as an "alteration distributor" (ISO 1891-4 term).
For systems containing hexavalent chromium, check whether they are subject to regulations such as RoHS.

iso-10684.sum: Standard for centrifugal hot-dip galvanizing of fasteners with coarse thread M8–M64. It covers bolts up to 10.9 and nuts up to class 12, and because of the thick zinc layer, thread allowance is created by oversize-tapped nuts or undersize bolts.
facts: Scope: coarse thread M8–M64; bolts, screws and studs up to 10.9, nuts up to class 12. Below M8 or pitch under 1.25 mm is not recommended.
The zinc layer is always thick, exceeding 40 µm, so thread allowance must be provided separately.
Nut threads are tapped after plating, and re-tapping is not permitted.
For parts of 320 HV or more, hydrogen absorption is reduced by acid, alkali and mechanical cleaning with inhibitors. For 10.9 M27 and above, high-temperature galvanizing (530–560 °C) is not done.
For oversize-tapped M8 and M10 nuts and undersize M8 and M10 bolts, the proof load is lower than the ISO 898 value and is set separately in an annex.
watch: Purchase plated bolts and plated nuts as a set made by the same method (oversize-tapped or undersize). Do not mix with black (uncoated) nuts or ordinary plated nuts.
Oversize-tapped nuts have shallow thread engagement, which reduces stripping strength. Check the nut property class.
Annex F (informative) covers the strength of hot-dip galvanized bolt–nut combinations. The property class of an oversize-tapped nut is set by this annex and the specification.
12.9 is not covered by this standard. Inch F3125 A490 is also prohibited from hot-dip galvanizing.
For the hot-dip galvanizing requirements of inch nuts (ASTM A563), check the separate standard, which is independent of the metric 6AZ and 6AX system.

iso-16228.sum: Standard that defines 4 inspection documents specific to fasteners. The numbering is similar to EN 10204 but with an F added in front, and some documents can also be issued by distributors.
facts: F2.1: declaration of compliance with the order and standard, no test values. Issued by the manufacturer or distributor.

F2.2: test report, non-specific inspection. It gives results of raw material certificates, in-process and final inspection for products made to the same standard, material and process, and may not be tests taken directly from the delivered lot (issued by the manufacturer).
F3.1: test report, specific inspection. It gives the test results of the original manufacturing lot being delivered (issued by the manufacturer or distributor).
F3.2: like F3.1 it gives the test values of that lot, and it is confirmed jointly by the supplier and the buyer's side (or an external representative).
Current fastener standards such as ISO 898-2 and ISO 3506-1 cite this standard for inspection documents.
watch: Distinguish whether a "3.1 certificate" requirement means EN 10204 3.1 (confirmed by the manufacturer's authorized inspection representative) or ISO 16228 F3.1. The issuing party and the object tested differ.
F2.1 is a declaration of compliance without test values, so it is not data for checking strength or hardness.
For a full comparison of document types, see the entry "Certificate types 2.1, 2.2, 3.1, 3.2".

iso-3269.sum: Standard that defines the sampling inspection procedure used when a buyer receives a fastener lot unless otherwise agreed, and the reference judgment procedure used in disputes.
facts: It applies to inspection lots of fasteners such as bolts, screws, studs, nuts, pins, washers and rivets.
The sample size and the acceptance (Ac) and rejection (Re) numbers are set for each characteristic.

AQL is the nonconforming rate corresponding to an acceptance probability of 95 % or more, and LQ is the nonconforming rate corresponding to an acceptance probability of 10 % or less (consumer's risk) (definitions of the 2000 edition).
The current edition introduced a staged incoming inspection starting with a small sample with acceptance number 0 (Ac = 0).
The "acceptability" clauses of product standards such as ISO 4014 and 4032 cite this standard.
watch: The manufacturer's quality assurance system (ISO 16426) and the buyer's incoming inspection (ISO 3269) are different documents.
If the incoming inspection method is not written in the contract, the procedure of this standard may become the criterion for judgment.
Destructive tests (tensile, proof load) use few samples, so first check whether the certificate lot and the delivered lot are the same.
The domestic KS B ISO 3269 is the identical (IDT) edition of ISO 3269:2000 (KS portal), so it differs from the current edition, which includes the staged (Ac = 0) procedure.

iso-16047.sum: Test method standard that measures torque and clamp force together while tightening a bolt and nut to obtain the torque coefficient K and the coefficients of friction (thread, bearing face, total).
facts: Values obtained: tightening torque T, clamp force F, torque coefficient K = T/(F·d), total friction coefficient μtot, thread friction μth, bearing face friction μb, yield and fracture torque.
ISO 898-1 and 898-2 do not specify torque and clamp force performance and only refer to this standard as the test method.
If the coating or lubrication specification changes, the clamp force at the same torque changes greatly, so it is used to check the friction range of coated fasteners.
Testing is done with the conditions of test bolt, nut, washer and test plate set in advance. If the conditions differ from actual assembly, the results cannot be carried over as they are.
watch: Torque values in tables are based on specific friction conditions. Do not use them as they are if plating or lubrication differs.
The friction coefficient μ and the torque coefficient K are different values. Check which value the data gives.
The K class of structural bolt sets is set by the preload conformity test of EN 14399-2, and its purpose differs from this test.

iso-15156.sum: Standard that defines conditions for resistance to sulfide stress cracking (SSC) of metallic materials in oil and gas production equipment containing H2S. For carbon steel and low-alloy steel, hardness of 22 HRC or below is the basic condition.
facts: 3-part structure: Part 1 general principles, Part 2 carbon steel and low-alloy steel, Part 3 corrosion-resistant alloys (CRA), etc.
NACE MR0175 and ISO 15156 are joint standards with the same content. NACE merged with SSPC in 2021 to become AMPP.
For carbon steel and low-alloy steel, hardness of 22 HRC or below is generally the basic condition.
Refinery process environments use the separate standard NACE MR0103 / ISO 17945.
watch: For a line that has B7 and 2H together with "NACE", check against the specification whether it is a grade with limited hardness.
The hardness range of ISO 898-1 8.8 (22–34 HRC) exceeds the 22 HRC limit, so it does not guarantee the hardness condition for sour-exposed bolting.
Do not confuse MR0175 (production) with MR0103 (refining).
Check the specification on whether bolting whose atmospheric exposure is blocked by insulation, burial or flange protection covers is also treated as exposed bolting.

en-10204.sum: European standard that defines the 4 inspection documents (2.1, 2.2, 3.1, 3.2) requested when ordering metal products. The "3.1 certificate" on a bolt drawing usually means this standard.
facts: 2.1 is a declaration of compliance with the order without test values, and 2.2 is a test report giving non-specific inspection results.
3.1 gives specific inspection results and is confirmed by the manufacturer's authorized inspection representative, independent of the manufacturing department.
3.2 is confirmed jointly by the manufacturer's authorized inspection representative and an inspector of the buyer's side (or an inspector designated by regulation).
3.1.B of the old edition corresponds to the current 3.1, and 3.1.A, 3.1.C and 3.2 correspond to the current 3.2 (2.3 no longer exists).
An intermediate distributor must pass on the manufacturer's document without changing it.
The classification of certificate item groups (A, B, C, D, Z) follows EN 10168. The document system specific to fasteners is ISO 16228.
watch: A "3.1" issued in a distributor's name is not EN 10204 3.1. Check whether it is confirmed by the manufacturer's authorized inspection representative.
A requirement written with the old designation "3.1.B" corresponds to the current 3.1.
Check that the heat number on the 3.1 matches the product and label.
For a detailed comparison, see the entry "Certificate types 2.1, 2.2, 3.1, 3.2".

en-14399.sum: European standard for bolt, nut and washer sets that apply preload in steel structure joints. It is divided into HR (British–French line), HV (German line) and HRC (preload-compensating type) systems.
facts: Bolt/nut property class combinations: HR is 8.8/8, 8.8/10, 10.9/10, and HV is 10.9/10, both M12–M36.

HR gets ductility from plastic elongation of the bolt, with a regular height (style 1) nut and a long threaded portion, while HV gets ductility from plastic deformation of the engaged threads, with a lower (reduced-height) nut of about 0.8d and a short threaded portion.

Torque characteristics are shown by K class (k-class): K1 range of individual k values, K2 mean value and coefficient of variation. K0, with no requirement, was a classification in the 2005 edition of EN 14399-1.
Washers are EN 14399-6 (quenched and tempered chamfered plain washer) and EN 14399-5 (plain washer, only on the nut side of HR sets).
Bolts and nuts are marked with HR or HV and the property class. EN 14399-1 is a harmonized standard linked to CE marking (Annex ZA).
DIN 6914 (bolts), 6915 (nuts) and 6916 (washers) were replaced by EN 14399-4 and -6.
watch: If bolts, nuts and washers from different lots or different manufacturers are mixed, the K class is not guaranteed.
KS B 1010 (high-strength bolt sets for friction joints) and HV sets are not the same standard. Do not substitute them without comparing dimensions.
The width across flats of an HV bolt is larger than an ordinary hexagon bolt (M20: HV 32 mm, ISO 4017 30 mm).
Do not reuse a set that has been tightened once or one that has spun freely.
For a line with only "10.9 high-strength bolt", ask again whether it is an ordinary hexagon bolt or a structural set.
eq_notes: DIN preceding standard of HV sets
Domestic high-strength bolt sets for friction joints (separate standard)
US structural bolts (A325, A490, etc., inch and metric) — separate system

head: Part
Content
rows: HR countersunk head bolts and nuts
HV hexagon fit bolts and nuts
Direct tension indicator washers (DTI) for HR and HV
HRC preload-compensating bolts and nuts (torque-shear type)

en-15048.sum: European standard for non-preloaded bolt and nut sets for steel structure joints. The "SB" type and CE marking are applied to bolts and nuts tested as a set.
facts: It consists of -1 general requirements and -2 suitability tests. Steel structures (EN 1090-2) cover M12–M39, and aluminum structures (EN 1090-3) cover M5–M39.
Steel bolt property classes are 4.6, 4.8, 5.6, 5.8, 6.8, 8.8, 10.9 of ISO 898-1, and for stainless steel 50, 70, 80 of ISO 3506.
Washers are not components of the set but are used together if necessary (2016 edition).
Bolts and nuts are marked with SB together with the property class. Only products tested as a set are subject to CE marking.
For joints that transmit load without preload, as in shear and bearing. For preloaded joints, EN 14399.
watch: Do not use SB sets in friction (preloaded) joints.
If a European steel structure specification requires SB and CE marking, purchase an SB set even for the same ISO 4017 8.8.

en-10269.sum: European material standard that defines steel grades, composition and mechanical properties of bar and wire for bolts and nuts, with properties specified at high and low temperatures. It is cited by flange bolting for pressure equipment (EN 1515).
facts: It covers bar and wire of unalloyed steel, alloy steel, stainless steel and nickel alloys.
Steel grade examples: C35E, C45E, 20Mn5 (unalloyed steel), 25CrMo4, 42CrMo4, 40CrMoV4-6, 21CrMoV5-7 (alloy steel), X8Ni9 (1.5662), 1.4980, etc.
Besides room-temperature properties, it specifies service temperature properties such as 0.2 % proof strength at high temperature and impact values at low temperature.
ISO 898-1 and 898-2 also advise referring to EN 10269, etc. for material selection outside −50 °C to +150 °C.
"+QT" after the steel grade means the quenched and tempered condition.
watch: Even for the same 42CrMo4, ISO 683-2 (formerly EN 10083-3, general quenched and tempered steel) and EN 10269 (for fasteners) certificates have different guaranteed items. For pressure equipment bolting, obtain a certificate that states EN 10269.
ASTM A193 grades and EN 10269 steel grades are separate standards, so do not write one as the same material as the other.
Do not set the upper service temperature limit by the steel grade table alone; check it against EN 1515 and the design code.
eq_notes: US high-temperature and low-temperature bolting materials — correspondence is approximate
Bolt and nut materials for high-temperature use — replaced by DIN EN 10269

en-1515.sum: Standard for the selection of bolts and nuts used in EN flanged joints and for material classification. Part 1 selection, Part 2 material classification for PN flanges, Part 3 material classification for Class flanges, Part 4 selection for equipment under the Pressure Equipment Directive.
facts: Part 1: bolting selection; Part 2: classification of bolt materials for PN steel flanges; Part 3: classification of bolt materials for Class steel flanges; Part 4: selection of bolting for equipment under the Pressure Equipment Directive (2014/68/EU).
Part 1 covers bolting materials such as EN 10269 steel grades and the property classes of ISO 898-1 and ISO 3506-1, and bolts and nuts are selected as a pair.
It is used together with EN 1092-1 (PN), the flange dimensional standard.
watch: If a PN flange bolt is written only as "8.8", there is no guarantee of properties at high or low temperature. If the design temperature is outside the room-temperature range, specify an EN 10269 steel grade.
For equipment under the Pressure Equipment Directive, check the requirements of 1515-4 and material certificates (EN 10204 3.1, etc.).
For the classification of bolt materials for Class flanges (EN 1759-1), see 1515-3.

en-1092-1.sum: European standard for steel pipe flanges whose pressure rating is shown by PN. For each DN and PN combination, the number of bolts, nominal size and bolt circle diameter are defined, and the bolts have metric threads.
facts: Facing types: A flat face, B raised face (RF), C and D tongue and groove, E and F spigot and recess, G and H O-ring groove.
It replaced the old DIN flanges (DIN 2633 weld neck PN16, DIN 2576 plate flange PN10, DIN 2527 blind, etc.).
Bolt material selection follows EN 1515.
watch: Even for the same DN, the number and diameter of bolts may differ between PN10, PN16 and PN40. Check the PN for each line.
ASME B16.5 series Class flanges are a separate system (EN 1759 in Europe) and are not interchangeable with PN flanges. Compare the bolt circle and the number of bolts.
Stud and bolt length varies with the flange type (01, 11, etc.) and gasket thickness.

pc-steel.sum: The bolt property class system of ISO 898-1. The first number × 100 is the nominal tensile strength (MPa), and the second number × 0.1 is the yield ratio.
facts: Example: 8.8 → nominal tensile 800 MPa × yield ratio 0.8 = nominal yield 640 MPa. 10.9 → 1000 × 0.9 = 900 MPa (nominal).
Judgment is made not by the nominal values but by the minimum values in the table. For 10.9 the minimum tensile is 1040 and the minimum 0.2 % proof strength is 940 MPa.
The value used for yield differs: for 4.6 and 5.6 the lower yield point (ReL), for 8.8 and above the 0.2 % proof strength (Rp0.2), and for 4.8, 5.8 and 6.8 the stress on the full-size bolt (Rpf).
8.8, 9.8, 10.9 and 12.9 must be quenched and tempered (tempering lower limit mostly 425 °C). For 4.6 to 6.8 no heat treatment condition is specified.
9.8 exists only for d ≤ 16 mm and was deleted in the current editions of ISO 4014 and 4017.
Reduced load capacity bolts have a 0 placed in front (08.8, 010.9).
Mating parts: 8.8 ↔ nut 8 · washer 200HV, 10.9 ↔ nut 10 · washer 300HV, 12.9 ↔ nut 12 · washer 380HV (to be agreed).
watch: The inch correspondences are approximate: 8.8 ≈ ASTM F3125 A325 (minimum 120 ksi), 10.9 ≈ A490 (minimum 150 ksi). Metric and inch threads do not fit each other.
10.9 and 12.9 electroplated products need hydrogen embrittlement measures (ISO 4042: for 10.9 process validation or baking, for 12.9 both process validation and baking).
For bolting outside −50 °C to +150 °C, specify by ASTM A193, A320 or EN 10269 material, not by property class.
For a line with only a material name (SCM435, etc.) and no property class, ask again for the property class. A material name does not guarantee strength.
