table.note: ISO 898-1 Table 3. The minimum Rpf values of 4.8, 5.8 and 6.8 are shown in the standard as "under investigation" (for calculation) values. The tensile values are the same as in the site's "strength comparison" table.

pc-8-8.sum: The most common high-strength metric bolt grade. Minimum tensile 800 MPa (d ≤ 16) / 830 MPa (d > 16); quenched and tempered carbon steel, boron-added steel and alloy steel.
facts: Nominal tensile 800 MPa × yield ratio 0.8 = nominal yield 640 MPa.
d ≤ 16 mm: minimum tensile 800, 0.2 % proof strength 640, proof stress 580 MPa, 250–320 HV (22–32 HRC).
d > 16 mm: minimum tensile 830, 0.2 % proof strength 660, proof stress 600 MPa, 255–335 HV (23–34 HRC).
Minimum elongation 12 %; for d ≥ 16 mm, impact at −20 °C of 27 J or more.
Material: carbon steel with boron etc. added, carbon steel, alloy steel, quenched and tempered (tempering 425 °C or higher).
Mating: nut class 8 (ISO 898-2), washer 200HV (ISO 898-3).
A grade that does not need baking when electroplated (below 10.9, ISO 4042), and it is eligible for hot-dip galvanizing (ISO 10684).
watch: 8.8 ≈ F3125 A325 (minimum 120 ksi) is an approximate correspondence. A449 is about 25 % lower than 8.8 (830 MPa) at minimum 90 ksi (about 621 MPa, converted) for 1-3/4" and above, so do not treat them as corresponding.
The judgment values differ at the 16 mm diameter boundary. M16 is judged by the d ≤ 16 values.
If class 5 or 6 nuts are used with 8.8 bolts, the nut threads may strip first.
The hardness range (22–34 HRC) exceeds the sour service limit (22 HRC or below), so it is not used for H2S-exposed bolting.
The structural HR 8.8 set (EN 14399-3) has set requirements different from an ordinary 8.8 hexagon bolt.

pc-10-9.sum: High-strength bolt grade. Minimum tensile 1040 MPa, 0.2 % proof strength 940 MPa, 320–380 HV. The mating nut is class 10 and the washer is 300HV.
facts: Nominal 1000 MPa × 0.9 = nominal yield 900 MPa (the minimum values for judgment are tensile 1040 and proof strength 940 MPa).
Proof stress 830 MPa, hardness 320–380 HV (32–39 HRC), minimum elongation 9 %.
Material: carbon steel with boron etc. added, carbon steel, alloy steel, quenched and tempered (tempering 425 °C or higher).
Mating: nut class 10 (ISO 4032, 4033), washer 300HV (300–370 HV).
Electroplating (ISO 4042): process validation and product testing or baking, at the manufacturer's choice.
Hot-dip galvanizing (ISO 10684) covers up to 10.9, but conditions apply such as no high-temperature galvanizing for M27 and above.
watch: 10.9 ≈ F3125 A490 (approximate). A490 has an upper tensile limit (173 ksi) and hot-dip galvanizing is prohibited, so do not substitute them as they are (RCSC).
For electro-zinc or black zinc 10.9, check by certificate whether baking and process validation were done.
Specify a 300HV washer instead of a 200HV mild steel washer.
If a class 8 nut is put on a 10.9 bolt, the nut threads may strip first.
The 10.9 of the structural HV set (EN 14399-4) and an ordinary 10.9 hexagon bolt differ in dimensions and set requirements.

pc-12-9.sum: High-strength bolt grade. Minimum tensile 1220 MPa, 0.2 % proof strength 1100 MPa, 385–435 HV. Baking is mandatory when electroplated.
facts: Nominal 1200 × 0.9 = nominal yield 1080 MPa (the minimum values for judgment are tensile 1220 and proof strength 1100 MPa).
Proof stress 970 MPa, hardness 385–435 HV (39–44 HRC), minimum elongation 8 %.

Material: alloy steel quenched and tempered (tempering 425 °C or higher) or carbon steel with boron etc. added (tempering 380 °C or higher). The standard's table distinguishes these as "12.9" and underlined "12.9".

Standard note: it says to use it with care, considering manufacturer capability, service environment and tightening method, and warns that stress corrosion cracking may occur depending on the environment.
Mating: nut class 12 (style 1 ISO 4032 only up to M16, above that style 2 ISO 4033), and the washer is the 380HV recommended by ISO 898-3 (not in the product standard, so to be agreed).
Electroplating (ISO 4042) needs both process validation and baking (alkaline zinc-nickel is an exception with testing and agreement). It is not eligible for hot-dip galvanizing (ISO 10684).
watch: The inch socket head cap screw standard is ASTM A574, which is not the same system as 12.9.
Electroplating of 12.9 is, by the standard, a high-risk combination in which baking is mandatory. Consider black oxide or zinc flake (ISO 10683) first.
In corrosive environments such as seawater and humid environments, consider the risk of stress corrosion cracking.
The mating nut for a 12.9 bolt larger than M16 is ISO 4033 (style 2) class 12.

pc-nut.sum: The nut property class number is the first number of the highest bolt property class it can be used with (class 10 nut → up to 10.9 bolt). Thin nuts are 04 and 05.
facts: Current property classes: 5, 6, 8, 10, 12 (regular and high nuts), 04, 05 (thin nuts). 9 and fine-thread 5 were deleted in the current edition.
A nut of a higher property class can replace one of a lower class. Prevailing torque nuts are an exception and are paired only with the same property class.
The 0 of a thin nut shows that it is not designed to prevent thread stripping under overload, and the second number × 100 is the approximate proof stress (05 → 500 MPa).
Class 10 and 12 nuts must be quenched and tempered. Non-heat-treated nuts must keep the maximum hardness of 334 HV.
Nut height types: style 1 (regular, ISO 4032), style 2 (high, ISO 4033), style 0 (thin, ISO 4035).
watch: For an order for nuts without a property class, determine it from the mating bolt strength.
Do not write it mixed with inch nut grades (A563 A·DH, A194 2H).
KS B ISO 898-2 is identical to the old edition (1992), so its list of property classes differs from the current ISO edition (the old edition has classes 4 and 9).
Do not mix hot-dip galvanized oversize-tapped nuts (marked Z, X) with ordinary nuts.

ISO 4033 (style 2)
rows: Style 1: optional for M16 and below, quenched and tempered above / Style 2: optional
table.note: ISO 898-2 Table 2, requirement tables of the current editions of ISO 4032 and 4033 (coarse thread). "Optional" means the manufacturer chooses between not heat-treated and quenched and tempered.

pc-a2-a4.sum: "A2-70" means austenitic steel grade A2 and property class 70 (minimum tensile 700 MPa). A4 is a steel grade with molybdenum added.
facts: Steel grade groups: A austenitic (A1–A5, A8), C martensitic, F ferritic, D duplex. For fasteners, A2 and A4 are the most common.

A1 to A3 are chromium-nickel types, and A4 to A8 are chromium-nickel-molybdenum types with molybdenum added. A1 is a free-cutting steel grade with increased sulfur, so its corrosion resistance is low (ISO 3506-6).
Austenitic property class 50 does not apply to A8, and 100 does not apply to A1, A2 and A3.
Strength is obtained by cold working. Product standards also set lower property classes for large diameters (ISO 4032 nuts: A4-80 up to M24, 50 and 70 above M24).
Low-carbon steel grades with carbon of 0.030 % or less may add L (A4L-80).
ISO 3506-1 note: −20 °C to +150 °C can be used without restriction, and −196 °C to +300 °C is left to the user's judgment.
watch: SUS304 = A2 and SUS316 = A4 are approximate correspondences. If a specific steel grade such as 316L is needed, state it separately.
For a line that has only "A2" without a property class, ask again for the strength.
Stainless bolts and nuts of the same kind gall easily. Consider an anti-seize compound and slow tightening.
Cold-worked austenitic bolts may be weakly magnetic, so do not judge the material by a magnet alone.
ASTM A193 B8 and B8M (plant bolting) and ISO A2 and A4 have different strength systems, so do not write one as the other.

head: Property class
Minimum tensile (MPa)
table.note: Property class number × 10 = minimum tensile strength (MPa) (ISO 3506-1). 50 is not available for A8, and 100 is not available for A1 to A3 (ISO 3506-1 Figure 1).

mat-42crmo4.sum: A representative European Cr-Mo quenched and tempered steel. It is a steel grade found both in general mechanical use (ISO 683-2, formerly EN 10083-3) and for fasteners (EN 10269).
facts: It is a steel grade found both in ISO 683-2 (EN ISO 683-2, replaced EN 10083-3 in 2018) and in EN 10269 (for fasteners with specified high- and low-temperature properties).
It is commonly matched with AISI 4140 and JIS·KS SCM440, but the standards differ, so check composition and properties against each standard.
Strength is set by the quenching and tempering conditions and the section size, and the larger the diameter, the lower the guaranteed strength.
watch: The general certificate of ISO 683-2 (formerly EN 10083-3) and the fastener certificate of EN 10269 differ in guaranteed items (high-temperature proof strength, impact).
When changing to a material of another standard such as SCM440 or 4140, compare the composition and properties of each standard and obtain the designer's approval.
Large-diameter studs may have lower core strength because of hardenability, so check the guaranteed values by section size.

iso-898-3.sum: Standard that defines the property classes (hardness classes) of steel plain washers and their combination with bolt and nut property classes. The number is the minimum Vickers hardness (200HV = 200 HV or more).
facts: Recommended combinations: 4.6–5.8 bolts (class 5 nuts) ↔ 100HV, 6.8 and 8.8 ↔ 200HV, 9.8 and 10.9 ↔ 300HV, 12.9 ↔ 380HV.
Combinations not to be used: 100HV with 8.8 and above, and 200HV with 12.9.

380HV is not currently in ISO product standards (ISO 7089, etc.), so agreement between buyer and supplier is needed, and designs in which the washer bends, such as slotted or oversize holes, must be avoided.
It applies to plain washers, square washers, square-hole washers and template washers of thickness 0.2–12 mm, and assumes use at −50 °C to +150 °C.
For screw-and-washer assemblies (sems), only 200HV and 300HV washers are standardized (ISO 10644, 10673).
It covers only carbon steel and alloy steel washers; stainless steel washers are not covered by this standard.
watch: For a plain washer line without a hardness class, determine it from the bolt strength (8.8 → 200HV, 10.9 → 300HV).
Electroplated 300HV washers normally do not need baking, but 380HV is subject to process validation or baking (ISO 4042).
ASTM F436 (inch hardened washers) is a separate system. Do not carry the hardness range over as it is.

table.cap: Washer property classes and recommended mates (ISO 898-3)

Hardness (HV)
Recommended bolt
Recommended nut
table.note: ISO 898-3 Tables 1 and 3. 380HV is a class agreed between buyer and supplier because it is not in ISO product standards. For 100HV, exceeding up to 250 HV is not grounds for rejection.

din-931.sum: Old DIN standard for partially threaded hexagon bolts. It was withdrawn and passed to ISO 4014 (DIN EN ISO 4014); the difference that most often causes problems when reading across is the width across flats of M10, M12, M14 and M22.
facts: DIN 931-1 (M1.6~M39, product grades A and B) is shown as withdrawn in the DIN Media catalog and was replaced by DIN EN ISO 4014 via DIN EN 24014.
The widths across flats in ISO 4014 are M10 16, M12 18, M14 21, M22 34 mm. Products marked DIN 931 are usually of the old series 17, 19, 22, 32 mm, and the other nominal sizes are the same.
The steel bolt property classes of ISO 4014 (8.8, 10.9, etc.) follow ISO 898-1, and stainless steel (A2-70, etc.) follows ISO 3506-1.
The main text of KS B 1002 and JIS B 1180 is of the ISO 4014 series (MOD). The width across flats of old-type bolts of the JIS annex (Annex JA) is 17, 19, 22, 32 mm.
A length so short that no cylindrical part remains is outside the partially threaded range, so select a fully threaded bolt (ISO 4017, formerly DIN 933).
watch: "DIN 931 M12" on a drawing may be based on a 19 mm tool. If received as ISO 4014 (18 mm), check tool, socket and bearing face interference again.
For M22, the ISO side is larger (34 mm). Interference may occur in narrow spot-facing and box wrench locations.
A BOM written with both, as "DIN 931 / ISO 4014", has not fixed the width across flats. Write the width across flats in the order.
eq_notes: Successor standard. Width across flats of M10, M12, M14, M22 may differ
Main text ISO 4014~4018 MOD; bolts outside the main text in Annex A
Main text ISO MOD; Annex JA has the old width across flats

din-933.sum: Old DIN standard for hexagon bolts threaded up to the head. It was withdrawn and passed to ISO 4017. The most common difference is the width across flats of M10, M12, M14 and M22, as with DIN 931.
facts: DIN 933 (M1.6~M52, product grades A and B) is shown as withdrawn and was replaced by DIN EN ISO 4017 via DIN EN 24017.
The widths across flats in ISO 4017 are M10 16, M12 18, M14 21, M22 34 mm. Products marked DIN 933 are usually of the old series 17, 19, 22, 32 mm, and the other nominal sizes are the same.
Product grade A of ISO 4017 is M24 or smaller with length of 10d or 150 mm or less (whichever is shorter), and everything else is grade B.
Besides KS B 1002 (hexagon bolts, ISO 4014~4018 MOD), KS has KS B ISO 4017 (hexagon head screws - product grades A, B). The portal shows no level of harmonization.
The fine-thread fully threaded DIN 961 (M8×1~M52×3) was also withdrawn and passed to ISO 8676.
watch: For nominal sizes whose width across flats is the same, such as "DIN 933 M16", changing to ISO 4017 causes no tool problem. The problem is M10, M12, M14 and M22.
If shop tools are based on 17 and 19 mm, tools will not fit when ISO type (16, 18 mm) bolts get mixed in.
For a BOM written with both, as "DIN 933 / ISO 4017", decide which width across flats to receive.
eq_notes: Successor standard. Width across flats of M10, M12, M14, M22 may differ
KS bearing the ISO 4017 number (no harmonization shown on the portal)
Main text ISO MOD; Annex JA has the old width across flats

din-934.sum: Old DIN standard for coarse and fine thread hexagon nuts. It was withdrawn and passed to ISO 4032 (coarse thread) and ISO 8673 (fine thread). The width across flats of M10, M12, M14 and M22 may differ, and the nut height must not be assumed to be the same.
facts: DIN 934 (coarse and fine thread, product grades A and B) is shown as withdrawn, and the successors are DIN EN ISO 4032 and DIN EN ISO 8673.
The widths across flats in ISO 4032 are M10 16, M12 18, M14 21, M22 34 mm. Nuts marked DIN 934 are usually of the old series 17, 19, 22, 32 mm, the same as the bolts.
ISO 4032 (style 1) has a maximum height of about 0.9D, which is taller than the old nuts that were 0.8d (JIS annex type, etc.). Example: M12 maximum 10.8 mm.
The purpose of making the nut taller in the ISO system is to let the bolt strength be fully used without the threads shearing first. Mating nuts by bolt strength are in ISO 898-2.
The high nut (style 2) is ISO 4033, and the thin nut is ISO 4035 (formerly DIN 439-2).
DIN 267-4, which set the nut property classes of the old system, was withdrawn and passed to DIN EN 20898-2 (ISO 898-2).
watch: If DIN 934 and ISO 4032 are mixed as one item, the tool size may differ for M10, M12, M14 and M22, and the nut height cannot be assumed to be the same either.
For nuts to be paired with high-strength bolts such as 10.9, check the property class marking and the pairing rules of ISO 898-2.
JIS "Type 1" nuts (annex type) are of the old width across flats series (example: M12 19 mm). Do not mix them with ISO 4032 nuts.
eq_notes: Successor (coarse thread). Width across flats of M10, M12, M14, M22 may differ
Main text ISO MOD; Annex A exists
Main text ISO MOD; Annex JA old-type nut

din-912.sum: Old DIN standard for socket head cap screws (hexagon socket head bolts). It was a "modified edition of ISO 4762" and was withdrawn and passed to ISO 4762 (DIN EN ISO 4762).
facts: DIN 912 (modified edition of ISO 4762) is shown as withdrawn, and the successor is DIN EN ISO 4762.
Japan's JIS B 1176 (2014 edition) is based on ISO 4762 and ISO 12474 (fine thread) and covers coarse thread M1.6~M64 and fine thread M8×1~M36×3.
KS B 1003 (hexagon socket head bolts) is shown on the KS portal as corresponding to ISO 4762, and its scope is M1.6~M64, product grade A.
Length L is measured from the underside of the head to the end.
watch: Electro-galvanizing 12.9 socket head cap screws increases the hydrogen embrittlement risk. If plating is indispensable, decide baking conditions or another coating in advance.
For a BOM with only "cap screw", first sort out whether it is inch (ASME B18.3, ASTM A574) or metric.

din-125.sum: Old DIN standard for plain washers for bolts and nuts. DIN 125-1 was withdrawn and passed to ISO 7089 for the type A without chamfer and ISO 7090 for the type B with outer chamfer.
facts: DIN 125-1 (product grade A, hardness 250 HV or less) is shown as withdrawn, and the successors are DIN EN ISO 7089 and DIN EN ISO 7090.
The type without chamfer (A) of DIN 125-1 passed to ISO 7089, and the type with outer chamfer (B) to ISO 7090. ISO 7090 exists from nominal size 5 mm.
ISO 7089 and 7090 divide the hardness classes into 200 HV and 300 HV.
The washer for ISO 7089 M10 has inside diameter 10.5, outside diameter 20 and thickness 2 mm.
Besides KS B 1326 (plain washers), KS has KS B ISO 7089 and KS B ISO 7090, and Japan's JIS B 1256 is based on ISO 7089~7094.
watch: DIN 125-1 is a standard for washers of 250 HV or less. For the 300 HV washer to be used with 10.9 bolts and class 10 nuts, specify ISO 7089 300 HV.
Electro-galvanizing a 300 HV (heat-treated) washer carries a hydrogen embrittlement risk.
The washer nominal size is the bolt diameter it fits. The actual hole is larger (10.5 mm for M10).
eq_notes: Successor of DIN 125-1 A, 200 HV · 300 HV
Successor of DIN 125-1 B, nominal size 5 mm and above
KS plain washer (dimension comparison with ISO 7089 not given)

din-127.sum: DIN standard for rectangular-section spring washers. It was withdrawn and no successor standard is shown in DIN Media. Products marked DIN 127 are still distributed after withdrawal.
facts: DIN 127 (raised-end type and flat-end type, rectangular section) is shown as withdrawn in the DIN Media catalog, with no successor standard shown.
The last edition in the catalog is the 1987 edition (replacing the 1970 edition). The date and reason of withdrawal are not given in the catalog.
ISO has no corresponding spring washer standard.

KS B 1324 (spring washers) covers steel, stainless steel and phosphor bronze, and JIS B 1251 (spring washers in Japanese terminology) covers spring washers, disc spring washers, toothed washers and wave washers together.
The inch spring washer is ASME B18.21.1.
watch: If a bolt of 8.8 and above is tightened sufficiently, the washer is fully compressed and a locking effect is hard to expect. For vibrating locations, consider disc washers, wedge-type washers, thread-locking compound and prevailing torque nuts.
Electro-galvanizing a spring steel washer carries a hydrogen embrittlement risk.
Do not assume that products marked DIN 127 B and products marked KS B 1324 have the same dimensions. If the outside diameter matters, state the standard as well.
eq_notes: Japanese spring washer (including 4 types of washers)

din-6914.sum: Old DIN standards for HV high-strength bolts (6914), nuts (6915) and washers (6916) for steel structures. All were withdrawn and passed to EN 14399-4 (bolts and nuts) and EN 14399-6 (washers).
facts: DIN 6914 (bolts) and DIN 6915 (nuts) were replaced by EN 14399-4, and DIN 6916 (round washers) by EN 14399-6 (DIN Media).
HV is a combination of a 10.9 bolt with a hexagon head of large width across flats and a class 10 nut.
EN 14399 treats bolt, nut and washer as a set and shows the torque coefficient performance of the set by K class (K1, K2, etc.).
Compared with an ordinary hexagon bolt (ISO 4014) of the same nominal size, the width across flats is larger and the threaded portion is shorter (example: M20 HV width across flats 32 mm).
The domestic KS B 1010 and Japan's JIS B 1186 are also set standards for friction joints in steel structures, but they are not the same standard as EN 14399.
watch: Do not change an HV bolt to an ordinary 10.9 hexagon bolt of the same diameter. Head, thread length and set performance differ.
Use a set of bolt, nut and washer from the same lot. If mixed, the torque coefficient changes.
Read DIN 6914 on a drawing as an EN 14399-4 HV set, and decide together the K class that suits the tightening method.
eq_notes: Successor of DIN 6914 and 6915 (HV bolts and nuts)
Domestic set for friction joints (same use, not the same standard)

table.cap: Width across flats of HV bolts and ordinary hexagon bolts (mm)
head: Nominal size
HV bolt (EN 14399-4)
Ordinary hexagon bolt (ISO 4014)
table.note: Reference dimensions. Values of EN 14399-4 Table 2 and ISO 4014.

din-7991.sum: Old DIN standard for hexagon socket countersunk head bolts. It was withdrawn and passed to ISO 10642 (DIN EN ISO 10642). ISO 10642 is defined as a screw with low load capacity.
facts: DIN 7991 is shown as withdrawn, and the successor is DIN EN ISO 10642.
ISO 10642 is defined as a screw with low load capacity because of the head shape. The standard title of KS B ISO 10642 is also "hexagon socket countersunk head screws with reduced load capacity".
ISO 898-1 places a 0 before the property class of such low load capacity screws (example: 010.9).
Length is measured from the top of the head to the end (overall length).
KS B ISO 10642 is shown on the portal as identical (IDT) to ISO 10642:1997, and its scope is M2~M20. In Japan it is JIS B 1194 (hexagon socket countersunk head bolts).
watch: Do not expect the same load as a socket head cap screw or hexagon bolt of the same diameter.
If mixed with inch countersunk heads (82°), the bearing face will not fit.
If the existing countersink machining is based on the DIN 7991 head, compare the head dimensions of the ISO 10642 product and check for protrusion or sinking.
eq_notes: Japanese hexagon socket countersunk head bolt

din-6921.sum: Old DIN standards for the hex bolt with a disc (flange) under the head (6921) and the flange nut (6923). They were replaced by EN 1665 (heavy series) and EN 1661, respectively.
facts: DIN 6921 is shown as withdrawn; its successor is DIN EN 1665 (flange bolts, heavy series).
DIN 6923 is shown as withdrawn; its successor is DIN EN 1661 (flange nuts).
ISO 4162, the ISO flange bolt standard, is a small series, so the width across flats is smaller for the same nominal size. Example: M8 heavy (DIN 6921 · EN 1665) 13 mm, small series (ISO 4162) 10 mm.
The ISO standard for flange nuts is ISO 4161. The width across flats of an M10 flange nut is 15 mm, which differs from the regular hex nut (ISO 4032, 16 mm).
In KS, they are KS B 1042 (hex flange bolts, ISO 4162 NEQ) and KS B 1043 (hex flange nuts); in Japan, JIS B 1189 (フランジ付き六角ボルト).
watch: If "flange bolt" is ordered without a series, heavy and small-series widths across flats may be mixed.
Serrated bearing faces are generally not used on painted surfaces, thin plates, or hardened washers.
"FLANGE BOLT" in an English BOM may also refer to a stud for fastening piping flanges (e.g., B7 + 2H), so confirm the item.
eq_notes: Small series, smaller width across flats

din-985.sum: Old DIN standards for hex lock nuts with a nylon ring insert. The low type DIN 985 moved to ISO 10511, and the regular type DIN 982 moved to ISO 7040 (fine thread: ISO 10512).
facts: DIN 985 (low type) is shown as withdrawn; its successor is DIN EN ISO 10511.
DIN 982 (regular type) is shown as withdrawn; its successors are DIN EN ISO 7040 (coarse thread) and DIN EN ISO 10512 (fine thread).

ISO 10511:2012 covers low nuts of M3 to M36, property classes 04 and 05, with dimensions of the ISO 4035 low nut plus a locking feature. The 2025 revision added M7, M18, M22, M27, M33, M39 and stainless steel.
Do not assume the nut height is the same in the DIN and ISO editions. Order by the dimensions of the standard written on the drawing.
In KS, it is KS B 1044 (prevailing torque type (non-metallic insert) steel hex nuts).
Nylon rings are weak at high temperature, so consider all-metal lock nuts for high-temperature locations.
watch: The ISO 10511 low type has property classes 04 and 05 and a low load capacity. For positions carrying bolt load, use the regular type (ISO 7040).
For a BOM that only says "nylon nut" without the type (regular or low), decide the type.
A nylon nut that has been loosened once has reduced breakaway torque, so replacing it with a new one is recommended.
eq_notes: Successor of DIN 985, property classes 04 and 05

din-439.sum: Old DIN standards for low hex nuts (jam nuts). DIN 439-2 (chamfered) moved to ISO 4035 and 8675, DIN 439-1 (unchamfered) moved to ISO 4036, and DIN 936 was withdrawn without a successor.
facts: DIN 439-2 (chamfered, product grades A and B, including fine thread) is shown as withdrawn; its successors are ISO 4035 and the fine-thread ISO 8675.
DIN 439-1 (unchamfered low nut, the last edition 1987-10 is product grade B) is shown as withdrawn; its successor is ISO 4036.
DIN 936 (M8 to M52, M8×1 to M52×3 low nuts) is shown as withdrawn, but DIN Media shows no successor standard. The ISO fine-thread low nut is ISO 8675.
ISO 4035 is style 0 (a nut with low load capacity) and its strength is marked 04 or 05.
The widths across flats of ISO 4035 are M10 16, M12 18, M14 21, M22 34 mm. Nuts marked DIN 439 B usually follow the old series of 17, 19, 22, 32 mm.
watch: Do not use low nuts in positions carrying bolt load. They are for double-nut and position-locking use.
When replacing a DIN 936 fine-thread low nut with ISO, check the ISO 8675 dimensions separately.
For a BOM that only says "lock nut", determine which it is: low nut, nylon, all-metal, or bearing lock nut.
eq_notes: Successor of DIN 439-2. The width across flats may differ for M10, M12, M14, M22
Fine-thread low nut (included in the successor of DIN 439-2)
din-439.status: Withdrawn (DIN 439 → ISO 4035 · 4036 · 8675, DIN 936 has no successor shown)

din-975.t: DIN 975 · DIN 976 (threaded rods and stud rods)
din-975.sum: The threaded rod DIN 975 was withdrawn after being marked "not for new designs", and DIN Media shows no successor standard. Metric-thread stud rods are covered by the current DIN 976-1.
facts: DIN 975 (Threaded rods, not for new designs) is shown as withdrawn in the DIN Media catalog with no successor standard shown.
DIN 976-1 is current and specifies the properties and marking of metric-thread stud rods (Gewindebolzen) in steel, stainless steel, and non-ferrous metals.
The current edition of DIN 976-1 changed the thread tolerance from 6g to 8g and the straightness criterion to product grade C compared with the previous edition (DIN Media change summary).
The strength of steel threaded rods is specified by ISO 898-1 property classes (4.8, 8.8, etc.), and stainless steel by ISO 3506-1 designations.
The US standard for metric continuous and double-end studs is ASME B18.31.1M, and for inch threaded rods it is ASME B18.31.3.
watch: For hot-dip galvanized threaded rods, use overtapped nuts as the mate. Regular nuts may not fit.
Ends cut in the field have crushed threads. Fit a nut first, then cut, and clean up the thread by backing the nut off.
For high-load hanger and anchor connections, specify the bolt property class (e.g., 8.8) together with the mating nut strength.
DIN 976-1 products may have an 8g thread tolerance. Do not judge them in incoming inspection only with a 6g gauge.
eq_notes: Current metric stud rod standard (no official successor to DIN 975 is shown)

din-938.sum: DIN standards for studs, which are driven into a tapped hole in the body at one end with a nut fitted on the other. The numbers are divided by the length of the driven end, all are current, and none were replaced by ISO.
facts: Threaded length of the driven end bm: DIN 938 about 1d, DIN 939 about 1.25d, DIN 835 about 2d, DIN 940 about 2.5d.
All four standards are current DIN and cover product grade A, steel or stainless steel products.
In the DIN Media summary, DIN 938 is described mainly for steel base material and DIN 940 for light metals with lower strength.
The ordering length l is the nut-end length excluding the driven end. The overall length is l plus the driven-end length.
National standards of the same kind are KS B 1037 (stud bolts) and JIS B 1173 (植込みボルト).
watch: The driven-end length is decided by the base material and tap depth. Even with the same nominal size and the same l, the overall length differs if the DIN number differs.
For a BOM that only says "stud bolt", determine whether it is a tap-end stud or a double-nut stud for flanges (ASME B18.31.2 · A193 B7).
For studs in pump and valve pressure parts, check the material and certificate requirements (e.g., A193 B7) separately.
eq_notes: Inch continuous and double-end studs (different form system)

head: Standard
Driven end bm
Coarse thread range
Fine thread range
table.note: Based on the DIN Media catalog summary (current edition).

din-471.sum: DIN standards for C-shaped retaining rings fitted into shaft grooves (471) and bore grooves (472). They include both regular and heavy types and are current. The domestic KS B 1336 and Japanese JIS B 2804 are of the same kind.
facts: DIN 471 (for shafts) and DIN 472 (for bores) are current DIN and specify both the regular type and the heavy type. For both standards, the new edition of May 2026 (5/2026) is current.
They also specify the dimensions of the groove in which the ring is fitted. They are used to fix parts such as bearings on a shaft or in a bore and to take axial force.
The nominal size of a shaft ring is the shaft diameter, and that of a bore ring is the bore diameter.
National standards of the same kind are KS B 1336 (C-type retaining rings) and JIS B 2804 (止め輪). E-rings are KS B 1337 · DIN 6799.
DIN 471 and 472 are current DIN not replaced by ISO.
watch: For a line that only says "snap ring", determine whether it is for a shaft or a bore. If the lugs are outside, it is for a shaft; if inside, for a bore.
Do not assume that KS and JIS rings have the same dimensions as DIN rings. Check the groove dimensions as well.
A ring that has been spread and removed may change shape, so replacing it with a new one at maintenance is generally done.
eq_notes: KS C-type retaining ring (dimension comparison not included)

din-6885.sum: DIN standard for parallel keys and keyways placed between a shaft and a hub. DIN 6885-1 (high type) is current. The old ISO/R 773 was withdrawn in 1998.
facts: DIN 6885-1 is the current standard specifying the dimensions, tolerances, and mass of high-type parallel keys and keyways.
DIN 6885-2 for machine tools (high type) and DIN 6885-3 (low type) are separate.
End shapes are form A (both ends round) and form B (both ends square), and the current edition added form AB (one end round, one end square).
The fit (tight, normal, sliding) is set not by the key but by the tolerances of the shaft and hub keyways.
KS B 1311 (sunk keys and keyways) covers parallel keys, taper keys, and Woodruff keys, and KS B 1313 covers sliding keys. In Japan, it is JIS B 1301 (キー及びキー溝).
ISO/R 773 (parallel keys) was withdrawn in 1998 (ISO catalog).
watch: Write the key designation as b × h × length. b × h is set for each shaft diameter range.
If there is no form A or B marking, check the end shape.
Do not assume that KS and JIS keys have the same dimensions and tolerances as DIN keys.

din-6888.sum: DIN standard for half-disc-shaped Woodruff keys and keyways. It is current. ISO 3912 was withdrawn, and in Korea, Woodruff keys are included in KS B 1311.
facts: DIN 6888 is the current standard specifying the dimensions and use of Woodruff keys.
Metric Woodruff keys are designated by b × h (width × height).
The scope of KS B 1311 (sunk keys and keyways) includes Woodruff keys (KS portal).
Inch Woodruff keys are ASME B17.2 (Woodruff Keys and Keyseats).
ISO 3912 (Woodruff keys) was withdrawn in 2021 (ISO catalog).
watch: Inch numbered keys (ASME B17.2) and metric b × h keys are not interchangeable.
Check whether KS and JIS Woodruff key dimensions are the same as DIN 6888 before substituting.
A Woodruff key has a deep keyway and reduces the shaft cross-section considerably. For large torque, consider a parallel key.

din-7-6325.sum: Old DIN standards for parallel pins. The unhardened DIN 7 moved to ISO 2338, and the hardened (tolerance zone m6) DIN 6325 moved to ISO 8734.
facts: DIN 7 is shown as withdrawn and was replaced by DIN EN ISO 2338 (parallel pins of unhardened steel and austenitic stainless steel) via DIN EN 22338.
DIN 6325 (hardened, tolerance zone m6) is shown as withdrawn; its successor is DIN EN 28734 (ISO 8734:1986). DIN EN 28734 is also shown as withdrawn.
For ISO 2338, the diameter tolerance is chosen from m6 and h8. ISO 8734 is m6 and has the through-hardened type A and the case-hardened type B.
KS has standards carrying ISO numbers: KS B ISO 2338 (nominal diameter 0.6 to 50 mm) and KS B ISO 8734 (dowel pins).
The bolt carries the fastening force, and the pin only locates.
watch: A pin placed in a blind hole is hard to pull out. Where disassembly is needed, consider parallel pins with internal thread.
Electroplating a hardened pin carries a risk of hydrogen embrittlement.
The tolerance (m6, h8) is easily omitted from a "DIN 7" line. Write the tolerance when ordering.

din-1481.sum: Old DIN standard for heavy-duty slotted spring pins. It was withdrawn and moved to ISO 8752. The light-duty DIN 7346 corresponds to ISO 13337.
facts: DIN 1481 is shown as withdrawn and was replaced by DIN EN ISO 8752 via DIN EN 28752.
The light-duty DIN 7346 was also withdrawn and replaced by DIN EN ISO 13337.
The spring pin nominal size is the diameter of the hole it fits.
KS B ISO 8752 (spring-type straight pins — slotted, heavy duty) exists.
The heavy-duty type is thick and has a large shear load, and the light-duty type is thin and easy to drive.
watch: For a line that only says "spring pin", determine whether it is heavy-duty or light-duty.
Avoid electroplating spring pins because of the risk of hydrogen embrittlement.
The standard has no shear load values for austenitic stainless steel pins.

din-94.sum: Old DIN standard for split pins. It was withdrawn and moved to ISO 1234 (DIN EN ISO 1234). KS adopted ISO as is as KS B ISO 1234.
facts: DIN 94 is shown as withdrawn; its successor is DIN EN ISO 1234.
KS B ISO 1234 (split pins) adopted ISO 1234 as identical (IDT) and covers steel, brass, and stainless steel split pins.
The split pin nominal size is not the pin diameter but the diameter of the hole it fits. The actual pin is thinner than the nominal size.
Inch split pins are ASME B18.8.1, with a different designation system.
watch: Do not reuse a split pin that has been spread once and straightened.
The length is from under the eye to the end of the short leg. Choose it as the through length plus allowance for spreading the legs.
Do not mix metric and inch designations.

din-913-916.sum: Four old DIN standards for hexagon socket set screws. Each was a modified edition of ISO 4026 to 4029, and they were withdrawn and moved to the corresponding ISO.
facts: DIN 913 flat point → ISO 4026, DIN 914 cone point → ISO 4027, DIN 915 dog point → ISO 4028, DIN 916 cup point → ISO 4029.
All four standards were issued as "ISO modified editions" and are now shown as withdrawn (successors DIN EN ISO 4026 to 4029).
The strength of steel set screws is marked by a hardness-based grade (45H, etc.).
Set screws are not for applications carrying tensile force.
National standards of the same kind are KS B 1028 (hexagon socket set screws) and JIS B 1177 (六角穴付き止めねじ).
watch: For a "set bolt" line without a point shape, decide the point shape. Cup point is the most common.
Because 45H steel set screws are parts not subject to tension, ISO 4042 (current edition) does not require baking after electroplating. Write the plating specification in the order.
Do not mix with inch set screws (ASME B18.3).
eq_notes: Japan 六角穴付き止めねじ

din-580.t: DIN 580 · DIN 582 (eye bolts and eye nuts)
din-580.sum: Current DIN standards for steel and stainless steel lifting eye bolts (580) and eye nuts (582). They are specified for lower loads than ISO 3266 eye bolts of the same diameter.
facts: DIN 580 and DIN 582 are current DIN and cover steel and stainless steel products.
On the basis of the same diameter, the DIN 580 eye bolt is for lower loads than DIN EN ISO 3266.
Both standards specify that they can be used at −20 °C to +200 °C without reducing the load.
In the EU, it is advised that a CE marking under the Machinery Directive (2006/42/EC) is required for these as removable lifting components.
KS B 1033 (eye bolts), KS B 1034 (eye nuts), and JIS B 1168 (アイボルト) are separate national standards.
DIN 444 (Augenschrauben) is the standard for eye bolts of M5 to M39 in product grades A, B, and C. Do not confuse it with the lifting DIN 580.
watch: The permissible load table differs by standard. Do not apply DIN 580 loads to KS, JIS, or ISO 3266 products.
The basic load in the standard table is the value for 1 bolt lifting vertically. It decreases greatly when tilted or when lifting with 2 or more.
Screw it in all the way so that the underside of the collar fully contacts the mating surface before use.
For use below −20 °C or above +200 °C, check the load reduction conditions separately.
eq_notes: Forged eye bolt grade 4, higher load at the same diameter (do not mix load tables)
KS eye bolts and eye nuts

din-2510.sum: A group of DIN standards for bolted connections with a thinned shank to increase elastic elongation. They are for equipment, piping, and turbines with large varying loads and temperature changes, and are divided into several parts.
facts: Contents by part: -1 overview, scope, installation examples; -2 thread; -3 stud bolts (Schraubenbolzen); -4 studs (Stiftschrauben); -5 hex nuts; -6 cap nuts; -7 extension sleeves; -8 tapped holes for studs.
-1, -2, -6, and -7 have been revised to new editions, and for -3, -4, -5, and -8 the 1971 edition is current (DIN Media).

The DIN 2510-2 thread is used for nominal sizes over 11.2 mm up to 180 mm, and gives the external thread a large fundamental deviation (clearance). It is intended for hydraulic tensioning and to prevent loosening and seizing at high temperature.
The permissible thread dimensions assume a nut of height 1d (DIN 2510-5).
For fine threads, only the next smaller pitch after the coarse thread in the DIN ISO 965-1 series is listed.
It is used for bolted connections in equipment, piping, and turbines with large varying loads and temperature changes.
watch: If a reduced-shank stud is replaced with a general threaded stud, the elastic elongation decreases and the characteristics for maintaining clamping force change. Do not substitute without design confirmation.
The thread tolerance differs from the general 6g, so set the inspection criteria by DIN 2510-2.
Confirm the type, material, and shank diameter by the drawing.

din-267.sum: A DIN series that specifies technical delivery conditions for fasteners by part. The strength, plating, and stainless steel parts moved to ISO, and some, such as the part for high- and low-temperature components (-13), are current.
facts: DIN 267-13 is the current standard specifying special mechanical properties of bolted connection components used at −200 °C to +700 °C.
The old-system nut strength DIN 267-4 was withdrawn and moved to the ISO 898-2 series (DIN EN 20898-2).
Electroplating DIN 267-9 → ISO 4042, hot-dip galvanizing DIN 267-10 → ISO 10684, stainless steel DIN 267-11 → ISO 3506-1 · -2 · -3.
Fine-thread nut strength DIN 267-23 moved to ISO 898-6, and ISO 898-6 was in turn merged into ISO 898-2 (2012 edition).
The hardness grades of nuts without proof load (DIN 267-24), microencapsulated adhesive coating (DIN 267-27), and thread-forming screws of 10.9 (DIN 267-30) are current.
Read a citation of "DIN 267" on an old drawing by checking the part number and replacing it with the current ISO.
watch: Do not directly replace high- and low-temperature bolting with a DIN 267-13 requirement by general ISO 898-1 property class bolts. ISO 898-1 parts assume use at −50 to +150 °C.
For an old drawing with a remaining DIN 267-10 (hot-dip galvanizing) requirement, check against ISO 10684 (overtapping, etc.).
"DIN 267" without a part number is meaningless. Confirm which part it is.

din-iso-map.en_title: Withdrawn DIN fastener standards and successor ISO and EN
din-iso-map.sum: A single table of the DIN numbers of fasteners that still remain on many drawings, their successor ISO and EN standards, and what actually changes when reading them as the successor.
facts: When DIN adopts an ISO standard, it issues it as a "DIN EN ISO number" and withdraws the old DIN number. Even when withdrawn, the notation on drawings and in distribution remains for a long time.
The most common dimensional difference is the hex width across flats: for M10, M12, M14, M22, ISO has 16, 18, 21, 34 mm, while DIN-marked products usually have 17, 19, 22, 32 mm.
Nuts also differ in height criteria: ISO 4032 style 1 has a maximum height of about 0.9D, which is higher than the old 0.8d series (JIS annex type, etc.).
Some standards, such as DIN 127 (spring washers), DIN 936 (low nuts), and DIN 975 (threaded rods), were withdrawn with no successor shown in DIN Media.

Retaining rings (DIN 471 · 472), keys (DIN 6885 · 6888), tap-end studs (DIN 938 · 939 · 835 · 940), eye bolts and eye nuts (DIN 580 · 582), reduced-shank bolts (DIN 2510), and stud rods (DIN 976-1) are current DIN.
An ISO successor does not mean it is "the same product". Check the width across flats, height, and strength marking for each line.
watch: If a BOM lists DIN and ISO together, decide which one's dimensions (especially the width across flats) to receive.
For nominal sizes with the same width across flats (M8, M16, M20, M24, etc.), switching to ISO causes no tool problem.
JIS annex type (old type) hex bolts and nuts also use the old widths across flats (M10 17, M12 19, M14 22, M22 32 mm).

ks-b-1002.sum: The basic KS for domestic hex bolts. The main text adopted ISO 4014 to 4018 with modification (MOD), and bolts and screws not following the main text are placed separately in Annex A.
facts: Corresponding international standards on the KS portal: ISO 4014 · 4015 · 4016 · 4017 · 4018, with the harmonization level for all being MOD (partially identical).
Scope: hex bolts of steel, stainless steel, and non-ferrous metals for general use.
Bolts and screws not following the main text are specified in Annex A (note to the scope, Korean Standards Association KSSN).
Cited standards: mechanical properties KS B 0233 (steel) · KS B 0241 (stainless steel, ISO 3506-1~3:1997 IDT), threads KS B 0201 · 0204, tolerance system KS B 0238 (ISO 4759-1 · -3:2000 IDT).
ISO 4017 (fully threaded) also exists separately as KS B ISO 4017.
The most recent revision reflected that the country of manufacturing origin is marked with the 2-letter country code of ISO 3166-1.
watch: A BOM that only says "KS B 1002 M10" does not settle whether it is the main text (ISO 4014 series) or the Annex A type. Have the width across flats written.
If bolts with the old width across flats (JIS annex type 17, 19, 22, 32 mm) are replaced by ISO 4014 · 4017 (16, 18, 21, 34 mm), the tool size changes for M10, M12, M14, M22.
There is no tool problem for M8, M16, M20, M24, which have the same width across flats.
eq_notes: Correspondence (main text ISO MOD + Annex composition)

ks-b-1012.t: KS B 1012 (hex nuts and hex low nuts)
ks-b-1012.sum: The KS for domestic hex nuts and low nuts. The main text adopted the ISO 4032 series with modification (MOD), and there is a separate Annex A.
facts: Corresponding international standards: shown as ISO 4032 (MOD) on the national standards portal, and as ISO 4032 · 4033 · 4034 · 4035 · 4036 (all MOD) on the Korean Standards Association KSSN.
Scope: hex nuts and hex low nuts of steel, stainless steel, and non-ferrous metals for general use.
There is an Annex A, and in the most recent revision, the stainless steel nut marking in the product designation method of Annex A was aligned with KS B 0241.
It cites KS B 0234 for the mechanical properties of steel nuts. KS B 0234 places the property classes 4T to 12T in an annex.
KS B ISO 4033 and KS B ISO 4035, which adopted the 1999 editions of ISO 4033 (style 2) and 4035 (low nut) as identical (IDT), also exist.
watch: A BOM that only says "KS B 1012 M12" does not settle whether it is the main text (ISO type) or the Annex A type. Write the width across flats and height together.
Strengths with a T, such as 4T and 8T, are the old system. Do not read them as the same grades as property classes 8 and 10 of ISO 898-2.
Specify the nut strength matching the bolt strength together. Ask back for a BOM lacking the nut strength.
eq_notes: Correspondence (main text ISO MOD + Annex composition)

ks-b-1010.t: KS B 1010 (high-strength bolt sets for friction grip joints)
ks-b-1010.en_title: High-strength hex bolt, hex nut, and plain washer sets for friction grip joints
ks-b-1010.sum: The KS for sets of high-strength hex bolts, hex nuts, and plain washers used in friction grip joints of steel structures. Grades use the F8T and F10T designations, and the 2004 revision introduced the 1300 MPa class F13T and a delayed fracture test.
facts: Scope: sets of high-strength hex bolts, hex nuts, and plain washers for friction grip joints, used mainly in steel structures.
Before the 2004 revision, there were three grades, F8T, F10T, and F11T, and the field mainstream was the 1000 MPa class F10T (Korean Agency for Technology and Standards revision commentary).
The 2004-12 revision added the 1300 MPa class F13T and a hydrogen delayed fracture sensitivity test (revision commentary of the Korean Agency for Technology and Standards, portal history).
It cites the hydrogen embrittlement preload test KS B ISO 15330, bolt holes KS B ISO 273, and others.
The KS portal shows no corresponding international standard. Japan's JIS B 1186 also states that it has no corresponding international standard.
watch: Use a set within the same lot. Mixing parts of different lots or different standards changes the torque coefficient.
Do not replace an F10T set with general 10.9 hex bolts and nuts. There are torque coefficient and lot requirements per set.
For torque-controlled tightening, check the torque coefficient value of the set (certificate) and set the tightening torque.
If plating is needed on an F10T set, examine the delayed fracture risk separately at the design stage.
eq_notes: European HV set (same use, not the same standard)

ks-b-2819.sum: The KS for sets of torque-shear type high-strength bolts, hex nuts, and plain washers, which are tightened until the pintail at the end breaks off to introduce clamping force. In Korea, they are commonly called S10T (T/S bolts).
facts: Standard title: sets of torque-shear type high-strength bolts, hex nuts, and plain washers for structures. Established in 2003.
The scope is defined as sets fastened mainly to steel structures and used in the range of 0 °C to 60 °C (KS portal).

The structure is such that the pintail outside the breaking groove at the thread end takes the tightening reaction force, and tightening continues until the groove twists and breaks off to obtain the specified axial force (KSSN note to the scope).
It cites KS B 1010 (sets for friction grip joints).
In Japan, the same kind is not a JIS but an association standard (for buildings JSS II 09, for road bridges a Japan Road Association standard), and the tensile strength of S10T is 1000 to 1200 MPa.
watch: S10T and F10T sets have different tightening methods and are not used interchangeably.
For use outside the applicable temperature range (0 to 60 °C), the designer decides separately.
For positions where the tightening tool does not fit, decide the tightening method separately at the design stage.
eq_notes: Japan torque-shear type set for buildings (S10T)
European HRC set (preload-compensating type, not the same standard)

ks-b-1336.sum: The KS for general-use eccentric C-type retaining rings. They are fitted in grooves to fix parts axially. The E type is separately KS B 1337.
facts: Scope: general-use eccentric C-shaped retaining rings (KS portal).
It cites special strip steel (KS D 3551) and hard steel wire rod (KS D 3559) for the material, and the Rockwell test (KS B 0806) for the hardness test.
The E-type retaining ring is KS B 1337 (for shafts).
Foreign standards of the same kind are Japan's JIS B 2804 (止め輪) and Germany's DIN 471 (for shafts) and DIN 472 (for bores).
The KS portal shows no corresponding international standard.
watch: The nominal size of a shaft ring is the shaft diameter, and that of a bore ring is the bore diameter.
Do not assume that KS rings have the same dimensions as DIN 471 · 472 rings. Check by the groove dimensions.
The "snap ring" designation does not distinguish shaft from bore.
eq_notes: Germany, for shafts and bores (dimension comparison not included)

ks-b-1311.en_title: Sunk keys and keyways (parallel, taper, and Woodruff keys)
ks-b-1311.sum: The KS that specifies steel parallel keys, taper keys, and Woodruff keys for general machinery and their keyways. Sliding keys are separately KS B 1313.
facts: The standard title is "Sunk keys and keyways", and it covers parallel keys, taper keys, Woodruff keys, and the corresponding keyways (KS portal scope).
Sliding keys and keyways are KS B 1313.
Japan's JIS B 1301 (キー及びキー溝) is a standard of the same kind.
In Germany, they are divided into parallel keys DIN 6885-1, Woodruff keys DIN 6888, and taper keys with head DIN 6887.
The KS portal shows no corresponding international standard (ISO/R 773 and ISO 3912 are withdrawn).
watch: Do not assume key dimensions are the same among KS, JIS, and DIN.
The fit is set by the keyway tolerance. Changing only the key does not change the fit.
In the BOM, write the type (parallel, taper, Woodruff), b × h, length, and end shape.

ks-thread.t: KS metric thread standards (coarse and fine)
ks-thread.en_title: KS for metric coarse and fine threads
ks-thread.sum: KS B 0201 specifies the metric coarse thread, KS B 0204 the fine thread, and KS B 0211 · 0214 the tolerances. The basic profile adopted ISO 68-1 with modification (MOD).
facts: KS B 0201 (metric coarse threads): basic profile, formulas, basic dimensions. Corresponding ISO 68-1 (MOD), ISO 261 · ISO 724 (NEQ).
KS B 0204 (metric fine threads): combinations of diameter and pitch, selection criteria of fine threads for bolts and nuts. Corresponding ISO 68-1 (MOD).
Tolerances: KS B 0211 (coarse thread) · KS B 0214 (fine thread), both adopted ISO 965-1~3 with modification (MOD).
Limit gauges are KS B 5221 (for coarse thread) · KS B 5222 (for fine thread).
Japan uses JIS B 0205-1~4 (a composition corresponding to ISO 68-1 · 261 · 262 · 724) and the tolerances JIS B 0209-1~5.
watch: Fine threads have several pitches for the same diameter (e.g., M10×1.25 · M10×1). For a line that only says "fine thread" without a pitch, decide the pitch.
For hot-dip galvanized bolts and nuts, use threads with a shifted tolerance position (overtapped nuts) as the mate.
eq_notes: Basic profile, overall system, selected sizes

head: Nominal size
Pitch
table.note: Coarse thread pitches of ISO 261 · 262.

ks-washer.t: KS washer standards (plain washers and spring washers)
ks-washer.en_title: KS washers: plain washers, spring washers, etc.
ks-washer.sum: KS B 1326 is the basic standard for plain washers and KS B 1324 for spring washers. KS B ISO 7089 · 7090, which carry ISO numbers, exist separately, and toothed washers and disc spring washers are also separate KS.
facts: KS B 1326 (plain washers): round plain washers and square washers of steel, stainless steel, and brass. Washers for timber construction are excluded (KS portal).
KS B 1324 (spring washers): spring washers of steel, stainless steel, and phosphor bronze.
KS B ISO 7089 (normal series, product grade A) · KS B ISO 7090 (chamfered type, nominal size 5 mm or more) have hardness grades of 200 HV · 300 HV.
In addition, there are KS B 1325 (toothed washers), KS B 1329 (conical spring washers), and KS B 1327 (washers for jigs and tools).
KS B 1326 · 1324 show no corresponding international standard on the portal.
In Japan, they are JIS B 1256 (plain washers, MOD based on ISO 7089~7094) and JIS B 1251 (spring, disc spring, toothed, and wave washers).
watch: Do not assume that a plain washer that only says "KS B 1326" has the same dimensions as ISO 7089. If the outside diameter matters, write a dimensional standard such as ISO 7089 together.
Specify a 300 HV washer for 10.9 bolts.
Zinc electroplating of spring washers and hardened washers carries a risk of hydrogen embrittlement.
eq_notes: KS B ISO 7089 · 7090 (no harmonization shown on the portal)
Japan plain washers and spring washers

ks-socket.en_title: KS for hexagon socket head bolts (wrench bolts)
ks-socket.sum: The basic KS for wrench bolts is KS B 1003 (hexagon socket head bolts). It is shown on the KS portal as corresponding to ISO 4762, and countersunk head, button head, set screws, and shoulder bolts are separate KS.
facts: KS B 1003: hexagon socket head bolts of nominal thread size M1.6 to M64, product grade A (KS portal scope).
The corresponding international standard on the KS portal is ISO 4762:1997 (old edition).

Countersunk head is KS B ISO 10642 (hexagon socket countersunk head screws with reduced loadability), button head is KS B 1067 (ISO 7380:1983 IDT), set screws are KS B 1028, and shoulder bolts are KS B 1104.
Japan's JIS B 1176 (2014 edition) is a MOD based on ISO 4762 · ISO 12474 and covers coarse thread M1.6 to M64 and fine thread M8×1 to M36×3.
Germany's DIN 912 was withdrawn and moved to ISO 4762.
watch: Electroplating of 12.9 wrench bolts carries a high risk of hydrogen embrittlement.
For a line that only says "cap bolt" or "cap screw", determine whether it is inch (ASME B18.3) or metric.
Do not expect a countersunk head wrench bolt to carry the same load as a wrench bolt of the same diameter.

ks-flange.t: KS pipe flange standards and bolts
ks-flange.en_title: KS steel pipe flanges (K designation) and bolts
ks-flange.sum: KS pipe flanges use the pressure designation K (5K · 10K · 20K, etc.). KS B 1511 specifies the basic dimensions and KS B 1503 the steel welding-type flanges, and the bolts have metric threads.
facts: KS B 1511 (basic dimensions and dimensional tolerances of steel pipe flanges): pressure designations 2K · 5K · 10K · 16K · 20K · 30K.
KS B 1503 (steel welding-type pipe flanges): 5K to 30K flanges whose reference dimensions follow KS B 1511. The portal correspondence is ISO 7005-1 (NEQ).
Stainless steel welding type is KS B 1506 (5K · 10K · 20K · 30K), the gasket seat is KS B 1519, and copper alloy is KS B 1510 (5K · 10K · 16K).

The old KS standards "basic dimensions of steel pipe flanges in kgf/cm²", which existed separately by pressure, were withdrawn, and KS B 1502 for dimensional tolerances was also merged into KS B 1511.

KS B 1511 cites KS B 1002 (hex bolts) and KS D 3755 (alloy steel bolt material for high temperature) as bolt-related cited standards. KS D 3755 was withdrawn and moved to an association standard (SPS-KOSA0033-D3755-5098) (KS portal).
Even for the same pipe nominal size, the number and diameter of bolts may differ depending on the K designation. Japan's JIS B 2220 also uses the K designation.
watch: Orders sometimes come as flange designations such as "10K 50A × n sets". Work out the number, nominal size, and length of bolts from the flange table and confirm.
Do not assume that the bolt circle and number of holes are the same as for ASME B16.5 (Class 150, etc.) and EN 1092-1 (PN) flanges. Compare dimensions before mixing them.

For high-temperature and high-pressure piping, check whether studs with a specified material such as A193 B7 or SNB7 are used instead of general hex bolts. KS D 3755, which was the KS for SNB7, was withdrawn.
eq_notes: Japan K-designation flange (dimension comparison with KS not included)

ks-iso-map.t: KS ↔ ISO correspondence (KS B ISO numbers)
ks-iso-map.en_title: ISO correspondence levels of KS fastener standards
ks-iso-map.sum: KS that transpose ISO as is (IDT) are usually given "KS B ISO number", and KS modified to reflect domestic circumstances (MOD) are given their own number. The portal shows the corresponding ISO and the harmonization level.
facts: Harmonization level notation: IDT (identical), MOD (modified, partially identical), NEQ (not equivalent).
KS B 1002 (hex bolts) is MOD of ISO 4014~4018, and KS B 1012 (hex nuts) is MOD of the ISO 4032 series; both have an Annex A.

KS B ISO 898-1 is shown on the basis of ISO 898-1:1999 and KS B ISO 898-2 on ISO 898-2:1992, so they are older than the current ISO editions. Japan's JIS B 1051 and B 1052-2 transposed ISO 898-1:2013 and ISO 898-2:2022 as is, respectively.
There are also KS that carry no ISO number but are shown as identical (IDT) to ISO: KS B 0241 (ISO 3506-1~3:1997), KS B 0238 (ISO 4759-1 · -3:2000), KS B 1067 (ISO 7380:1983).
There are also KS B ISO standards whose harmonization field on the portal is "no data" (e.g., KS B ISO 4017 · 2338 · 8734 · 8752).
watch: "KS B 1002" and "ISO 4014" are not the same thing. It is MOD and has an Annex A, so check the width across flats.
The ISO edition on which a KS B ISO standard is based may be old. Decide the edition to use for certificate evaluation.
Do not mix the KS-specific strength standards (KS B 0233 bolts, KS B 0234 nuts — 4T to 12T in the annex) with the numeric strengths of the ISO 898 series.

jis-b-1180.sum: Japanese hex bolt standard. The main text is a MOD based on ISO 4014~4018 · 8676 · 8765, and old-type bolts not following ISO remain in 附属書JA (normative).
facts: The main text is a MOD based on ISO 4014 · 4015 · 4016 · 4017 · 4018 and the fine-thread ISO 8676 · 8765. The form and dimensions parts transposed ISO without technical changes, and the changed places are marked with underlines and collected in Annex JB (Introduction).
Old-type hex bolts not following ISO are in 附属書JA (normative). At the 1985 revision, the preceding standard was moved to an annex.
The 2014 revision kept the annex content but stated that it is preferable not to use it for new designs.
For the annex type, the width across flats of M10, M12, M14, M22 is 17, 19, 22, 32 mm, which differs from the main text (16, 18, 21, 34 mm), and the head height also differs in part.
The annex type divides finish quality into upper, middle, and ordinary (上·中·並), and the main text into product grades A, B, C. Small hex bolts exist only in the annex.
The Japanese industry decided to use the designations "JA hex bolts" (annex) and "IS hex bolts" (main text) to distinguish them.
watch: "JIS B 1180 M10" alone does not settle the width across flats (16 or 17). Check main text or annex (IS · JA).
According to a Japanese industry survey (2014), general distribution products at that time were almost all the annex type. For Japanese equipment spare parts, check the actual width across flats.
The mate for annex type bolts is the JIS B 1181 annex type nut. Mixing with main text nuts changes the tool size.
eq_notes: Correspondence (main text ISO MOD + Annex composition)
Withdrawn DIN. Products marked with it usually have the old width across flats, the same as the annex type

jis-b-1181.sum: Japanese hex nut standard. The main text is a MOD based on ISO 4032~4036 · 8673~8675, old-type nuts are in 附属書JA, and the old property classes 4T to 10T are in 附属書JB (normative).
facts: The main text is a MOD based on ISO 4032 (style 1) · 4033 (style 2) · 4034 · 4035 · 4036 and the fine-thread 8673 · 8674 · 8675 (Introduction).
附属書JA (normative) is the old-type hex nut not following ISO, and 附属書JB (normative) is the steel nut property classes 4T to 10T.
The height of old-type nuts (type 1 · type 2) is 0.8d (M12 10 mm), and main text style 1 is higher (M12 max 10.8 mm).

The old strengths are 4T · 5T · 6T · 8T · 10T, and main text nut strengths follow JIS B 1052-2 (current edition 04 · 05 · 5 · 6 · 8 · 10 · 12). Even when the numbers are the same, the T system and the strength differ.
In the main text system, the nut is chosen to match the bolt strength (JIS B 1052-2).
The width across flats difference applies to the same 4 nominal sizes as for bolts (M10 · M12 · M14 · M22).
watch: "Nut type 1" is the annex type (0.8d, M12 width across flats 19 mm). Do not mix it with main text (IS) nuts.
Do not regard nuts with a T marking such as 4T and 8T as the same grades as strengths 8 and 10 of ISO 898-2.
The annex type low nut is not shown as the same as ISO 4035.
eq_notes: Correspondence (main text ISO MOD + Annex composition)
Withdrawn DIN. Products marked with it usually have the old width across flats, the same as the old type

jis-b-1176.sum: Japanese wrench bolt standard. It is a MOD based on ISO 4762 (coarse thread) and ISO 12474 (fine thread), and the 2014 edition covers coarse thread M1.6 to M64 and fine thread M8×1 to M36×3.
facts: The corresponding international standards are ISO 4762 and ISO 12474 (fine thread), and the overall evaluation is MOD.
Scope (2014 edition): product grade A, coarse thread M1.6 to M64, fine thread M8×1 to M36×3. An amendment (追補) of 2015-12-21 is shown on JISC.

The form and dimensions parts transposed ISO without technical changes, and terms, marking items, and an informative annex (limit dimensions of 5g6g threads, strength 12.9) were added (序文 · table of contents).
Unlike hex bolts (JIS B 1180), there is no annex for old-type products not following ISO (based on the table of contents of the 2014 edition).
The same item is KS B 1003 and DIN 912 (withdrawn → ISO 4762).
watch: Electroplating of 12.9 wrench bolts carries a high risk of hydrogen embrittlement.

Strength 12.9 wrench bolts are sometimes specified with a 5g6g thread tolerance (JIS B 1176 places the 5g6g limit dimensions in an informative annex). Check the specified tolerance before gauge evaluation.
For a line that only says "cap screw", determine whether it is inch or metric.

jis-b-1186.sum: Japanese standard for sets of high-strength hex bolts, nuts, and plain washers for friction grip joints of steel structures. It has class 1 (F8T) and class 2 (F10T) and no corresponding international standard. The grade marking is the same as the domestic KS B 1010.
facts: Scope: sets for friction grip joints, used mainly in steel structures. There is no corresponding international standard (Introduction).
Classes: Class 1 (1種) F8T, Class 2 (2種) F10T. The tensile strength is F8T 800~1000, F10T 1000~1200 MPa (Japanese public research institute data).
There are two types, A and B, according to the torque coefficient value.
It specifies together the set composition, lot composition, mechanical properties of bolts and nuts, washer hardness, and set torque coefficient value (table of contents).
The nominal sizes used in the Japanese building field are M12 · M16 · M20 · M22 · M24 · M27 · M30.
The torque-shear type S10T is not specified in JIS and uses association standards (JSS II 09, etc.).
watch: Use a set within the same lot, and check the torque coefficient class (A · B) to set the tightening torque.
Do not replace F10T with general 10.9 bolts.
For "高力ボルト" and "HTB" in a Japanese equipment BOM, check the grade (F8T · F10T), nominal size, and length.

jis-b-1256.sum: Japanese plain washer standard. It is a MOD based on ISO 7089~7094 (normal, small, large, and extra-large series) and covers round plain washers of steel and stainless steel. Square washers are in an informative annex.
facts: Corresponding international standards: ISO 7089 · 7090 · 7091 · 7092 · 7093-1 · 7093-2 · 7094, overall evaluation MOD.
The types, form, and dimensions parts transposed ISO without technical changes and marking items were added (Introduction).
Scope: round plain washers of steel and stainless steel used with general-use bolts, small screws, and nuts.
Square washers (角座金) have their form and dimensions in 附属書JA (informative).
The domestic KS B 1326 (plain washers) covers round and square washers together and also includes brass.
watch: ISO 7089 (normal) · 7092 (small) · 7093 (large) differ in outside diameter. For a line that only says "plain washer", decide the series.
Specify a 300 HV washer for 10.9 bolts.
The washers of high-strength bolt sets (JIS B 1186 · KS B 1010) are dedicated to the set, so do not replace them with general plain washers.

jis-b-1251.sum: Japanese spring washer standard. It covers together four types used with general-use bolts, small screws, and nuts: spring washers, disc spring washers, toothed washers, and wave spring washers.
facts: Scope: four types, ばね座金 · 皿ばね座金 · 歯付き座金 · 波形ばね座金.
Spring washers fitted in washer-assembled screws (sems) are in Annex A (informative).
It sets the material, hardness, spring action, toughness tests, and inspection items (table of contents).
The domestic corresponding items are KS B 1324 (spring washers), KS B 1325 (toothed washers), and KS B 1329 (conical spring washers), and Germany's DIN 127 was withdrawn without replacement.
ISO has no corresponding spring washer dimension standard.
watch: Electroplating of spring steel washers carries a risk of hydrogen embrittlement.
When a high-strength bolt is tightened sufficiently, the anti-loosening effect of a spring washer is small.
Do not assume that JIS, KS, and DIN 127 spring washers have the same dimensions.

jis-b-1051.sum: JIS B 1051 is the property classes of bolts, small screws, and studs (corresponding to ISO 898-1), and JIS B 1052-2 is the property classes of nuts (corresponding to ISO 898-2). The old JIS B 1052 is not in the current list.
facts: JIS B 1051: carbon steel and alloy steel bolts, small screws, and studs with specified property classes (coarse and fine thread, M1.6~M39 · M8×1~M39×3). The current edition transposed ISO 898-1:2013 without changes in technical content or structure.

JIS B 1052-2: nuts with specified property classes. The current edition transposed ISO 898-2:2022 without changes in technical content or structure, and has property classes 04 · 05 · 5 · 6 · 8 · 10 · 12 and styles 0 · 1 · 2.
The old "JIS B 1052" (mechanical properties of nuts) is not in the JISC current JIS list (a number search found only B 1052-2).
The 4T to 10T strengths of old-type nuts are now in JIS B 1181 附属書JB (normative).
Stainless steel is JIS B 1054-1 (bolts) and JIS B 1054-2 (nuts).
Domestically, KS B ISO 898-1 · 898-2 (IDT of old ISO editions) and the KS-specific KS B 0233 (steel bolts and small screws) and KS B 0234 (steel nuts, annex 4T to 12T) coexist.
watch: T markings such as 4T and 8T are old JIS series notation. Do not read them 1:1 as numeric strengths of the ISO 898 series.
KS B ISO 898-1 is based on an old ISO edition, so details may differ from the current ISO and JIS. Decide the edition to use for certificate evaluation.
Nut strength 9 in old materials is not in the current JIS B 1052-2 (ISO 898-2:2022). Choose the mating nut again on the basis of the current edition.
jis-b-1051.status: Current (the old JIS B 1052 is not in the current list)

jis-b-0205.sum: The Japanese metric thread is divided into JIS B 0205-1~4 (basic profile, overall system, selected sizes, basic dimensions), a composition corresponding to ISO 68-1 · 261 · 262 · 724. The old fine thread standard JIS B 0207 was withdrawn in 2001.
facts: JIS B 0205 has a 4-part composition: -1 basic profile, -2 overall system, -3 selected sizes for threaded parts, -4 basic dimensions.
JIS B 0205-2 is shown as identical (IDT) to ISO 261 (note on cited standards in JIS B 1176).
Coarse and fine threads are in the same system. The old JIS B 0207 (metric fine threads, 1982 edition) was withdrawn in 2001-12 (JSA catalog).
The tolerances are JIS B 0209-1~5, and there are separate parts for tolerances for hot-dip galvanized thread combinations (-4 · -5).
The domestic correspondence is KS B 0201 (coarse) · KS B 0204 (fine) · KS B 0211 · 0214 (tolerances).
watch: Read the "JIS B 0207" fine thread notation on an old drawing as the current system after checking diameter × pitch.
For a line that does not state the fine thread pitch, decide the pitch.
Hot-dip galvanized bolt and nut combinations use separate tolerances, such as JIS B 0209-4 · -5.
jis-b-0205.status: Current (JIS B 0207 is not in the current list)

jis-b-2220.sum: Japanese steel pipe flange standard. It covers nominal pressures 5K · 10K · 10K thin type · 16K · 20K · 30K · 40K · 63K and pipe nominal sizes 10A~1500A, and has no corresponding international standard. The bolts have metric threads.
facts: Scope: steel pipe flanges for general, pressure, high-pressure, high-temperature, alloy steel, and stainless steel piping. Nominal pressures 5K · 10K · 10K thin type · 16K · 20K · 30K · 40K · 63K, nominal sizes 10A~1500A.
2K flanges are in an informative annex.
There is no corresponding international standard (Introduction).
The items on precautions for use have a separate clause on "JIS B 1180 · 1181 main text (ISO type) bolts and nuts" (table of contents).
Even for the same pipe nominal size, the number and diameter of bolts may differ depending on the K designation. Check the number and nominal size of bolts in the standard table.
The domestic KS B 1511 · KS B 1503 also use the K designation.
watch: If ISO type (main text) bolts and nuts are used on JIS flanges, the M22 width across flats grows from 32 to 34 mm. Check for seat interference.
Do not assume that the bolt circle and number of holes are the same as for ASME B16.5 and EN 1092-1 flanges. Compare dimensions before mixing them.
Match fine-pitch bolts with nuts of the same pitch as the mate.
eq_notes: Domestic standards using the K designation (dimension comparison not included)

jis-hex-af.t: JIS width across flats (old JIS · ISO differences)
jis-hex-af.en_title: Differences in hex width across flats and height between old JIS (annex) and ISO
jis-hex-af.sum: Old JIS (now annex) type and ISO (now main text) type hex bolts and nuts differ in width across flats at M10, M12, M14, M22, and also differ in bolt head height and nut height. Products marked DIN 931 · 933 · 934 also usually have the same width across flats as old JIS.
facts: Width across flats (old JIS → ISO): M10 17 → 16, M12 19 → 18, M14 22 → 21, M22 32 → 34 mm. The other nominal sizes are the same. Products marked DIN usually have the old JIS values.
The old-type bolt head height is M10 7, M12 8, M14 9 mm, and ISO is 6.4 · 7.5 · 8.8 mm.
The old-type nut height is about 0.8d (M12 10 mm), and ISO style 1 has a higher maximum height of about 0.9D (M12 max 10.8 mm).
Japan moved the old standard to an annex at the 1985 revision, and the 2014 revision stated that it is preferable not to use it for new designs.
The width across flats series itself is specified separately by JIS B 1002 (二面幅の寸法) and KS B 1001 (width across flats dimensions).
watch: A site that uses a 17 mm tool on M10 bolts follows the old type. If ISO type 16 mm bolts get mixed in, the tool does not fit.
For M22, the ISO side is larger (34 mm). Check for interference with box wrenches, spot facing, and flange bolt seats.
Writing the width across flats in the BOM (e.g., "M10 s=17") prevents confusion between old-type and ISO type.

Main text type (IS) and annex type (JA) look similar on the outside and are easily mixed. The Japanese industry decided to put an identification projection mark around the top face of main text type bolt heads.
eq_notes: Withdrawn DIN. Products marked with it usually have the same width across flats as the old type
Main text ISO MOD + Annex A (annex dimensions not included)

t-f10t.en_title: Structural high-strength bolt grades F8T, F10T, S10T
t-f10t.sum: Grade markings of high-strength bolt sets for steel structures in Korea and Japan. F is the friction grip hex set, S is the torque-shear type set, and the number means the lower limit of tensile strength (× 100 MPa).
facts: Tensile strength by Japanese standards: F8T 800~1000, F10T · S10T 1000~1200 MPa. Proof strength (yield) is F8T 640, F10T · S10T 900 MPa or more.

F8T · F10T are the grade markings of KS B 1010 · JIS B 1186. S10T is the marking of the torque-shear type set; in Korea the KS B 2819 set is called this, and in Japan it is an association standard such as JSS II 09.
F10T specifies tensile strength as a range up to the upper limit, while ISO 10.9 specifies a minimum of 1040 MPa. They are not the same grade.

Japanese road bridges have not used F11T and above as new since 1980 because delayed fracture occurred. KS B 1010 added the 1300 MPa class F13T together with the delayed fracture test in the 2004 revision.

In the Japanese building field, there are the ultra-high-strength bolts F14T · S14T certified by the Minister of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism (tensile strength 1400, proof strength 1260 MPa or more).
watch: Do not replace an F10T set with general 10.9 hex bolts and nuts. The strength and torque coefficient requirements per set differ.
S10T and F10T sets have different tightening methods and are not interchanged.
The higher the strength, the more sensitive to hydrogen delayed fracture. Avoid pickling, electroplating, and corrosive environments, and if plating is needed, decide it at the design stage.
For a BOM that only says "HTB", check whether it is an F10T set or S10T, and the nominal size and length.

t-en10204-types.sum: A standard that divides inspection documents for metallic products into four types: 2.1, 2.2, 3.1, and 3.2. Type 2.x is non-specific inspection by the manufacturer's own procedure, and type 3.x is the specific inspection result of the delivered product (or its test unit); they differ in who confirms and signs.
facts: 2.1: The manufacturer only declares compliance with the order and gives no test values.

2.2: The manufacturer declares compliance and attaches test values, but they are representative values of products of the same standard and process (non-specific inspection), so they may not be values of the delivered lot.

3.1: The result of testing the delivered product or the test unit it belongs to (specific inspection), confirmed by the manufacturer's authorized inspection representative, independent of the manufacturing department.

3.2: A document prepared and confirmed jointly by the manufacturer's authorized inspection representative and the buyer's inspector (or an inspector designated by regulation); which type to receive is decided by the order conditions.

What to look at when receiving 3.1: whether the issuer is the manufacturer of that product, whether the name, title, and confirmation of the inspection representative are present, whether it connects to the delivered product by heat and lot number, and, if it is a copy, whether there are no alterations.

The manufacturer may transfer the specific inspection results of the material it used (primary (1st-stage) product) into 3.1 and 3.2. It must operate a traceability procedure and be able to produce the original document, and the standard gives this authority only to the manufacturer.

An intermediate distributor only passes on the original or a copy of the manufacturer's document without altering it, together with a means of identifying the product. The only thing that can be changed on a copy is the partial quantity actually delivered, and the original must be producible on request.
In the 2004 edition, 3.1.B became 3.1, 3.1.A · 3.1.C and the old 3.2 became 3.2, and 2.3 was dropped. The codes of the entries in steel documents (groups A · B · C · D · Z) follow EN 10168.
watch: A document made by a distributor retyping the manufacturer's certificate into its own format, or a copy with the issuer's name or address changed, is not EN 10204 3.1. Check whether it is a copy in which the original manufacturer's name and the inspection representative's confirmation remain as they are.

Read "3.1.B" or "DIN 50049 3.1B" in a drawing or specification as the current 3.1. "3.1.A" and "3.1.C" correspond to the current 3.2, so check whether the condition requires confirmation by the buyer's (or statutory) inspector.
If 2.2 is received instead of 3.1, the test values may not be values of the delivered lot. For items that need lot values, such as pressure-boundary bolting, write 3.1 in the purchase order.
For 3.2, the buyer's (or statutory) inspector confirms and signs together, so decide at the time of ordering who will be the inspector (inspection body).
ISO 16228 F3.1 is a test report for fasteners that a distributor can also issue, so its rule on the issuing party differs from EN 10204 3.1. Write in the purchase order which type of which standard.
eq_notes: International standard for inspection documents of steel and steel products (uses the 2.1 · 2.2 · 3.1 · 3.2 classification)
General rules for inspection of steel (MOD of the old edition of ISO 10474)
F2.1 · F2.2 · F3.1 · F3.2 dedicated to fasteners
German standard before EN 10204 ("3.1B" notation on drawings)

t-mtr.sum: The on-site term for a certificate issued by a steelmaker, material manufacturer, or bolt manufacturer stating the chemical composition and mechanical test values by heat. The document type (EN 10204 2.2, 3.1, etc.) is decided by the order, so first check who tested what, in what condition.
facts: A mill certificate has two layers: the material certificate of the steelmaker or bar manufacturer (heat composition, bar mechanical values) and the product certificate of the bolt or stud manufacturer (heat treatment lot, hardness, tensile, proof load, etc.).
Composition is a value per heat (melt), and mechanical values differ by heat treatment lot and diameter. Check that the diameter and lot on the certificate match the delivered product.

Order of reading: issuer · standard · grade · heat number → whether the composition is within the grade range → tensile · yield · elongation · reduction of area → hardness → impact (low-temperature grades) → heat treatment conditions → confirmation by the inspection representative.
watch: If there is only the bar steelmaker's mill certificate and no product test by the bolt manufacturer, the properties after heat treatment and thread machining are not guaranteed.
If copies of the same certificate keep being attached to multiple lots, compare the heat number and the marking one by one.
If plating or PTFE coating was applied later, the mill certificate gives the results before coating. Receive the coating certificate (including baking records for high-strength products) separately.
CMTR, MTC, and mill certificate differ only in name. Check the EN 10204 type and the issuing party rather than the name.
