t-pattern.t: Flange tightening sequence (star and cross pattern)
t-pattern.sum: ASME PCC-1 covers the legacy method of tightening flange bolts in a star (cross) sequence over several steps, and alternative methods with a changed sequence and number of tools. The % per step and the number of passes follow the procedure of the edition applied.
facts: Purpose: to compress the gasket evenly, keep the flange from tilting, and compensate over several passes for the elastic interaction in which a bolt tightened first is loosened by later bolts.

PCC-1 (2013 edition) provides the single-tool legacy star sequence (Table 4), its alternative sequences (Table 4.1, Appendix F), and an example of bolt grouping for large-diameter flanges (Figure 4). Use an alternative after verifying it on that joint.

Manufacturer and distributor procedure documents commonly give three steps in star (cross) sequence — first pass about 30 % or less, second pass in the range of 50 to 70 %, third pass 100 % — followed by circular passes at 100 %. The step % differs by document, such as 20 to 30/50 to 70 % or 30/60 %.
The circular pass is described not as a set number of times but as repeated until the nut no longer turns at the target torque.
watch: Each site understands "star pattern" differently. Number the bolts and write the sequence, step %, lubricant and torque unit together in the procedure.
A large-diameter flange with many bolts needs several final circular passes. Do not fix the number of passes in advance; leave it as "until the nut no longer turns".
Do not tighten a bolt to the target torque from the start — the documents keep the first pass at around 30 % or below.

t-tensioning.sum: A hydraulic tensioner pulls the stud directly in the axial direction and the nut is then run down by hand, giving preload without friction effects. The turn-of-nut method is a structural bolt method that produces preload by turning a set angle after snug-tight.
facts: Tensioning sequence: grip the stud end with the tool and pull hydraulically → turn the nut down while the stud is stretched → release the pressure. Nut torque is hardly used.

When the pressure is released, the nut threads and bearing face seat themselves and part of the preload is lost (load transfer loss). So it is pulled higher than the target, and the shorter the grip length, the greater the loss.

Turn-of-nut method (RCSC): after snug-tight, turn the nut 1/3 turn if the bolt length L ≤ 4d, 1/2 turn if 4d < L ≤ 8d, and 2/3 turn if 8d < L ≤ 12d (when both faces are normal to the bolt axis). Above 12d, it is set by testing.

The turn-of-nut method stretches the bolt threaded portion into the inelastic range, so the preload is more reliable than torque tightening. The RCSC rules apply only to structural joints where everything in the grip is steel (A325, A490, etc.), so they are not used for gasketed flanges.
watch: If the thread at the stud end for the tensioner is damaged, the tool will not go on. Use thread protection caps during transport and storage.
Do not use the turn-of-nut method angles as is for flange studs. Gasket compression is mixed into the angle and the preload will not be right.
RCSC (2025) prohibits reuse of A490 (Group 150) heavy hex bolts and of galvanized or coated bolts.

t-engagement.sum: The length over which the external and internal threads actually engage. It is set so that the bolt breaks before the internal thread strips. ISO hex nut height is at most about 0.9d, an inch heavy nut is about 1d, and the driven-in side of a DIN tap-end stud is about 1 to 2.5d.
facts: Design principle: make the stripping strength of the internal thread (nut, tapped hole) greater than the bolt breaking strength, so that the bolt breaks first in a visible way. The bolt and nut strength pairing of ISO 898-2 (a nut of class 8 or above for an 8.8 bolt) follows this principle.
ISO 4032 hex nut height is at most about 0.9d (M16 14.8 mm, M20 18 mm), and inch heavy nut height is nearly the same as the nominal diameter.
The driven-in side length (bm) of DIN tap-end studs is divided into about 1d (DIN 938, mainly steel base material), 1.25d (939), 2d (835) and 2.5d (940, mainly low-strength light metals).

The principle is that the stud or bolt end passes completely through the nut. For structural use (RCSC 2025), the bolt end flush with or beyond the outer face of the nut is regarded as sufficient thread engagement.

Thin nuts (ISO 4035, steel 04 and 05) have a lower load capacity than regular nuts and are not designed to prevent thread stripping. When used as jam nuts, they are assembled together with a regular or high nut.
Where thread strength is insufficient in a soft base material, supplement with a thread insert (coil insert) or a longer engagement.
watch: If a shortened bolt is put into a tapped hole in aluminum or cast iron, the thread strips. Keep the existing engagement depth.
In a blind hole, a few incomplete threads at the bottom do not count toward engagement. Look at the thread depth and the drill depth on the drawing separately.
If assembled so that the stud does not protrude from the nut, it may fail inspection. If the gasket or washer was changed, recalculate the length.
Hot-dip galvanized overtapped nuts have shallower engagement and lower strength. Pair them with the higher-grade nut the standard specifies.

t-across-flats.sum: The distance (s) between two opposite faces of a hex head or nut, which determines the tool size. Current ISO and the old ISO/R 272 (1962) differ at M10, M12, M14 and M22, and the inch heavy hex is 1/8" larger than the regular hex.
facts: Width across flats s and width across corners e: for an ideal regular hexagon, e = s / cos30° ≈ 1.155s. Actual products have chamfered corners and are slightly smaller than this.
The widths across flats in the old ISO/R 272 (1962) are M10 17, M12 19, M14 22, M22 32 mm, differing from current ISO 272 (16, 18, 21, 34 mm).
For inch regular hex it is 1.5D (3/4" → 1-1/8", ISO/R 272:1962 inch series), and for heavy hex it is 1.5D + 1/8" (3/4" → 1-1/4", RCSC 2025 Table C-2.1).
In KS, it is set by KS B 1001 (dimensions of width across flats).
watch: Drawings written with the withdrawn DIN 933 and 934 have been replaced by ISO 4017 and 4032 products, so recheck the width across flats when looking at tool and box wrench interference.
If a mm tool is used on an inch nut, it is loose or does not fit and the corners are rounded off (1-1/4" = 31.75 mm, 1-5/8" = 41.28 mm).
A heavy nut has a width across flats 1/8" larger than a regular nut of the same diameter, so the tool differs. When preparing sockets and tensioners, use the heavy basis.
Old JIS hex still has widths across flats that differ from ISO (see the JIS width across flats item).

t-heavy-hex.sum: The width across flats of an inch heavy hex is 1.5D + 1/8", which is 1/8" larger than the 1.5D of a regular hex, and the nut is thicker. Structural bolts and nuts (A325 and A490 bolts, A563 DH and A194 2H nuts) are heavy hex.
facts: Width across flats: heavy hex is 1.5D + 1/8" (3/4" → 1-1/4", 1" → 1-5/8", RCSC 2025 Table C-2.1), and regular hex is 1.5D (3/4" → 1-1/8", 1" → 1-1/2", ISO/R 272:1962 inch series).
Nut height: a heavy nut is slightly less than the nominal diameter (1" → 63/64", 1-1/2" → 1-15/32", RCSC 2025 Table C-2.1).

Structural bolts (F3125 A325 and A490) also have a heavy hex head, and the head width across flats is the same as that of the heavy nut. The mating nut is an A563 heavy nut (A194 2H can be used in its place), and the dimensions follow ASME B18.2.6 (RCSC 2025).
The wide bearing face lowers the pressure on the clamped surface, and the thick nut gives a long thread engagement. This is advantageous for high-load and high-temperature bolting.
watch: "Heavy" differs not only in width across flats but also in height. If a regular nut is used in place of a heavy nut, the engagement length is reduced.
Do not mix structural A325 bolts (heavy hex head) with A449 or SAE Gr 5 regular hex bolts. Head size, thread length and mating nut differ.
A 32 mm tool is loose on a 1-1/4" (31.75 mm) heavy nut. Use an inch tool.

t-stud-length.t: How to measure stud bolt length
t-stud-length.sum: Flange stud length is used as the first-thread-to-first-thread length with both end points (chamfers) excluded, per the B16.5 table, while a hex bolt (ISO 4014) is measured from under the head bearing face to the end.
facts: For a hex bolt (ISO 4014), the nominal length is from under the head bearing face to the end (including the chamfer).
Stud length in the B16.5 table is used as the first-thread-to-first-thread length, excluding the points. It differs from the overall length measured end to end.

ASME Interpretation 2-4 (covering B16.5-1988): the stud length in the table does not guarantee that 2 threads protrude beyond the nut. The table length is a value set by the calculation method in the B16.5 appendix (Annex F of the 1988 edition, Appendix C of the 2017 edition).
RF length examples: Class 150 NPS 8 is 4-1/4", Class 300 NPS 4 and 8 are 4-1/2" and 5-1/2", Class 600 NPS 4 is 5-3/4" (table).
watch: Check whether the BOM length is the overall length including points, or follows the flange standard's convention (points excluded, etc.).
Even among public charts, the same nominal length sometimes differs by 1/4" (example: Class 150 NPS 4 RF 3-1/2" and 3-3/4"). Check the chart's source and the edition it applies to.
When converting an inch length to mm and rounding (3.50" = 88.9 mm), do not shorten it arbitrarily. If it becomes shorter, the thread does not protrude beyond the nut.
Joints with tensioning allowance, insulating kits, thick gaskets, or wafer-type valves, spacers or orifice flanges cannot use the table length. Calculate separately.
If an RTJ flange is bought with the RF length, the engagement falls short.

t-flange-bolting.t: Determining flange bolt count and diameter (B16.5)
t-flange-bolting.sum: For B16.5 flanges, once the pressure class (Class) and nominal size (NPS) are set, the bolt count and diameter are fixed by a table. It is a value to look up, not to calculate, and the bolts differ if the Class differs even at the same NPS. Use the table value for stud length, but recheck it against the face type and joint configuration.
facts: B16.5 covers up to NPS 24. NPS 26 and above fall under B16.47, which has separate Series A and Series B.
EN 1092-1 (PN), KS and JIS (5K, 10K, 20K) flanges use metric bolts and a different bolt layout. Do not use the B16.5 table as is.
At the same NPS, as the Class goes up the bolts get thicker or more numerous: for NPS 4, Class 150 is 8 × 5/8", 300 is 8 × 3/4", and 600 is 8 × 7/8" (table).
All bolt counts in the table are multiples of 4.
ASME Interpretation B16.5-17-02: B16.5 (2013 edition) has no provision for using metric bolts.
The actual bolt area table in ORNL/Sub/2913-3 (NRC, 1976) also matches the bolt count and diameter for NPS 4, 8, 16 and 24.
watch: If the BOM has only NPS and no Class, the bolts cannot be determined. Get the Class together with the face type (RF, RTJ).
Set quantity: studs = bolt count × number of joints, and nuts are twice that.

t-rf-rtj.t: RF and RTJ face types and stud length
t-rf-rtj.sum: RF has a gasket fitted on a raised face, and RTJ has a metal ring (R, RX and BX types of ASME B16.20) fitted in a groove. Confirm the ring number and stud length from the table of the applicable flange standard.
facts: RTJ rings come in R, RX and BX types, and the pipe size that fits each type is set by a table (ASME B16.20).
RF raised face height: Class 150 and 300 are 1/16" (converted 1.6 mm), Class 600 is 1/4" (converted 6.4 mm).
ASME Interpretation B16.5-18-07 (covering B16.5-2009): B16.5 sets no tolerance on RF height.
For the same Class and NPS, RTJ studs are often longer than RF. Example: Class 150 NPS 8 is RF 4-1/4", RTJ 4-3/4".
For Class 150 NPS 1/2 and 3/4, public charts have no RTJ stud length.
ASME Interpretation 2-34 (covering B16.1-1989 and B16.5-1988): bolting an RF flange to a flat-face (FF) flange is not prohibited.
watch: If an RTJ flange is bought with the RF length, nut engagement falls short. Write the face type in the BOM.
An RTJ ring must match both the type (R, RX, BX) and the number. Check the bolt BOM and the ring BOM together.
When flanges with different RF heights (1/16" and 1/4") are mated, the table length does not fit. Recalculate the length.
For joints mating RF and FF (cast iron or non-metallic flanges, etc.), review the gasket type and bolt tightening conditions separately.

t-clearance.sum: ISO 273 sets clearance holes for metric bolts in three series: fine (f), medium (m) and coarse (c). For M16: 17 · 17.5 · 18.5 mm.
facts: Hole tolerances of the three series (for reference): fine H12, medium H13, coarse H14.
The inside diameter (minimum) of ISO 7089 plain washers is the same as the ISO 273 fine-series hole up to M36 (M12 13, M16 17, M20 21 mm).
The coarse series is used where position error is large, such as castings and welded structures, and the bearing face is reduced, so consider a washer.
Inch bolt holes follow ASME B18.2.8. The standard hole for steel structures, per RCSC, is bolt diameter + 1/16" for bolts under 1" and + 1/8" for 1" and over.
A clearance-hole bolt does not locate position. If position or shear must be taken by the bolt, use a reamer bolt (fitted bolt) or a dowel pin.
watch: Changing the bolt by looking only at the drawing hole may not fit: a 7/8" (22.23 mm) bolt does not fit in an M20 medium hole (22 mm).
Fastening without a washer in a coarse-series hole raises bearing pressure and increases embedding and loosening.
The "bolt diameter + 1 mm" practice is the same as the ISO fine series for M12 to M45, but differs for small screws (M10 fine 10.5 mm).

t-full-partial.sum: A fully threaded bolt (ISO 4017, DIN 933) is threaded up to the head, while a partially threaded bolt (ISO 4014, DIN 931) has only the thread length b cut and the rest is shank. The shear, fatigue and engagement positions differ, so check when substituting one for the other.
facts: ISO 4014 thread length b (reference values): 2d + 6 for L ≤ 125 mm, 2d + 12 for 125 < L ≤ 200, and 2d + 25 for L > 200. Example: M16 × 100 → b = 38 mm.

When the shank is at the shear plane, it resists with the shank cross-sectional area and is stronger than the threaded portion. Steel structure design also divides strength by whether the thread is in the shear plane (N) or not (X).
The shank of a partially threaded bolt has a long stretching length, which is advantageous for preload retention and fatigue. A reduced-shank bolt enhances this effect further.
ISO 4014 has a minimum length for each diameter (example: M16 is 65 mm); for shorter lengths, use the ISO 4017 fully threaded bolt (ISO 4014:2022).
watch: If a shear connection bolt is replaced with a fully threaded one, the thread falls in the shear plane and strength drops.

If a partially threaded bolt is replaced by shortening only the length, the threaded portion may be buried inside the plate and the nut cannot be tightened fully. Check the grip length and b together.
If the BOM does not distinguish fully and partially threaded, an unwanted type may arrive. Distinguish them by writing the ISO 4014/4017 (DIN 931/933) number.

t-product-grade.t: Product grades A, B and C
t-product-grade.sum: These are the dimensional tolerance grades of ISO 4759-1, where A is the most precise and C the coarsest. They are a different concept from property class (8.8) or ASTM Grade A.
facts: Product grade refers to the precision of dimensional and form tolerances (shank diameter, width across flats, head height, perpendicularity, etc.). It is unrelated to strength.
ISO 4014 and 4017 hex bolts: A if d ≤ 24 mm and L ≤ 10d or 150 mm (whichever is shorter), B if thicker or longer.
ISO 4032 hex nuts: A for M16 and below, B above.

Grade C: ISO 4016 (partially threaded) and 4018 (fully threaded) bolts, ISO 4034 nuts, ISO 7091 washers. Thread tolerances are also coarse: 8g for bolts (6g for property class 8.8 and above), 7H for nuts.
"Grade A" in an inch BOM may be a material or strength grade such as ASTM A307 Grade A, not an ISO product grade.
watch: Look at the context of "Grade A" in a BOM: check whether it is ISO product grade A or ASTM A307 or A563 Grade A.
Using a Grade C bolt in a precision assembly (fitted hole, tight space) may cause interference due to dimensional deviation.

t-inch-mm.t: Inch ↔ mm conversion and fraction notation
t-inch-mm.sum: 1 in = 25.4 mm (defined value). Bolt diameters are written in fractional inches, and the hyphen in 1-1/4" joins the whole number and the fraction.
facts: "1-1/4"" is 1 and 1/4 = 1.25" = 31.75 mm. The hyphen is not a minus but joins the whole number and the fraction.
Common unit conversions: 1 in² = 645.16 mm², 1 ksi = 6.895 MPa, 1 lbf = 4.448 N, 1 lbf·ft = 1.356 N·m.
The pipe nominal size NPS (inch) is not the bolt diameter. The bolt diameter of an NPS 4 flange is looked up separately in the flange standard table.
watch: Do not round 3/4" bolts to "19 mm" or 1" to "25 mm". Use the inch nominal size as it is (3/4" = 19.05 mm).
Check whether a "4-inch bolt" means the bolt diameter, a bolt for an NPS 4 flange, or a length of 4".
"1.1/4", "1 1/4" and "1-1/4" are the same value. It is sometimes mis-transcribed as the decimal "1.14".

t-thread-gauge.sum: External threads are inspected with ring gauges and internal threads with plug gauges. The GO gauge must enter all the way, and the NOT GO gauge fails if it enters more than the specified number of turns. A pitch gauge checks only the thread spacing.
facts: The GO gauge checks the maximum material dimension (the thickest side for a bolt) with a full thread form. It must turn in by hand over the entire thread length.
The NOT GO gauge checks the minimum material limit of the pitch diameter. Because its thread crests are truncated, it engages only at the pitch diameter.
Standards: metric ISO 1502 (gauges and gauging), inch ASME B1.2 (gauges) and ASME B1.3 (acceptability gauging systems).
A pitch gauge (thread gauge) only identifies pitch or TPI and is not an acceptance tool.

For plated parts, the point of inspection matters. The maximum dimension of an inch 2A thread applies to the part before plating, and the basic dimension to the part after plating (NIST H28). Hot-dip galvanized overtapped nuts are judged to 6AZ and 6AX (ISO 965-5).
Gauges also need calibration certificates, and wear skews the judgment.
watch: Do not judge "OK" by holding only a pitch gauge to the thread. A short contact cannot distinguish 1.5 mm from 16 TPI, and the diameter and tolerance are not checked.
State in the order or inspection plan whether inspection is based on before or after plating.
If the GO ring does not go in, separate the cause into thread damage, excess plating or pitch error. Do not force it on.
When a hot-dip galvanized bolt is inspected with a standard 6g ring gauge, it is normal for it to fail. Judge it by the mating nut method (overtap).

t-self-loosening.sum: The main cause of vibration loosening is transverse slip at the joint interface. The best countermeasure is sufficient preload so that no slip occurs, and anti-loosening parts come next. A split spring washer has almost no anti-loosening effect.
facts: There are two kinds of loosening: ① Rotational loosening: when the joint interface slips transversely, the friction on the thread flanks and bearing face momentarily disappears and the nut turns. ② Preload loss without rotation: embedding (settlement), gasket relaxation, creep, temperature.
Anti-loosening performance is compared by a transverse vibration test (Junker test, DIN 65151). The result is for comparison under the same conditions and is not a guaranteed value in actual use.
Basic countermeasures: sufficient and even preload, long grip (a bolt with more elasticity), a hard and flat bearing face, hardened washers.
Prevailing torque nuts (nylon insert and all-metal) follow the ISO 2320 performance requirements and slow rotation. Nylon insert nuts have a temperature limit and a reuse restriction.
DIN 127 (spring washer) was withdrawn with no successor standard. NASA-STD-5020 holds that a split spring washer has almost no anti-loosening effect.
Split pins and castle nuts, wire locking and tab washers prevent the nut from coming off but do not prevent preload loss.
watch: A split spring washer has almost no anti-loosening effect (NASA-STD-5020). Start with preload management for loosening countermeasures.
Even with an anti-loosening nut, it loosens if preload is insufficient. Torque control comes first.
Leakage in flange bolting is usually a problem of gasket relaxation or uneven preload rather than loosening. Respond with a re-tightening procedure.
Serrated flange nuts and bolts scratch the bearing face and damage painted or plated surfaces, and their effect is reduced on a hardened washer.

t-fatigue.sum: Bolt fatigue arises when cyclic load acts on the stress concentration at the thread root. The fatigue amplitude limit of a thread is tens of MPa, almost independent of strength grade, so the remedy is preload, stiffness and bending control rather than higher strength.
facts: Failure occurs most often at the first thread engaged by the nut, followed by the thread runout (incomplete thread portion) and the radius under the head.

With sufficient preload, the share of the external cyclic load carried by the bolt becomes small, Φ·P. If preload is insufficient and the joint interface opens, the whole load acts on the bolt and life drops sharply.

Fatigue limit amplitude of bolts rolled before heat treatment (VDI 2230): σASV ≈ 0.85 × (150/d + 45) MPa (d in mm). M16 ≈ 46 MPa, M24 ≈ 44 MPa. It is set by diameter alone and is almost independent of strength grade.
Rolled threads retain compressive stress at the root surface and resist fatigue cracks (NASA RP-1228). The formula above is based on bolts rolled before heat treatment.

Improvements: high and even preload, lowering bolt stiffness with long, slender (reduced-shank) bolts, rounded root (UNR, UNJ), eliminating bending with a parallel bearing face or spherical washer, preventing fretting on contact surfaces.
The axial load fatigue test method is ISO 3800.
A fatigue fracture surface shows streaks spreading from the origin (beach marks) and the final fracture zone.
watch: Replacing a fatigue-failed bolt with one a grade higher in strength usually does not solve it. Look first at insufficient preload, bending and stiffness causes.
Hot-dip galvanizing and some coatings can lower fatigue strength. Check when adding a coating to rotating machinery bolting.
For bolts of rotating machinery couplings, connecting rods and bearing caps, check the reuse count and elongation criteria in the equipment manual.
Do not substitute a general-purpose bolt for a bolt specified "rolled after heat treatment" on the drawing.

t-gasket-seating.sum: Flange bolts must withstand, at first, the seating load that compresses the gasket to fill the face and, during operation, both the force of internal pressure separating the flange and the residual compression of the gasket. Gasket stress = total bolt load / gasket area.
facts: Gasket stress σg = n·F / Ag (n number of bolts, F preload of 1 bolt, Ag effective gasket contact area).

Flange calculation in the ASME pressure vessel code (Section VIII Div.1 Appendix 2, etc.): operating load Wm1 = (π/4)G²P + 2b·π·G·m·P, seating load Wm2 = π·b·G·y (G gasket reaction diameter, b effective width, m·y gasket factors).
Required bolt area Am = max(Wm1 / Sb, Wm2 / Sa) (Sb allowable stress at design temperature, Sa at ambient temperature). Here the bolt area is based on the root diameter.

m·y is an old method but is still used in Section VIII Appendix 2. EN 1591-1 calculates with gasket values (Qmin, Qsmax, etc.) obtained by EN 13555 tests, and ASME PCC-1 covers in Appendix O how to determine the assembly bolt stress.
Insufficient bolt load causes leakage; excessive load causes over-compression of spiral wound gaskets, flange rotation and bolt yielding.
watch: If the bolt grade is lowered (B7 → B8 Class 1) or the gasket type is changed, review the bolt and gasket combination again.
Do not apply the same torque table as is to a different gasket (PTFE, graphite, spiral wound, RTJ). The target gasket stress differs.
If the gasket thickness changes, redetermine both stud length and torque.
If even one bolt is under-tightened, the gasket stress there falls short and leaks. Even preload is the key.

t-tap-drill.sum: The pilot hole for a cutting tap on a metric thread is roughly d − P (ISO 2306: M12 → 10.2 mm, M16 → 14 mm). ISO 2306 also gives mm drills for UNC and UNF inch threads (1/2"-13 → 10.8 mm).
facts: ISO 2306 sets the drill diameter before tapping a parallel thread of normal engagement length, and the drill diameter is roughly the nominal diameter − pitch.
Metric coarse thread (ISO 2306): M6 5.0, M8 6.8, M10 8.5, M12 10.2, M16 14.0, M20 17.5, M24 21.0 mm. Fine thread M16×1.5 → 14.5 mm.
ISO 2306 also gives mm drills for inch threads: 1/4"-20 5.1, 1/2"-13 10.8, 3/4"-10 16.5, 1"-8 22.25 mm.
A larger drill reduces thread height and lowers pull-out strength, and a smaller one makes the tap likely to break.
A forming tap (roll tap) pushes the material to form the thread, so it uses a larger pilot hole than a cutting tap. Follow the tool data for the values.
watch: When using a mm drill for an inch tapped hole, use the ISO 2306 values (e.g., 1/2"-13 → 10.8 mm, 3/4"-10 → 16.5 mm) instead of approximations.
Set the depth of a blind tapped hole as thread depth + incomplete thread at the tap end + drill point allowance.
Do not mix forming-tap pilot holes and cutting-tap pilot holes.

p-hex-bolt.t: Hex bolt (Hex bolt · Hex cap screw)
p-hex-bolt.sum: In a BOM, "hex bolt" maps to ISO 4014 (partially threaded) and ISO 4017 (fully threaded) for metric, and to hex bolt and hex cap screw of ASME B18.2.1 for inch. Thread, length, strength and surface treatment must be stated together to make an order specification.
facts: Metric hex bolts divide into partially threaded ISO 4014 (formerly DIN 931) and fully threaded ISO 4017 (formerly DIN 933). KS B 1002 and JIS B 1180 are national standards of the same family.
In the titles of ISO 4014 (hexagon head bolts) and ISO 4017 (hexagon head screws), "bolt" refers to partially threaded and "screw" to fully threaded.
ASME B18.2.1 treats hex bolt and hex cap screw as separate products with separate dimension tables. This is different from the partially/fully threaded distinction.
Length L is measured from the underside of the head (bearing face) to the end of the thread (ISO 4014 Figure 1).
Thread length b of ISO 4014 partially threaded bolts is 2d + 6 for l ≤ 125 mm, 2d + 12 for 125 < l ≤ 200, and 2d + 25 mm for l > 200.
Strength is specified by ISO 898-1 for metric steel (4.6, 4.8, 8.8, 10.9, etc.), ISO 3506-1 for stainless steel (A2-70, A4-80, etc.), and SAE J429 Grade 2, 5, 8 or ASTM A307, A449, A354 for inch.
ISO 4014 and 4017 and DIN 931 and 933 differ in width across flats for M10, M12, M14 and M22: ISO 16, 18, 21, 34 mm; DIN 17, 19, 22, 32 mm.
watch: Ask back, together with the length, for lines without "partially threaded" or "fully threaded" notation. Below the standard minimum length no partially threaded bolt exists, so it comes as fully threaded (example: M12 partially threaded starts from 50 mm).
Do not translate English "HEX CAP SCREW" as "fully threaded". For inch cap screws too, partially threaded is the default when long.
If an ISO product is sent against a line marked DIN 931 or 933, the tool size changes for M10, M12, M14 and M22.
For inch lines without a thread count, do not assume UNC; confirm. UNC and UNF do not mate.
For zinc electroplating or black zinc plating on 10.9 and above, check on the certificate whether hydrogen embrittlement baking was done.

p-heavy-hex-bolt.sum: A bolt whose head width across flats is larger than that of a hex bolt of the same nominal size. For inch general use it is ASME B18.2.1 heavy hex, for structural use ASME B18.2.6 + ASTM F3125, and metric mainly comes from structural set standards.
facts: Even among heavy hex, the bolt type (heavy hex bolt) and the screw type (heavy hex screw) are treated in separate dimension tables in ASME B18.2.1.
ASTM A307 Grade B is a grade for cast iron flange piping joints, and its default mating nut is A563 Grade A heavy hex (A307-21).

Structural heavy hex bolts (F3125 A325 and A490) have ASME B18.2.6 dimensions, a shorter threaded portion than general-purpose bolts, and the same head width across flats as the heavy nut (RCSC 2025).

ISO general hex bolts (ISO 4014 and 4017) have the normal-series width across flats, and metric bolts with a larger width across flats come mainly from structural standards (EN 14399, ISO 7412 withdrawn in 2006).
watch: For lines with only "HEAVY HEX BOLT", confirm whether it is structural (F3125 A325 and A490) or general (A307 Grade B and A354), and whether it is bolt type or screw type.
Do not substitute SAE Grade 5 and 8 hex cap screws for structural bolts. Thread length, mating nut and test requirements differ.
Heavy bolts are usually paired with heavy nuts. State the nut shape (hex, heavy) and grade together.
For metric "heavy bolt" notation, the width across flats basis differs by standard (example: EN 14399-4 HV M20 is 32 mm). Match to the dimensions of the stated standard.

p-stud-bolt.sum: A bolt threaded over its whole length without a head, which tightens a flange with 2 nuts. For inch piping, the basis is ASME B18.31.2 form, ASTM A193 B7 + A194 2H material, and the ASME B16.5 length table.
facts: "STUD BOLT" in a plant BOM usually means one set of 1 continuous thread stud + 2 heavy hex nuts.
Form standards are ASME B18.31.2 for inch and ASME B18.31.1M for metric, and for general metric use DIN 976-1 stud bolts are also used.
Material is specified by ASTM A193 (high-temperature and general), A320 (low-temperature) and A453 (high-temperature austenitic flange) grades. The most common combination is A193 B7 + A194 2H.
The specified minimum tensile strength of B7, 125 ksi (about 862 MPa, converted), is the value for the normal diameter range. Values drop for thick diameters, so check the current A193 table.
watch: For lines with only "stud bolt", distinguish whether it is a continuous thread stud for flanges or a tap-end stud driven into a tapped hole at one end.
Ask back if the number of nuts and the nut grade are missing. B7 + 2H is a common combination, but the nut grade must be written separately in the order.
Plant bolting over 1" uses a mix of UNC and 8UN (8 threads per inch), which do not mate with each other, so check the thread count in the BOM.
Check the length basis (whether both end points are included) in the drawing or standard. Studs for hydraulic tensioners have a longer extra thread.
A stud made from SCM440, SNB7 or 42CrMo4 may be marked B7 only if it satisfies all B7 composition and test requirements.

p-double-end-stud.sum: A stud with an unthreaded shank in the middle and threads at both ends. Tap-end types, with one end driven into a tapped hole in the body, are specified by DIN 938, 939, 835 and 940, KS B 1037, JIS B 1173, and for inch ASME B18.31.2.
facts: DIN tap-end studs are divided by the thread length on the driven end (bm): DIN 938 ≈1d, DIN 939 ≈1.25d, DIN 835 ≈2d, DIN 940 ≈2.5d.
The driven-end length is chosen by the base material: DIN 938 (≈1d) is mainly for steel, and DIN 940 (≈2.5d) is for light metals of lower strength.

Inch double-end studs fall under ASME B18.31.2, with types having equal thread length at both ends and types with a different tap end. An interference-fit thread (ASME B1.12 Class 5) is sometimes used on the tap end.
They are widely used as basic fastening parts for pump casings, bearing housings, seal glands and valve bonnets.
The KS standard title is KS B 1037 "stud bolt", and JIS is B 1173 "植込みボルト (bolt to be planted)".
watch: Confirm from the drawing whether the order length is the overall length or the length excluding the driven end.
Thread tolerances on the driven end and the nut end may differ (inch Class 5 interference fit). Take the drawing notation as is.
"Double-thread bolt" is a term used for both continuous thread studs and double-end studs, so check for a shank and the thread length on both sides.
If the tapped thread in the body is damaged, consider a thread insert repair before replacing it with a stud of the same nominal size.

p-threaded-rod.sum: A rod threaded over its whole length. Metric is specified by DIN 976-1 (DIN 975 is withdrawn), inch by ASME B18.31.3 form with material grades such as ASTM A193 B7, A307 and F1554.
facts: "Jeonsan" is a field term meaning fully threaded. It is used as stock for hangers, anchor connections, chemical anchor rods and field-cut studs.
DIN 975 (threaded rod) is withdrawn, and no replacement standard is shown in DIN Media. The current DIN 976-1 has Form A and B.
Metric steel threaded rods are specified by ISO 898-1 property classes (4.8, 8.8, etc.), and stainless steel by ISO 3506-1 (A2-70, A4-70, etc.).

A193 B7 strength also applies to B7 threaded rod. The specified minimum tensile strength of 125 ksi (about 862 MPa, converted) is the value for the normal diameter range, and thick diameters should be checked against the current A193 table.
watch: If the length is missing, as in "threaded rod M12", confirm whether it is standard length (full bar) or cut length.
For inch hanger rod, match the thread form (Whitworth, UNC) to the nuts, anchors and coupling nuts.
Use overtapped nuts and coupling nuts for hot-dip galvanized threaded rod. A regular nut may not go on.
Inch standard-length threaded rod may have different thread classes, so specify the thread class when cutting it for use as a flange stud.
Specify F1554 for anchor use. The old Grade C of A307 (for anchors) was replaced by F1554 Grade 36 (A307-21).
eq_notes: Metric stud bolt and threaded rod (DIN 975 is withdrawn)

p-shcs.t: Socket head cap screw (hex socket head bolt)
p-shcs.sum: A bolt with a hex socket in a cylindrical head. Specified by metric ISO 4762 (DIN 912, KS B 1003, JIS B 1176) and inch ASME B18.3 + ASTM A574 (alloy steel) and F837 (stainless steel).
facts: Length L is measured from the underside of the head to the end.
Metric property classes are 8.8, 10.9 and 12.9, and ISO 4762:1997 Table 2 sets the thread tolerance of 12.9 at 5g6g and the others at 6g.
ASME B18.3 retains the dimensions of the old 1936 series socket head cap screws in a separate appendix, so check the 1936 series on old drawings separately from the current dimensions.
watch: Electro-galvanizing of 12.9 has a high hydrogen embrittlement risk, so black oxide is the default. If plating is needed, check the baking conditions on the certificate or switch to zinc flake.
"CAP SCREW" alone in an inch BOM does not tell whether it is a hex cap screw (hex head) or a socket head cap screw, so ask back.
For lines with a sour service requirement (NACE MR0175/ISO 15156), first check the hardness suitability of high-strength socket head cap screws (A574, 12.9).
M14 is a non-preferred (in parentheses) size in ISO 4762, and M18 and M22 are not in the ISO 4762 table.

p-csk.sum: A socket head cap screw whose conical head sits flush with the member surface. Specified by metric ISO 10642 (90°, formerly DIN 7991) and inch ASME B18.3 + ASTM F835 (usually 82°), and the length is measured from the top of the head.
facts: Length is from the top of the head to the end (overall length). This differs from a general socket head cap screw, which is measured from under the head.
The countersink angle is 90° for metric ISO 10642 and usually 82° for inch, so the countersinks do not match.
Because of the head shape the load capacity is low, so a 0 is placed before the property class (example: 010.9).
From the 2019 edition of ISO 10642, the thread length of M14–M20 partially threaded screws is increased to 3d.
Inch ASTM F835 (alloy steel) covers up to 1-1/2", and F879 (stainless steel) covers up to 5/8".
The wrench size is smaller than that of a socket head cap screw of the same diameter (M8: socket head cap screw 6 mm, countersunk 5 mm).
watch: "Sara bolt" often refers to a countersunk socket head cap screw, but it may also be a Phillips countersunk machine screw or a square-neck countersunk bolt, so confirm the drive (hex socket, Phillips).
Do not calculate a countersunk bolt with the same load as a 10.9 socket head cap screw of the same diameter.
If a metric 90° bolt is put into an inch drawing part (82° seat), the head does not fit.
A 100° countersunk head (common in aerospace standards, etc.) does not fit 90° and 82° seats.

p-button.sum: A bolt with a low round head and a hex socket. Specified by metric ISO 7380-1 (ISO 7380-2 for the flanged type) and KS B 1067, and inch ASME B18.3 + ASTM F835 and F879; it is for light fastening.
facts: Length is measured from under the head to the end.
The standard treats it as a bolt with low load capacity. Where large clamping force is needed, use a general socket head cap screw (ISO 4762).
The wrench size is smaller than that of a socket head cap screw of the same diameter (M8: socket head cap screw 6 mm, button 5 mm).
ISO 7380-2 is a flanged type with a disc (collar) under the head.
In the 2022 edition of ISO 7380-1, the thread length of M16 partially threaded screws is increased to 48 mm (3d).
Inch button heads cover 0.060–0.625" (5/8") for both ASTM F835 (alloy steel) and F879 (stainless steel).
watch: A "round head bolt" without a hex socket may be a pan head machine screw or a carriage bolt, so check the drive.
It is for light fastening such as guards, covers and hinges. Replacing a socket head cap screw location with a button bolt may give insufficient clamping force.
Inch button heads above 5/8" are outside the scope of F835 and F879.

p-set-screw.sum: A headless screw with only a hex socket, which presses on a shaft with its end to fix pulleys and couplings. Specified by ISO 4026 to 4029 (DIN 913 to 916) by point shape for metric, and ASME B18.3 + ASTM F912 for inch.
facts: Each point shape has a different standard number (table below). For lines without a point shape, the distribution practice is to treat it as cup point.
Length is measured as the overall length, end to end.
The strength of steel set screws is indicated not by tensile strength but by hardness class (ISO 898-5, e.g., 45H), and for stainless steel by ISO 3506-3 classes (e.g., A2-21H, A4-21H).
A set screw is not for carrying tensile load.
Inch stainless steel ASTM F880 covers socket set screws 0.060–1.000" (F880-24), and alloy steel is specified by ASTM F912.
KS B 1028 (hex socket set screw) and JIS B 1177 are national standards of the same family.
watch: Ask back if the point shape is missing, as in "set screw M8×10". If it is treated as cup point, write it that way and have it confirmed.
A 45H steel set screw is a part that carries no tensile load, so ISO 4042:2022 does not require baking after electroplating. State the plating specification in the order.
Even with the same thread count, UNC (60°) and Whitworth thread (55°) have different thread angles and do not mate.
Nylon patch, soft tip, square head and slotted set screws are separate items, so get their specifications separately.
Dog point has a longer minimum length than cup and flat points.

p-hex-nut.sum: The basic nut that mates with a bolt. Specified by metric ISO 4032 (style 1), 4033 (style 2) and 4035 (thin nut), DIN 934, KS B 1012, JIS B 1181, and inch ASME B18.2.2 + ASTM A563 and SAE J995.
facts: Nut strength is matched to the bolt: 8.8 bolt → property class 8, 10.9 → class 10, 12.9 → class 12 nut (ISO 898-2).
ISO 4032 and DIN 934 differ in width across flats for M10, M12, M14 and M22: ISO 16, 18, 21, 34 mm; DIN 17, 19, 22, 32 mm.
The current edition of ISO 4032 (2023) puts requirements such as property class only on M5–M39, and other sizes are covered in Annex A.
The tall nut (style 2) is ISO 4033, and the fine thread nut is ISO 8673.
Thin nuts (ISO 4035, formerly DIN 439-2) have low load capacity and are marked with property class 04 or 05; they are for double nuts and position locking.
Inch hex nut dimensions are in ASME B18.2.2, and the material grade is specified separately, such as ASTM A563 or SAE J995.
watch: For "hex nut M20" without a strength, check against the mating bolt strength.
For hot-dip galvanized bolts, use overtapped nuts, whose threads are re-cut after plating, as the mate.
For lines with only "jam nut", sort by thread: metric is the thin nut (ISO 4035), inch is the jam nut or heavy jam nut of ASME B18.2.2.
If an ISO 4032 product is sent against a line marked DIN 934, the tool size changes for M10, M12, M14 and M22.
Even at the same diameter, UNC, UNF and 8UN do not mate with each other. Always check the thread count for inch nuts.

p-heavy-hex-nut.sum: A nut whose width across flats and height are larger than those of a hex nut of the same nominal size. Grades are set by ASTM A194 (2H, etc.) for plant studs and A563 DH for structural use, and dimensions use ASME B18.2.2 (inch) and B18.2.6M (metric, successor to the withdrawn B18.2.4.6M).
facts: Inch heavy hex nut widths across flats are 7/8" for 1/2", 1-1/4" for 3/4", and 1-5/8" for 1" (RCSC 2025 Table C-2.1, ASME B18.2.6).
Inch heavy nut height is almost the same as the nominal diameter (example: 1" → 63/64").

A194 2H is a carbon steel nut grade commonly paired with B7 studs (quenched and tempered, per public material from manufacturers and distributors). 2HM and 7M are grades with hardness limited to a low value, used in sour environments, etc.
Even for the same M20, the width across flats of the ISO 272 large series is 34 mm, and that of the normal series (ISO 4032) is 30 mm.
A194 does not allow grade substitution without purchaser approval. Obtain approval when replacing a grade in an old specification with another grade.
A563 DH is used as the mating nut of structural bolts (F3125 A325 and A490), and A194 2H may be substituted for it (RCSC 2025 2.3).
watch: If a "2H nut" is received in regular hex shape, the tool, bearing face and proof load differ. Check shape (heavy) and grade together.
Order an impact-tested nut as the mate of an L7 stud for low temperature (A320 1.4).
Hot-dip galvanized nuts are overtapped after plating, so use them only as a set with the stud.
The nuts of metric structural sets (EN 14399-4 HV) are M12 22 mm and M20 32 mm, which differ from the ISO 272 large series (21 and 34 mm), so do not mix them.

p-lock-nut.sum: A nut that creates friction against the thread (loosening torque) by itself. Specified by nylon insert types ISO 7040 and 10511 (DIN 982 and 985), all-metal types ISO 7042 and 7719 (DIN 980), KS B 1044, and for inch ASME B18.16.6.
facts: In the nylon insert type, the nylon ring at the top of the nut presses on the threads to create loosening torque. The normal type is ISO 7040 (DIN 982) and the low type is ISO 10511 (DIN 985).

The all-metal type creates loosening torque by deforming the upper part of the nut, and is used in high-temperature areas where nylon cannot be used: ISO 7042 (tall type), ISO 7719 (normal type), ISO 10513 (fine thread tall type). DIN 980 was replaced by ISO 7042 and 10513.
Loosening torque performance is tested by ISO 2320.
Loosening torque arises only when the bolt end passes completely through the nylon ring (locking part).
KS B 1044 is the hex nut of the prevailing torque type with a non-metallic insert, and KS B 1068 is the standard for mechanical properties and performance of prevailing torque steel nuts.
Inch prevailing torque nuts are in ASME B18.16.6 (Prevailing Torque Locknuts, Inch Series).
watch: Ask back for "nylon nut" lines without a type (normal, low).
For lines with only "lock nut", check which one in the table above it is.
The nylon ring is weak at high temperature. Consider the all-metal type for high-temperature areas, and check the service temperature by material and plating.
For a disassembled prevailing torque nut, the loosening torque generally decreases, so replacing it with a new nut is recommended.

p-flange-nut.sum: A hex nut with a disc (flange) acting as a washer on the bearing face. Specified by ISO 4161 and EN 1661 (formerly DIN 6923), KS B 1043, and for inch ASME B18.2.2, and the presence of serrations is decided together.
facts: The wide bearing face acts as a washer, so sheet metal and frames are fastened without a washer.
The width across flats of the ISO 4161 M10 flange nut is 15 mm, which differs from the regular hex nut (ISO 4032, 16 mm).
ISO 4161 is style 2 height and covers coarse thread M5–M20.
The serrated type has bearing-face teeth that bite into the mating surface to reduce loosening, but it scratches painted surfaces and thin plates.
The mating bolt is the hex flange bolt ISO 4162, EN 1665 (formerly DIN 6921), KS B 1042.
The inch serrated flange locknut is ASME B18.16.4.
watch: Ask back for lines without serration information.
The serrated type is generally not used on painted surfaces, thin plates or hardened washers.
The width across flats of M10 is 15 mm, so it differs from the regular hex tool (16 mm).
"FLANGE BOLT·NUT" in an English BOM often means pipe flange bolting (B7, 2H). If a grade (2H) is stated, treat it as a heavy nut.

p-cap-nut.sum: A hex nut closed with a round dome on one side, covering and protecting the thread end and tidying the appearance. Specified by metric DIN 1587 (tall type) and DIN 917 (low type), KS B 1026, and inch SAE J483.
facts: The tall type DIN 1587 is the basic one, and the low type DIN 917 has a shallow internal thread depth.
The length by which the bolt protrudes beyond the nut bearing face must be shorter than the internal thread depth in the cap (t min) for it to tighten fully.
The inch cap nut (acorn nut) is SAE J483 (High and Low Crown Hex Nuts).
watch: Choose the bolt length as clamped thickness + protrusion inside the nut (less than t min). If it is longer, it touches the cap and cannot be tightened.
"Acorn nut", "hat nut" (mojaneoteu) and "bag nut" (bongjineoteu) are the same item.
Width across flats is distributed in two series, so write the width across flats if the tool size is fixed.

p-wing-nut.sum: A nut or bolt tightened by hand by turning the wings. Specified by metric wing nut DIN 315 and KS B 1014, wing bolt DIN 316, and for inch ASME B18.6.9 (nut) and B18.6.8 (bolt, thumb screw).
facts: Used for covers, access doors and jigs that are opened and closed often without tools.
DIN 315 is the wing nut with round wings, and DIN 316 is the wing bolt with the same round wings (both M4–M24).
Knurled thumb screws (DIN 653, etc.) are a different item from wing bolts.
Inch wing nuts are specified by ASME B18.6.9 (Wing Nuts), and the wing type is also checked.
Wing nuts are specified by writing the material (steel, A2, A4, etc.) and surface treatment together.
watch: It is a hand-tightened fastener. Do not use it where tightening to a specified torque is required.
Write "wing bolt" and knurled-head "thumb screw" distinctly.
For inch wing nuts, also obtain the type (wing shape).

p-flat-washer.sum: A washer that spreads the pressing force under a bolt head or nut over a wider area. Specified by metric ISO 7089 and 7090 (DIN 125), large washer ISO 7093 (DIN 9021), small washer ISO 7092, KS B 1326, JIS B 1256, and inch ASME B18.21.1 and ASTM F844.
facts: ISO 7089 is the type without chamfer, and ISO 7090 is the chamfered type. DIN 125-1 was replaced by ISO 7089 and 7090 (DIN Media).
Hardness classes are 200 HV and 300 HV. Up to 8.8 bolts and property class 8 nuts, 200 HV is used; for 10.9 bolts (property class 10 nuts), 300 HV is used.
The large washer (ISO 7093-1, formerly DIN 9021) has an outside diameter about 3 times the bolt diameter and is used for slotted holes and soft materials.
In inch, "SAE washer" is the common name for ASME B18.21.1 Type A narrow (N), and "USS washer" for Type A wide (W).
Structural high-strength bolts (F3125) use hardened washers (ASTM F436), not general flat washers (RCSC 2025 2.5).
watch: For lines with only "washer", confirm which of flat, spring or hardened washer it is, and what the mating bolt strength is.
Flat washers of 300 HV or less do not need baking after electroplating per ISO 4042:2022, but for locations where bending is applied, such as slotted or large holes, specify baking in the order.
"M16×50×3" means for M16, outside diameter 50 mm, thickness 3 mm.
Fender washers have various outside diameters for the same inside diameter, so write the outside diameter too (example: 3/8 × 1-1/2).
For lines marked KS B 1326 where the outside diameter matters, also write a dimensional standard such as ISO 7089.

p-spring-washer.sum: A helically split spring ring, used as auxiliary loosening prevention in general fastening with little vibration. Specified by DIN 127 (withdrawn), KS B 1324 and JIS B 1251 for metric, and ASME B18.21.1 for inch.
facts: DIN 127 was withdrawn, and no replacement standard is shown in DIN Media.
There is no corresponding spring washer standard in ISO.
The spring washer series of ASME B18.21.1 are Regular, Heavy, Extra-Duty and High-Collar. For notations not in the current names, such as "Medium", check which series it is.
Inside a socket head cap screw counterbore, use the High Collar type (inch) with a small outside diameter.
Where vibration is large, consider disc spring washers (DIN 6796), wedge-type washers, anti-loosening nuts, and thread lockers.
watch: Electro-galvanizing of spring steel washers has a hydrogen embrittlement risk. For critical fastening, black oxide, mechanical zinc or stainless steel is recommended.
When replacing a line marked KS B 1324 with a DIN 127 product, compare dimensions.
Do not add spring washers to structural high-strength bolt sets. The set washer configuration is fixed.
Stainless steel lock washers have a lower hardness range than carbon steel.

p-hardened-washer.sum: A flat washer hardened by heat treatment, used for high-strength structural bolts, B7 studs and anchor bolts. Specified by ASTM F436/F436M (Type 1 and 3).
facts: Type 1 is carbon steel, and Type 3 is weathering steel (mated with Type 3 structural bolts).
The current standard combines inch and metric into F436/F436M.
When tightening a high-strength bolt, it is placed on the side that rotates (usually the nut side) so that the bearing face is not dented.
Besides round, F436 also includes the clip type (one side cut off) and 1:6 square beveled washers for beams and channels.
watch: "1 1/2" is 1-1/2 inches. Do not read it as 1/2 inch.
For galvanized structural sets, the bolt, nut and washer are plated by the same method and grouped in one lot.
Do not substitute a general flat washer (ASTM F844, SAE, USS) for F436.
Metric structural sets (KS B 1010) use the set washer and are not mixed with F436.

p-anchor-bolt.sum: A bolt embedded before concrete is poured, used to fix pumps, motors and columns. Metric is specified by KS B 1016 and JIS B 1178, inch by ASTM F1554 (Grade 36, 55, 105) material and ASME B18.31.5 (bent bolt) form.
facts: The forms are L and J types with a bent end, LA and JA types with an anchor plate, headed types, and straight rod + nut types.
ASTM F1554 has Grade 36, 55 and 105 with minimum yield strengths of 36, 55 and 105 ksi, and Grade 105 is up to 3".
F1554 specifies the mating nut (6.7) and washer (6.8) separately, so select them to match grade, diameter and plating conditions.
The old A307 Grade C anchor bolt designation was changed to F1554 Grade 36.
DIN 529 is the German standard for embedded anchor bolts (Steinschrauben).
Domestic concrete anchor design (cast-in and post-installed) follows KDS 14 20 54.
watch: For lines with only "anchor bolt", first confirm whether it is a cast-in foundation bolt or a post-installed anchor.
Obtain overall length, thread length, bend (hook) length, projection length, and the number of nuts and washers from the foundation drawing.
Use overtapped nuts as the mate of hot-dip galvanized anchor bolts, and have the bolt and nut done in the same galvanizing process.
Pump foundation anchor bolts are often not in the equipment supply scope, so separate purchase is needed.

table.note: ksi values are from ASTM F1554 (cited from WSDOT Bridge Design Manual M 23-50). MPa values are converted from ksi (1 ksi = 6.895 MPa). Confirm the diameter range, end color marking and mating nut against the current F1554.

p-eye-bolt.sum: Ring-shaped bolts and nuts for lifting equipment. Specified by metric DIN 580 (bolt), DIN 582 (nut) and ISO 3266, KS B 1033 and 1034, JIS B 1168 and 1169, and inch ASME B18.15 + ASTM A489; the allowable load differs by standard and lifting direction.
facts: The allowable load differs by standard and cannot be interchanged. Do not apply DIN 580 loads to KS or JIS products.

Eye bolt load tables are usually values for lifting 1 bolt in the axial direction. ISO 3266 also treats axial and angled loads separately, so for angled lifting check the reduced load in the standard.
Turn it in fully so that the underside of the collar fully contacts the mating surface. The engagement length and strength of the mating thread must be sufficient.
DIN 444 (Fasteners – Eye bolts) is a fastening eye bolt different from DIN 580 (Lifting eye bolts) for lifting, and is not used for lifting.
Inch ASTM A489 is the standard for carbon steel eye bolts for lifting, and ASTM F541 is for alloy steel eye bolts with increased toughness for low-temperature use.
Inch forged eye bolts (ASME B18.15, ASTM A489) come in Type 1 plain and Type 2 shoulder.
If tilted lifting is frequent, consider a swivel lifting ring (hoist ring).
watch: Do not lift with the collar raised off the mating surface. Do not leave it under-tightened to align the ring direction.
If "DIN 444", "GLAND", "SWING" or "HINGE" is attached to English "EYE BOLT", it is a swing bolt, not for lifting.
An eye bolt made by bending a rod (ASME B18.31.5 bent bolt) is a different product from a forged lifting eye bolt (ASME B18.15), so check the lifting rating separately.
For stainless steel eye bolts and eye nuts, check the load table separately.
When lifting with 2 or more, check the reduced load by angle in the table of the applicable standard.
eq_notes: Eye bolt · eye nut (load table separate)
アイボルト · アイナット
Inch forged eye bolt (material ASTM A489 · F541)

p-u-bolt.sum: A bolt made by bending a rod into a U shape with threads at both ends, used to fix a pipe to a support. Metric is specified by DIN 3570 (dimensions by pipe size), inch by ASME B18.31.5 (bent bolt) or the pipe support drawing.
facts: A U-bolt is called by pipe size (25A, 50A, DN50, 2") rather than thread diameter. Write the pipe size and thread together.
DIN 3570 sets the thread, inside width and leg spacing for each pipe size, so it is easy to match the hole spacing of the support.
ASME B18.31.5 covers the dimensions and ordering notation of bent bolts such as U-bolts, J-bolts, hook bolts and bent eye bolts.
KS and JIS steel pipes (A designation) and ISO steel pipes differ slightly in outside diameter, and coated or insulated pipes have a larger outside diameter.
Decide together whether 2 nuts are included and whether washers are needed.
watch: If the pipe outside diameter (including insulation and coating) is not written, the inside width may not fit.
Check from the support drawing whether it is for fixing or for guiding where the pipe can move. The tightening degree differs.
Use overtapped nuts for hot-dip galvanized U-bolts.
It is a different item from "bando" (band-type pipe clamp).

p-structural-set.sum: A bolt, nut and washer set used for steel frame connections. Domestically specified by KS B 1010 (friction grip) and KS B 2819 (torque-shear type), in Europe by EN 14399, and in the US by ASTM F3125 (A325 and A490) + A563 DH + F436.
facts: A structural set is a product that guarantees torque coefficient or rotation capacity with the bolt, nut and washer grouped in one lot, so do not mix parts from other lots or other standards.
The width across flats is larger and the threaded portion is shorter than a general hex bolt (example: EN 14399-4 M20 width across flats 32 mm).
EN 14399 is divided into parts by system: HR -3, HV -4, preload-adjusted HRC -10, washers -5 and -6.
Since 2015, ASTM F3125 has grouped A325, A490, F1852 and F2280 as grades. F1852 and F2280 are TC types.
Hot-dip and mechanical galvanizing (including metal spraying) cannot be used on A490, while zinc flake coating (ASTM F3393) is allowed (RCSC 2025).
watch: "High-strength bolt" in a BOM often means 8.8 or 10.9 hex bolts, not a structural set. Check the set standard and grade notation.
Do not substitute SAE Grade 5 and 8 bolts for A325 and A490.
Do not reuse a set that has spun idle after tightening (bolt and nut turning together) or a set that has been used once.
For galvanized inch sets, also obtain the rotation capacity test record.

p-dowel-pin.sum: A cylindrical pin pressed into holes to position two parts accurately. Specified by hardened ISO 8734 (DIN 6325), unhardened ISO 2338 (DIN 7), internally threaded ISO 8735 and 8733, and inch ASME B18.8.2.
facts: A dowel pin only positions; the clamping force is carried by bolts.
Hardened ISO 8734 has diameter tolerance m6, with type A through-hardened and type B case-hardened.
Unhardened ISO 2338 is chosen from diameter tolerance m6 and h8. The standard stainless steel material is A1 (303 series).
For blind holes, use parallel pins with an internal thread for extraction (hardened ISO 8735, unhardened ISO 8733).
National standards are KS B ISO 8734 (fitting pin), KS B ISO 2338 (parallel pin) and JIS B 1354 (平行ピン).
watch: "Knock pin" is a field term for dowel pin. Confirm whether it is hardened and the tolerance (m6, h8).
Electroplating a hardened pin has a hydrogen embrittlement risk, so the default is untreated (rust preventive oil).
304 and 316 parallel pins are unhardened pins and do not substitute for hardened dowel pins. If hardened stainless steel is needed, it is martensitic (C1).
Hole tolerance follows the design drawing.

p-spring-pin.sum: A tubular pin slightly larger than the hole, which clamps itself when driven in so that it does not come out. Specified by slotted ISO 8752 (heavy duty) and ISO 13337 (light duty), coiled ISO 8750, 8748 and 8751, and inch ASME B18.8.2.
facts: The nominal size is the diameter of the hole to be fitted, and the hole is drilled to the nominal diameter with H12 tolerance.
Heavy-duty ISO 8752 (formerly DIN 1481) is thick and has a large shear load, and light-duty ISO 13337 (formerly DIN 7346) is thin and easy to drive.
The coiled type is a pin made by winding a sheet in a spiral: standard duty ISO 8750, heavy duty ISO 8748, light duty ISO 8751.
Because of hydrogen embrittlement risk, spring pins are by default not plated. If corrosion is a concern, choose stainless steel.
The standard has no shear load values for austenitic stainless steel pins.
watch: The nominal size is the hole diameter, not the shaft diameter.
For lines with only "spring pin", the distribution practice is to treat it as a heavy-duty slotted type, so write separately if light-duty or coiled is needed.
"Roll pin" and "tension pin" are other names for the slotted spring pin.
To use an austenitic stainless steel pin where load matters, check the strength separately.

table.note: ISO 8752:2009 Table 1 (steel and martensitic stainless steel pins). Austenitic stainless steel pins have no shear load values.

p-split-pin.sum: A pin inserted in the hole of a castle nut or clevis pin and spread at the legs to prevent coming off. Metric is specified by ISO 1234 (formerly DIN 94), KS B ISO 1234 and JIS B 1351, inch by ASME B18.8.1.
facts: The nominal size is the diameter of the hole to be fitted, not the pin diameter. The actual pin diameter is slightly smaller than the nominal size.
Length l is measured from under the eye to the end of the shorter leg.
The ISO 1234 table has the range of bolt and clevis pin diameters that fit each nominal size, and the nominal size is chosen from it.
For railway use, or when alternating transverse load acts on the clevis pin, one size larger than the table is recommended (ISO 1234 Table 1 note).
Do not reuse a split pin that has been spread and straightened once.
Materials are steel (St), stainless steel (A), brass (CuZn), etc.
watch: If ordered by pin diameter, one size smaller nominal size arrives. Write it by hole diameter.
Inch split pins (ASME B18.8.1) have a different nominal size system, so do not read them by converting to metric nominal sizes.
"Wari-pin", "hal-pin" and "cotter pin" are split pins. The R-pin (spring cotter), which is inserted without tools, is a different item.

p-retaining-ring.sum: A spring ring fitted in a groove on a shaft or in a hole to keep bearings and gears from slipping out axially. Specified by DIN 471 for shafts, DIN 472 for holes, E-ring DIN 6799, KS B 1336 and 1337, JIS B 2804, and inch ASME B18.27.
facts: The nominal size of a retaining ring for shafts is the shaft diameter, and for holes the hole diameter. It is not the groove diameter.
If the lugs (plier holes) are on the outside it is for shafts, and if on the inside it is for holes.
The rated load is obtained only when the groove diameter, groove width and groove edge margin match the table.
An E-ring cannot take large axial force, so a C-type retaining ring for shafts is used to secure bearings.
KS B 1336 is the C-type and KS B 1337 is the E-type retaining ring.
Inch rings (ASME B18.27) have different groove dimensions from metric rings and are not interchanged.
watch: For lines with only "snap ring", confirm whether it is for shafts (external) or for holes (internal).
A ring that has been spread and removed may change shape, so replacing it with a new one at maintenance is the general practice.
Zinc electroplating is discussed separately because of hydrogen embrittlement.
Wire snap rings (DIN 7993) and rings with lugs (DIN 983 and 984) are different items.
Before interchanging a ring marked KS B 1336 with a DIN 471 or 472 ring, compare the groove dimensions.

p-key.sum: A part that transmits torque by fitting in the keyways of a shaft and a hub (impeller, coupling, pulley). Specified by parallel key DIN 6885-1, KS B 1311 and JIS B 1301, woodruff key DIN 6888, and inch ASME B17.1 and B17.2.
facts: The parallel key cross-section b×h is set for each shaft diameter range (example: shaft over 22 up to 30 → 8×7, ISO/R 773).
Type A has rounded ends (end mill keyway) and type B has square ends (side cutter keyway).
The fit (tight, normal, sliding) is set not by the key but by the shaft and hub keyway tolerances (P9, N9, JS9, H9, D10).
The ISO parallel key standard (ISO/R 773) and woodruff key standard (ISO 3912) have been withdrawn.
A 1/4" key (6.35 mm) does not fit a metric 6 mm keyway.
Key stock (DIN 6880) is bar material drawn to the key cross-section and cut in the field for use.
watch: The single word "key" is not enough. Obtain b×h×length, end shape (A, B) and material together.
First check whether the shaft is inch or metric.
If the equipment drawing has separate height and length tolerances, as for a pump impeller key, treat it as a drawing item.
Before interchanging a key marked KS B 1311 (sunk key and keyway) with a DIN 6885-1 key, compare the keyway dimensions.

p-blind-rivet.sum: A rivet for fixing sheet materials that can be worked from one side only. When the mandrel is pulled and broken off, the rear body swells and locks; metric is specified by the ISO 15973 to 15983 series, inch by IFI 114.
facts: The standard differs by material combination: aluminum body with steel mandrel ISO 15977, steel/steel ISO 15979, stainless steel A2/A2 ISO 15983 (all open-type dome head).
Countersunk head is ISO 15978, and the sealed type with a closed end is ISO 15973.
Terminology is in ISO 14588, and mechanical tests (shear, tensile, mandrel tests) are in ISO 14589.
Length is chosen by the sum of the plate thicknesses (grip). Even at the same length, a thicker diameter accepts a thinner grip.
"Pop rivet" comes from POP (a trademark) and is used generally for blind rivets.
Solid rivets (KS B 1101 and 1102, ASME B18.1.1), whose head is formed from both sides, are a different item.
watch: Obtain the grip (sum of plate thicknesses) together with the diameter. For lines with only the length, confirm the plate thickness.
Using an aluminum rivet on a stainless steel plate easily causes dissimilar metal corrosion. Choose a material of the same family as the plate.
Specify the sealed type where water or gas must not leak.

p-rivet-nut.sum: A part that is crimped from one side to form an internal thread in places where tapping is not possible, such as thin plates and square tubes. There is no common ISO or ASME product standard, so it is specified by thread designation, grip (plate thickness), head and body type, and material.
facts: The thread follows ISO 261 and 965 for metric and ASME B1.1 for inch, but product dimensions are the manufacturer's standard.
Even with the same nominal size there are several products with different grips (plate thickness ranges), so always write the plate thickness.

Heads are flat head, countersunk head and small head, and bodies are round, knurled and hex. For locations where rotation is not allowed, choose a hex or knurled body, and a hex body needs a hex hole.
Hole diameter follows the manufacturer's table.
A rivet bolt with an external thread (blind rivet stud) is a different item.
"Rivnut" (a trademark) is also used as a name for rivet nuts.
watch: Ask back for lines without the plate thickness (grip).
It is a different item from clinch nuts that are pressed into the plate and insert nuts for wood (spiked T-nuts).
Choose from steel, aluminum and stainless steel the material that matches the plate to avoid dissimilar metal corrosion.
Crimping needs a dedicated tool.

p-thread-insert.sum: An insert made by coiling diamond-section wire, which reinforces internal threads in weak base material or restores damaged threads to the same nominal size. Metric is specified by DIN 8140 and ASME B18.29.2M, inch by ASME B18.29.1.
facts: It is commonly called "Helicoil" (a trademark), but the generic name is wire thread insert (coil insert).
There are free-running types and screw-locking (anti-loosening) types (ASME B18.29.1 and B18.29.2M).
The insert hole is machined with a dedicated STI tap (screw thread insert tap), whose dimensions differ from a general tap of the same nominal size.
There are types where the tang at the end is bent off and removed after insertion, and types without a tang.
Widely used to repair damaged threads in aluminum and cast iron parts (pump casings, etc.).
watch: The insert nominal size is the nominal size of the bolt to be fitted. Drill the hole larger and tap it with the dedicated tap.
Specify the screw-locking type where a bolt loosens from vibration.
Write the nominal thread, length, type (free-running, locking) and presence of a tang together.
Thick key-locking inserts, which are fixed against rotation by driving keys, are a different series.

p-key-locking-insert.sum: A cylindrical threaded insert that is fitted into a hole with its external thread and has keys driven into the base material to prevent rotation. Used to repair damaged internal threads or to reinforce threads in soft metals.
facts: It is commonly called "key insert", and also "Keensert" or "Keysert" (trademarks). The generic name is key-locking insert.
It is a cylindrical body with an internal thread into which the bolt goes and an external thread on the outside that fits into the hole.
The hole is machined with a general drill and tap. Drill diameter, tap and installation tools follow the manufacturer's table and are set for each size.
After fitting, the keys on the insert are driven toward the base material to prevent rotation.
Used to repair damaged or worn internal threads, and also to reinforce threads from the start in parts of soft metals such as aluminum and magnesium.
There are wall thickness series (thin wall, solid, heavy duty, etc.; names differ by manufacturer) and carbon steel and stainless steel bodies.
watch: For lines with only "key insert" in the BOM, ask back for the internal thread nominal size, length, wall thickness series, material, and metric or inch.
The nominal size is the thread nominal size of the bolt to be fitted. The external thread and hole diameter differ by product, so check against the manufacturer's table.
For brittle base materials such as cast iron and plastic, sources split between "not recommended" and "can be used". For such base materials, check the manufacturer's guidance.
Wire coil inserts (Helicoil family) are a different series, and there are also self-tapping inserts used without keys, so write the type distinctly.

p-jack-bolt.sum: A bolt that pushes a casing or cover apart, or adjusts the height and alignment of equipment or a base plate. Rather than a dedicated product standard, it is made by machining the end of a hex bolt (ISO 4017) or socket head cap screw (ISO 4762) as the body.
facts: A pushing jack bolt is screwed into a threaded hole in a flange or cover and pushes apart the mating surfaces. The end is machined flat or rounded so that the mating surface is not damaged.
A leveling screw sets the height before base plate grouting, and is often removed after the grout has hardened.
The position is fixed with a jam nut.
Body strength is 8.8 or 10.9, and for corrosive environments stainless steel (A2, A4) is used.
watch: Write the end shape (flat, round, dog point, hardened pad) and whether a jam nut is included.
When a leveling screw is removed after grouting, also consider a short bolt to plug the remaining hole.

p-flange-bolt-set.sum: A bolting bundle that tightens one pipe flange location. Usually 1 stud and 2 heavy hex nuts are bought as 1 set, and the bolt count and nominal size are set by the table of the flange standard (ASME B16.5 and B16.47, JIS B 2220, etc.).
facts: The purchase unit is usually a "set", and 1 set = 1 stud + 2 heavy hex nuts. Washers are specified separately.
Bolt count and diameter are set by the flange standard table: ASME B16.5 (up to NPS 24), B16.47 (NPS 26 and above), JIS B 2220, EN 1092-1.
Domestic buyers order by flange designation, such as "JIS 10K 50A × n sets".
watch: English "FLANGE BOLT" is usually a stud set for pipe flanges. Distinguish it from the hex flange bolt (ISO 4162) with a disc on the head.
Confirm whether the quantity is in "sets" or "pieces" (number of studs, or including nuts).
If Class, NPS, face type (RF, RTJ) and gasket thickness are given together, the stud length can be calculated.
Flanges tightened with hydraulic tensioners need a longer extra thread length.
For B16.47 large diameters, dimensions differ between Series A and B, so check up to the flange standard.

p-machine-screw.sum: Small-diameter screws with a Phillips or slotted head. They divide into machine screws with metric threads (ISO 7045 and 7046, KS B 1023, inch ASME B18.6.3) and self-tapping screws that cut their own threads (ISO 7049 to 7051, self-drilling screws ISO 15480, etc.).
facts: "Piseu" in the field is a general term for machine screws, tapping screws and self-drilling screws, so first confirm the screw type.

Machine screws are fastened with metric threads into nuts or tapped holes: Phillips pan head ISO 7045 (DIN 7985), Phillips countersunk head ISO 7046 (DIN 965), Phillips raised countersunk head ISO 7047 (DIN 966), slotted ISO 1207, 1580, 2009 and 2010.
Tapping screws are ST screws (ISO 1478, e.g., ST4.2) that cut their own threads in thin plate and resin: Phillips pan ISO 7049, countersunk ISO 7050, raised countersunk ISO 7051, hex ISO 1479.
Self-drilling screws have a drill at the tip and are driven into steel plate without a pilot hole (ISO 15480, etc., formerly DIN 7504).
For pan and truss heads, length is measured from under the head, and for countersunk heads from the top of the head (overall length).
Phillips recesses come in H type and Z type, and the matching driver differs (ISO 4757).
Inch machine screws are specified by ASME B18.6.3 (Machine Screws and Machine Screw Nuts), and even for the same #10 the UNC and UNF thread counts differ, so write the thread count together.
Machine screws often have no grade marking on the head, so write the material (steel, 18-8, 316) and surface treatment on the line.
watch: "Piseu M4×10" may be a machine screw and "piseu 4×16" a tapping screw (ST4.2), so confirm the thread type.
A self-drilling screw cannot be used if the sum of plate thicknesses is thicker than the drill point length.
Truss and binding heads are heads not in the ISO machine screw standards, so confirm against the form in the standard the drawing follows (KS, JIS or ASME B18.6.3).
A 100° countersunk screw (common in aerospace standards, etc.) does not fit 90° (metric) and 82° (inch) countersink seats.

p-screw-plug.sum: A male-threaded stopper that closes a hole. First decide the thread type (R taper "PT", G parallel "PF", NPT, metric fine thread), then specify hex head DIN 910 and 909, hex socket DIN 906 and 908, and inch NPT plugs.
facts: In domestic notation, PT is the KS B 0222 pipe taper thread (partial match with ISO 7-1), and PF is the KS B 0221 pipe parallel thread.
Taper threads (R, NPT) seal at the thread (usually with a sealant), and parallel threads (G, metric) seal with a sealing ring under the collar (DIN 7603, etc.) or an O-ring.
The hex head collar plug is DIN 910 (parallel), the hex head taper plug is DIN 909, the hex socket taper plug is DIN 906, and the hex socket plug with collar is DIN 908.
NPT (60°) and R·PT (55°) are both tapered, but their thread angles differ and they are not mixed. Inch NPT is ASME B1.20.1.
O-ring boss hydraulic ports (SAE J1926, ISO 11926, ISO 6149) use dedicated O-ring plugs.
watch: Do not put a parallel thread plug into a taper hole or the reverse.
Even at the same diameter, metric fine thread (M16×1.5) and G have different threads and do not mate.
The sealing ring of a collar plug is a separate item, so order it together.
